title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
試左布政使王遵右布政使
陳大賓司提調按察使張子
弘僉事何全司監試及諸執
事皆就列御史申
詔令誓衆曰以人事君人臣之上
務今玆之役所不如
明詔者謂人臣何乃合提學副使
===
姜寶所簡士二千二百有奇
進之三試得雋者九十籍
奏之州不佞宜宣言於首簡惟
閩僻在南海至漢始與中國
通當古昔盛時不遑疆理徒
以聲敎所曁喁喁嚮風海隅
蒼生罔不率俾此非文明之
punctuated: 試，左布政使王遵、右布政使陳大賓司提調，按察使張子弘、僉事何全司監試，及諸執事皆就列。御史申詔令，誓衆曰：「以人事君，人臣之上務。今玆之役，所不如明詔者，謂人臣何？」乃合提學副使姜寶所簡士二千二百有奇，進之三試，得雋者九十，籍奏之。州不佞宜宣言於首簡：惟閩僻在南海，至漢始與中國通。當古昔盛時，不遑疆理，徒以聲敎所曁，喁喁嚮風，海隅蒼生罔不率俾。此非文明之
translation_en:
…examination. Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Wang Zun and Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Chen Dabin served as Proctors; Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Zihong and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner He Quan supervised the examination. They and all the other functionaries took their assigned places. The censor reiterated the imperial commands and solemnly admonished the assembled officials: “To serve the ruler by providing worthy men is a minister’s foremost duty. In this undertaking, if we fail to comply with the illustrious edict, what claim have we to be ministers?” They then assembled the more than 2,200 candidates selected by Jiang Bao, the Surveillance Vice Commissioner in charge of education, and admitted them to the three examination sessions. Ninety distinguished themselves; their names were entered on a register and reported to the throne. I, unworthy as I am [?], ought to set forth these words on the opening pages.

Min lay remote by the southern sea and only began to communicate with the Central Lands during the Han. In the flourishing ages of antiquity, there had been no opportunity to delimit and administer its territory. Yet wherever the influence of moral instruction reached, the people eagerly turned toward it; among the common people in those coastal reaches, none failed to obey. This was not a land of cultivated refinement …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
域其應感殊哉
明興以來閩得人為盛蓋天將開
我
國家文明之治則宋儒為之先
鳴歷數百年臚傳響應
今天子南面而治久道成化愈益
斌斌比年日本苦閩士未知
===
所息踵賴
天子神武
詔司馬徵師司徒轉餉一舉殲焉
由是文學諸生始得脩其故
業卽
文德四洽萬國攸同要以
武功耆定戢干戈而俎豆之則
punctuated:
域，其應感殊哉！
明興以來，閩得人為盛。蓋天將開我國家文明之治，則宋儒為之先鳴，歷數百年，臚傳響應。今天子南面而治，久道成化，愈益斌斌。比年日本苦閩，士未知所息踵，賴天子神武，詔司馬徵師、司徒轉餉，一舉殲焉。由是文學諸生始得脩其故業。卽文德四洽，萬國攸同，要以武功耆定，戢干戈而俎豆之，則
translation_en:
…realm, how extraordinary its response to transforming influence!
Since the rise of the Ming, Fujian has been particularly abundant in men of talent. When Heaven was about to inaugurate civilized government for our dynasty, the Confucian scholars of the Song sounded its first notes; over several centuries, their teachings were transmitted in succession and met with answering echoes. The present Son of Heaven faces south to govern; through long adherence to the Way, his transforming influence has taken effect, and cultural refinement has flourished ever more richly. In recent years, the Japanese afflicted Fujian, and its scholars knew nowhere to rest their feet. They relied upon the Son of Heaven’s divine martial prowess: he commanded the Minister of War to levy troops and the Minister of Revenue to transport provisions, and annihilated the enemy in a single campaign. Only then could the students devoted to literary learning resume their former studies. Even though his civil virtue extends everywhere and all the myriad states share in it, what is essential is that military achievement establish peace, that shields and spears be put away, and that sacrificial vessels take their place; then …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
閩士獨也士旣錄行且偕計
吏上公車駸駸乎嚮用如將
圖報於萬分之一則何以哉
當
今之時
至治之澤
廣運無疆
===
===
壽考作人濟濟在列第令多士旅
進其何以佐百姓而利
國家於報何有今夫天生而不
有長而不宰天固未嘗責報
於人今夫父敎之義方弗納
于邪父固未嘗責報於子仁
人不以天之高明而忘有相
punctuated: 閩士獨也。士旣錄，行且偕計吏上公車，駸駸乎嚮用。如將圖報於萬分之一，則何以哉？當今之時，至治之澤，廣運無疆，壽考作人，濟濟在列。第令多士旅進，其何以佐百姓而利國家？於報何有？今夫天生而不有，長而不宰，天固未嘗責報於人。今夫父敎之義方，弗納于邪，父固未嘗責報於子。仁人不以天之高明而忘有相
translation_en:
…the scholars of Fujian alone [?]. Now that the scholars have been selected, they will soon accompany the officials bearing provincial accounts to the capital to present themselves for examination, advancing swiftly toward appointment. If they intend to repay even one ten-thousandth of this favor, how shall they do so? In this age, the blessings of perfect government extend everywhere without limit; the sovereign enjoys longevity and nurtures men of talent, and worthy men throng the ranks. Yet if all these scholars merely advance together into office, how will they aid the common people and benefit the state? What repayment would there be in that?

Heaven gives life without claiming possession and nurtures without exercising mastery; Heaven has never demanded repayment from humankind. A father teaches his son the ways of righteousness and does not allow him to stray into wickedness; a father has never demanded repayment from his son. A benevolent person does not, because Heaven is lofty and luminous, forget to assist it…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
孝子不以父之燕翼而忘克
家此惟自盡爲兢兢要亦以
不報報之耳人臣事君如事
天天工人其代之敢不自盡
事君如事父夙夜匪懈以事
一人敢不自盡幸而在事無
寧後其身而讓能故枹鼓不
===
聞兵革不試臣不言安四方
露積民無赭衣臣不言佚國
事脩明吏治罔缺臣不言私
精白一心兢兢然務得其職
凡以自盡而已此之爲報於
仁人孝子何讓焉
聖天子德象
punctuated:
孝子不以父之燕翼而忘克家。此惟自盡爲兢兢，要亦以不報報之耳。人臣事君如事天，天工人其代之，敢不自盡？事君如事父，夙夜匪懈，以事一人，敢不自盡？幸而在事，無寧後其身而讓能。故枹鼓不聞，兵革不試，臣不言安；四方露積，民無赭衣，臣不言佚；國事脩明，吏治罔缺，臣不言私。精白一心，兢兢然務得其職，凡以自盡而已。此之爲報，於仁人孝子何讓焉？
聖天子德象
translation_en:
… A filial son does not, because his father has provided for his descendants’ peace, forget to uphold the family. In this, he strives conscientiously only to give his utmost; ultimately, he repays by offering no repayment as such. A minister serves his ruler as he serves Heaven: human beings must perform Heaven’s work on its behalf—how could he dare not give his utmost? He serves his ruler as he serves his father, untiring morning and night in service to the One Man—how could he dare not give his utmost? Fortunate enough to hold office, he should rather put himself last and yield to the capable. Thus, though no war drums are heard and arms are not put to use, your servant does not speak of taking his ease; though grain lies heaped in the open throughout the realm and the people wear no convict’s ochre robes, your servant does not speak of leisure; though affairs of state are well ordered and the administration of officials has no deficiencies, your servant does not speak of private interests. With a single, pure heart, he conscientiously strives to fulfill his office, seeking only to give his utmost. In repaying thus, how does he fall short of the benevolent man or the filial son?
The sagely Son of Heaven’s virtue takes as its model …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
重玄道彌六合嘉生溢於
帝藉上瑞集於
宸居其在草木昆蟲猶然效神奇
而應
明德何論多士頃者吏習於恬嬉
俗流於茅靡
天子計羣吏之治埽而更之乃今
===
茂對
昌期
作新髦士將以潤色
鴻業衍億萬年有道之長
申令敕法程督有司慎始進也御
史曁諸執事對揚
顯命罔或不虔禁機利儆干掫斥
punctuated: 重玄，道彌六合，嘉生溢於帝藉，上瑞集於宸居。其在草木昆蟲，猶然效神奇而應明德，何論多士？頃者，吏習於恬嬉，俗流於茅靡。天子計羣吏之治，埽而更之。乃今茂對昌期，作新髦士，將以潤色鴻業，衍億萬年有道之長。申令敕法，程督有司，慎始進也。御史曁諸執事對揚顯命，罔或不虔，禁機利，儆干掫，斥
translation_en: …the highest heavens, and his Way pervades the six directions. Auspicious growth abounds in the imperial ploughing field, and supreme portents gather at the imperial residence. Even plants and insects display wondrous powers in response to his luminous virtue; how much more should the many scholars! Recently, officials had grown accustomed to complacency and idleness, while common customs had fallen into laxity [?]. The Son of Heaven assessed the administration of the officials and swept away its failings to reform it. Now, fittingly meeting this flourishing age, he renews outstanding scholars, intending thereby to embellish the grand imperial enterprise and extend enlightened rule for countless millions of years. He reiterates commands, enforces regulations, and sets standards for and supervises the responsible officials, taking care over men’s initial entry into service. The investigating censors and all those charged with duties reverently carry out his illustrious command, none failing in devotion: they prohibit opportunistic pursuit of advantage, admonish the watchmen to vigilance, and exclude…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
雷同擯勦說業已不遺餘力
州等屈首受筴退然如將不
勝目之所擊口之所誦手之
所披於吾心惴惴然懼無當
於軌物蓋不敢不虔其始庶
幾乎以人事
君之心有司之技單於此矣由此
===
而圖厥終則多士事也非有
司能也州始畢事覆讀多士
所爲文其指遠其義章其言
必稱先王其持論中當否其
出謀發慮達
國體之宜此非儲精應會儼然
以
punctuated:
雷同，擯勦說，業已不遺餘力。州等屈首受筴，退然如將不勝。目之所擊，口之所誦，手之所披，於吾心惴惴然懼無當於軌物。蓋不敢不虔其始，庶幾乎以人事君之心，有司之技單於此矣。由此而圖厥終，則多士事也，非有司能也。
州始畢事，覆讀多士所爲文，其指遠，其義章，其言必稱先王，其持論中當否，其出謀發慮達國體之宜。此非儲精應會，儼然以
translation_en:
…conformity, and rejected plagiarized arguments, already sparing no effort. We, Zhou and the others, bowed our heads to receive our instructions, humbly withdrawing as though unequal to the task. What met our eyes, what we recited, and what we opened and read—all filled our hearts with apprehension lest we fail to conform to the proper standards. We dared not be remiss at the outset, hoping thereby to fulfill our intention of serving the ruler through the selection of men. Here the capacities of the responsible officials were exhausted. To proceed from this beginning and bring it to fulfillment is the responsibility of the many scholars; it lies beyond what the officials can accomplish.
When I, Zhou, had just completed my duties, I reread the compositions of the many scholars. Their purport was far-reaching, their meaning clear. Their words invariably invoked the former kings; their arguments accurately distinguished what was fitting from what was not; their proposals and deliberations grasped what was appropriate to the institutions of the state. Had they not stored up their intellectual energies to meet this occasion, and solemnly …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
帝德照臨之宜不及此有司得此
以進其愉快可知雖然懼未
釋也士不聞古人之善相馬
者乎直中繩曲中鉤方圓中
規矩國馬也此可以形容筋
骨相也乃若天下之馬必自
牝牡驪黃之外求之此唯九
===
方皐能耳卅下才也索爾多
士於方圓曲直之間則既當
於吾心吾且知爲良馬矣異
日躡嶠而入
天子之庭其爲九方皐者何限假
令執策當道超軼絶塵則天
下馬也上也次之則範我馳
punctuated: 帝德照臨之宜，不及此。有司得此以進，其愉快可知。雖然，懼未釋也。士不聞古人之善相馬者乎？直中繩，曲中鉤，方圓中規矩，國馬也。此可以形容筋骨相也。乃若天下之馬，必自牝牡驪黃之外求之，此唯九方皐能耳。卅下才也，索爾多士於方圓曲直之間，則既當於吾心，吾且知爲良馬矣。異日躡嶠而入天子之庭，其爲九方皐者何限！假令執策當道，超軼絶塵，則天下馬也，上也。次之，則範我馳
translation_en:
…the fitting reach of imperial virtue’s illumination; otherwise, this could not have been attained [?]. That the officials have obtained such men to recommend must, as one can imagine, give them great pleasure. Nevertheless, their apprehension has not yet been dispelled.

Have you scholars not heard of those in antiquity who excelled at judging horses? A horse whose straight parts accord with the measuring line, whose curved parts accord with the hook, and whose square and round parts accord with the carpenter’s square and compass is a fine horse of the realm. Such a horse can be judged by its outward form, sinews, and bones. But a horse unsurpassed under Heaven must be sought beyond distinctions of female and male, black and yellow. Only Jiufang Gao could do this.

I [the transcription here reads 卅, possibly Zhou 州], being of inferior talent, have examined you scholars by these standards of squareness, roundness, curvature, and straightness. You have satisfied my judgment, and I regard you as fine horses. On some future day, when you scale the heights and enter the Son of Heaven’s court, how many men like Jiufang Gao there will be! Suppose that, when someone takes up the whip and stands upon the road, you surge ahead and leave the dust behind: then you will be horses unsurpassed under Heaven—the highest class. Next come those who conform to the prescribed manner of galloping …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
驅猶不失爲良馬脫或詭銜
竊轡失故步而倍周行將焉
用彼相者終之不令慎始何
爲有司安所傅其罪也州以
一日長乎多士不敢廢久要
之言爾多士務自盡而慎有
終無違爾共惟
===
帝臣之始願於有司得矣有司亦
將持此以報
天子况多士乎是役也提督巡撫
前右副都御史譚綸今右僉
都御史汪道昆保釐疆埸振
厲章縫提督南贛右僉都御
史吳百朋憲令來宣風教孔
punctuated:
驅，猶不失爲良馬。脫或詭銜竊轡，失故步而倍周行，將焉用彼相者？終之不令，慎始何爲？有司安所傅其罪也？州以一日長乎多士，不敢廢久要之言。爾多士務自盡，而慎有終，無違爾共。惟帝臣之始願，於有司得矣。有司亦將持此以報天子，况多士乎？
是役也，提督巡撫前右副都御史譚綸、今右僉都御史汪道昆，保釐疆埸，振厲章縫；提督南贛右僉都御史吳百朋，憲令來宣，風教孔
translation_en:
…when driven, they would still qualify as good horses. But if they should evade the bit and steal control of the reins, lose their accustomed gait, and turn away from the proper road, what use would there be for the man who judged them? If the outcome is bad, what purpose did care at the outset serve? How could the responsible officials escape blame?
I, Zhou [?], being a little older than you scholars, dare not neglect the words of our longstanding pledge. You scholars must exert yourselves fully and take care to finish well, never departing from your reverent duty. Thus the initial aspiration of a servant of the Emperor will have been fulfilled in the responsible officials [?]. The officials, too, will hold to this in repaying the Son of Heaven; how much more should you scholars!
For this examination, the former Superintendent and Grand Coordinator, Tan Lun, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and the present incumbent, Wang Daokun, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, have safeguarded and governed the frontier territory and encouraged the scholars. Wu Baipeng, Superintendent of Nan-Gan and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, has come to promulgate authoritative commands, and his moral instruction has greatly…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
邇鎮守總兵官署都督同知
戚繼光投戈講藝士類歸心
巡按直隸監察御史姜儆奉
使咨諏樂有觀法前左布政使
今陞太僕寺卿曾于拱首事
圖議綜理周詳左參政塗澤
民左參議黃朏右參議金淛
===
副使周賢宣僉事曾一經金
定遊擊將軍李超署都指揮
僉事路良張僑張斌周元燧
戮力效謀贊襄成事右參政
劉佃僉事黃可大署都指揮
同知徐高署都指揮僉事劉
公臣先期入
punctuated: 邇。鎮守總兵官署都督同知戚繼光，投戈講藝，士類歸心。巡按直隸監察御史姜儆，奉使咨諏，樂有觀法。前左布政使、今陞太僕寺卿曾于拱，首事圖議，綜理周詳。左參政塗澤民、左參議黃朏、右參議金淛、副使周賢宣、僉事曾一經、金定、遊擊將軍李超、署都指揮僉事路良、張僑、張斌、周元燧，戮力效謀，贊襄成事。右參政劉佃、僉事黃可大、署都指揮同知徐高、署都指揮僉事劉公臣，先期入
translation_en:
…close at hand. Qi Jiguang, the Regional Commander serving as acting Vice Commissioner-in-Chief, laid aside his spear to discuss the literary arts, winning the allegiance of the scholars. Jiang Jing, Investigating Censor for Zhili serving as Regional Inspector, undertook his commission and sought information and counsel, delighting in having exemplary practices to observe. Zeng Yugong, formerly Left Provincial Administration Commissioner and now promoted to Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, initiated the undertaking and its deliberations, managing all matters thoroughly and carefully.

Tu Zemin, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Huang Fei, Left Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner; Jin Zhe, Right Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner; Zhou Xianxuan, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Zeng Yijing and Jin Ding, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; Li Chao, Mobile Corps Commander; and Lu Liang, Zhang Qiao, Zhang Bin, and Zhou Yuansui, acting Regional Military Assistant Commissioners, pooled their efforts and contributed their counsel, helping bring the undertaking to completion.

Liu Dian, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Huang Keda, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner; Xu Gao, acting Regional Military Vice Commissioner; and Liu Gongchen, acting Regional Military Assistant Commissioner, entered ahead of the appointed date…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
賀皆與有聞者也法得書
湖廣寶慶府儒學教授王州
謹序
punctuated:
賀，皆與有聞者也，法得書。
湖廣寶慶府儒學教授王州謹序。
translation_en:
…to offer congratulations. All had a part in these proceedings and, according to established practice, merit being recorded.
Wang Zhou, Professor of the Confucian School of Baoqing Prefecture, Huguang, respectfully composed this preface.

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試
監臨官
巡按福建監察御史陳萬言〔道襄廣東南海縣人丙辰進士〕
提調官
福建等處承宣布政使司左布政使王遵〔子法四川南充縣人乙未進士〕
福建等處承宣布政使司右布政使陳大賓〔敬夫湖廣江陵縣人甲辰進士〕
監試官
福建等處提刑按察司按察使張子弘〔汝容江西廬陵縣人甲辰進士〕
福建等處提刑按察司僉事何全〔原學四川儀衞司籍溫江縣人癸丑進士〕
===
考試官
湖廣寶慶府儒學教授王州〔惟冀廣西灌陽縣人壬子貢士〕
山東東昌府高唐州恩縣儒學教諭甘宮〔惟中江西餘干縣人己酉貢士〕
同考試官
直隸保定府儒學教授王承志〔子孝山西蒲州人辛卯貢士〕

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
中庸之爲德也其至矣乎
言而民莫不信行而民莫不說
可欲之謂善有諸己之謂信充實之謂美
充實而有光輝之謂大大而化之之謂
聖聖而不可知之之謂神
易
中正以觀天下
===
上九鼎玉鉉大吉无不利
以言乎天地之間則備矣夫乾其靜也專
其動也直是以大生焉夫坤其靜也翕
其動也闢是以廣生焉廣大配天地
齊也者言萬物之潔齊也
書
惟帝時克益曰都帝德廣運乃聖乃神乃
武乃文
嶓冢導漾東流爲漢又東爲滄浪之水過
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

中庸之爲德也，其至矣乎！

言而民莫不信，行而民莫不說。

可欲之謂善，有諸己之謂信，充實之謂美，充實而有光輝之謂大，大而化之之謂聖，聖而不可知之之謂神。

易

中正以觀天下。

上九，鼎玉鉉，大吉，无不利。

以言乎天地之間，則備矣。夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉。夫坤，其靜也翕，其動也闢，是以廣生焉。廣大配天地。

齊也者，言萬物之潔齊也。

書

惟帝時克。益曰：「都！帝德廣運，乃聖乃神，乃武乃文。」

嶓冢導漾，東流爲漢，又東爲滄浪之水，過
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

As a virtue, is not the constant mean the highest perfection!

When he speaks, none among the people fails to trust him; when he acts, none among the people fails to be pleased.

What is desirable is called goodness. Possessing it in oneself is called authenticity. Being filled with it is called beauty. Being filled with it and radiating brilliance is called greatness. Being great and exercising a transforming influence is called sagehood. Being a sage whose workings cannot be fathomed is called spirit-like.

Book of Changes

Through centrality and correctness, he presents a model for all under Heaven.

Nine at the top: the cauldron has a jade carrying bar. Great good fortune; nothing is unfavorable.

As for what lies between Heaven and Earth, it is all encompassed here. Qian, when still, is concentrated; when moving, is direct. Thus it brings forth greatness. Kun, when still, is closed; when moving, is open. Thus it brings forth breadth. In breadth and greatness they match Heaven and Earth.

“Making things even” means that the myriad things are purified and brought into order.

Book of Documents

Only the emperor can accomplish this. Yi said: “Ah! The emperor’s virtue extends far and wide. He is sagely and spirit-like, martial and cultivated.”

From Bozhong, he traced the course of the Yang River. Flowing east, it becomes the Han; farther east, it becomes the waters of the Canglang, passing …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
三澨至于大別南入于江東匯澤為彭
蠡東為北江入于海岷山導江東別為
沱又東至于澧過九江至于東陵東迆
北會為匯東為中江入于海導沇水東
流為濟入于河溢為滎東出于陶丘北
又東至于菏又東北會于汶又北東入
于海導淮自桐栢東會于泗沂東入于
海
皇建其有極斂時五福用敷錫厥庶民
===
其克詰爾戎兵以陟禹之迹方行天下至
于海表罔有不服
詩
羔裘晏兮三英粲兮彼其之子邦之彦兮
君子萬年福祿綏之
鳳凰于飛翽翽其羽亦集爰止藹藹王多
吉士維君子使媚于天子鳳凰于飛翽
翽其羽亦傅于天藹藹王多吉人維君
子命媚于庶人鳳凰鳴矣于彼高岡梧
punctuated:
三澨，至于大別，南入于江，東匯澤為彭蠡，東為北江，入于海。岷山導江，東別為沱，又東至于澧，過九江，至于東陵，東迆，北會為匯，東為中江，入于海。導沇水，東流為濟，入于河，溢為滎，東出于陶丘北，又東至于菏，又東北會于汶，又北，東入于海。導淮自桐栢，東會于泗、沂，東入于海。
皇建其有極，斂時五福，用敷錫厥庶民。
其克詰爾戎兵，以陟禹之迹，方行天下，至于海表，罔有不服。
詩
羔裘晏兮，三英粲兮！彼其之子，邦之彦兮！
君子萬年，福祿綏之。
鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦集爰止。藹藹王多吉士，維君子使，媚于天子。鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦傅于天。藹藹王多吉人，維君子命，媚于庶人。鳳凰鳴矣，于彼高岡；梧
translation_en:
…past Sanshi, reaching Dabie, then south into the Jiang; eastward, the waters collect in a marsh to form Pengli, then flow east as the Northern Jiang and enter the sea. From Mount Min, the Jiang was channeled; eastward it branches off as the Tuo, then proceeds farther east to the Li, passes the Nine Rivers, and reaches Dongling. Winding eastward, it converges to the north to form a great gathering of waters, then flows east as the Central Jiang and enters the sea. The Yan River was channeled; flowing east, it becomes the Ji, enters the He, and overflows to form the Xing. It emerges eastward north of Taoqiu, continues east to the He 菏, then northeast to join the Wen, and then north, before entering the sea to the east. The Huai was channeled from Tongbai; eastward it joins the Si and Yi and enters the sea.
The sovereign establishes the supreme standard, gathering these five blessings and bestowing them widely upon his common people.
May you put your troops and weapons in good order, advancing over the lands where Yu left his traces and marching freely throughout all under Heaven, even beyond the seas, with none failing to submit.
Book of Odes
How splendid is his lambskin coat! How brilliant its three ornaments! That man is an outstanding talent of the state!
May the lord live ten thousand years; may blessings and emoluments bring him peace.
The phoenixes fly, their feathers rustling; they gather and come to rest here. Abundant are the king’s worthy officers: the lord employs them, and they are beloved by the Son of Heaven. The phoenixes fly, their feathers rustling; they reach up to Heaven. Abundant are the king’s worthy men: the lord appoints them, and they are beloved by the common people. The phoenixes call upon that high ridge; the wutong…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
桐生矣于彼朝陽菶菶萋萋雝雝喈喈
豐年多黍多稂亦有高廩萬億及秭爲酒
爲醴烝畀祖妣以洽百禮降福孔皆
春秋
冬十有二月會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯
許男滑伯滕子同盟于幽〔莊公十有六年〕
夏六月公孫敖會宋公陳侯鄭伯晉士縠
盟于垂隴〔文公二年〕晉放其大夫胥甲
===
父于衛〔宣公元年〕冬十有一月庚午蔡
侯以吳子及楚人戰于栢舉楚師敗績
楚囊瓦出奔鄭　庚辰吳入郢〔俱定公四年〕
晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕夏曹公孫會
自鄸出奔宋〔昭公二十年〕
夏公會齊侯于夾谷公至自夾谷〔定公十年〕
禮記
punctuated:
桐生矣，于彼朝陽。菶菶萋萋，雝雝喈喈。
豐年多黍多稂，亦有高廩，萬億及秭。爲酒爲醴，烝畀祖妣，以洽百禮，降福孔皆。
春秋
冬十有二月，會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、滑伯、滕子，同盟于幽。〔莊公十有六年〕
夏六月，公孫敖會宋公、陳侯、鄭伯、晉士縠，盟于垂隴。〔文公二年〕晉放其大夫胥甲父于衛。〔宣公元年〕冬十有一月庚午，蔡侯以吳子及楚人戰于栢舉，楚師敗績，楚囊瓦出奔鄭。庚辰，吳入郢。〔俱定公四年〕
晉欒書帥師救鄭。〔成公六年〕夏，曹公孫會自鄸出奔宋。〔昭公二十年〕
夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。〔定公十年〕
禮記
translation_en:
…the parasol tree grows on that east-facing slope. Lush and luxuriant is its foliage; harmonious and melodious are the phoenixes’ calls.
In a year of abundant harvests there is much millet and much darnel [?], and lofty granaries hold grain in countless millions. They make wine and sweet liquor and present them to their ancestral fathers and mothers, completing the hundred rites. Blessings descend in fullest measure.
Spring and Autumn Annals
In winter, in the twelfth month, [the Duke of Lu] met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Hua, and the Viscount of Teng. Together they concluded a covenant at You. 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
In summer, in the sixth month, Gongsun Ao met the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, and Shi Hu of Jin, and they concluded a covenant at Chuilong. 〔Second year of Duke Wen.〕 Jin banished its Grand Master, Xu Jiafu, to Wei. 〔First year of Duke Xuan.〕 In winter, in the eleventh month, on the gengwu day, the Marquis of Cai, with the Viscount of Wu, fought the men of Chu at Boju. The army of Chu suffered a crushing defeat. Nang Wa of Chu fled to Zheng. On the gengchen day, Wu entered Ying. 〔Both entries belong to the fourth year of Duke Ding.〕
Luan Shu of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng. 〔Sixth year of Duke Cheng.〕 In summer, Gongsun Hui of Cao fled from Meng to Song. 〔Twentieth year of Duke Zhao.〕
In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu. 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding.〕
Book of Rites

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
旅幣無方所以别土地之宜而節遠邇之
期也龜爲前列先知也以鐘次之以和
居參之也虎豹之皮示服猛也束帛加
璧往德也
久則天天則神天則不言而信神則不怒
而威
福者備也備者百順之名也
外無敵内順治此之謂盛德
第貳場
===
===
論
聖人太極之全體
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢戒俗吏矯飾者詔〔元和二年〕
擬唐以楊綰爲國子祭酒誥〔大曆五年〕
擬宋作敬天圖羣臣賀表〔乾道七年〕
判語〔五條〕
擅離職役
漏用鈔印
punctuated:
旅幣無方，所以别土地之宜而節遠邇之期也。龜爲前列，先知也；以鐘次之，以和居參之也；虎豹之皮，示服猛也；束帛加璧，往德也。
久則天，天則神。天則不言而信，神則不怒而威。
福者，備也；備者，百順之名也。
外無敵，内順治，此之謂盛德。
第貳場
論
聖人太極之全體。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢戒俗吏矯飾者詔〔元和二年〕。
擬唐以楊綰爲國子祭酒誥〔大曆五年〕。
擬宋作敬天圖羣臣賀表〔乾道七年〕。
判語〔五條〕
擅離職役。
漏用鈔印。
translation_en:
The tribute offerings are displayed without a fixed arrangement, so as to distinguish the appropriate products of each region and regulate the intervals of presentation according to distance. Tortoises are placed foremost because they possess foreknowledge. Bells come next, with harmony occupying the third position [?]. Tiger and leopard skins demonstrate the subjugation of fierce creatures. Bundles of silk topped with jade discs convey beneficence.
Through enduring constancy one becomes like Heaven; through becoming like Heaven one becomes numinous. Like Heaven, one commands trust without speaking; being numinous, one inspires awe without anger.
Blessing means completeness; completeness is the name for the hundred forms of favorable accord.
Having no enemies abroad and harmonious government within: this is called consummate virtue.
Second Session
Discourse
The sage embodies the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety.
Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One topic from among these [?]〕
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor admonishing commonplace officials who engage in false displays of virtue. 〔Second year of Yuanhe〕
Compose a proclamation in the voice of a Tang emperor appointing Yang Wan as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education. 〔Fifth year of Dali〕
Compose a congratulatory memorial in the voice of the assembled Song officials on the production of the Diagram of Reverence for Heaven. 〔Seventh year of Qiandao〕
Legal judgments 〔Five items〕
Leaving one's official post or assigned service without authorization.
Failure to apply the banknote seal [?].

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
優恤軍士
驛使稽程
修理倉庫
第參場
策五道
問自古帝王君臨天下繼天立極而皇極
之說載在洪範訪之者武王敘之者禹
而啓之者天也然洪範九疇而獨以皇
極居五者何耶說者訓皇以大訓極以
===
中所謂惟大作中大則受之者然歟否
也若以中極爲二則帝王相授守一道
何堯舜禹湯言執中建中而武王則曰
建極也可得聞其說歟歷漢而唐而宋
雖亦能輝煌治具然而此義未明無怪
乎治不古若也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
文武聖神親註洪範立我蒸民莫匪爾極肆
我
punctuated:
優恤軍士。
驛使稽程。
修理倉庫。

第參場
策五道

問：自古帝王君臨天下，繼天立極，而皇極之說載在《洪範》，訪之者武王，敘之者禹，而啓之者天也。然《洪範》九疇，而獨以皇極居五者，何耶？說者訓皇以大，訓極以中，所謂「惟大作中，大則受之」者，然歟否也？若以中極爲二，則帝王相授守一道，何堯舜禹湯言執中、建中，而武王則曰建極也？可得聞其說歟？歷漢而唐而宋，雖亦能輝煌治具，然而此義未明，無怪乎治不古若也。洪惟我太祖高皇帝，文武聖神，親註《洪範》，立我蒸民，莫匪爾極。肆我
translation_en:
Provide preferential relief for soldiers.
Postal couriers exceeding the prescribed travel time.
Repair granaries and storehouses.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: From antiquity, emperors and kings have ruled all under Heaven, succeeding Heaven and establishing the supreme standard. The teaching concerning the August Standard (huangji) is recorded in the Great Plan (Hongfan): King Wu inquired about it, Yu set it forth, and Heaven revealed it. Yet among the Great Plan’s nine categories, why does the August Standard specifically occupy the fifth position? Commentators explain huang as “great” and ji as “the mean.” Is the saying “Only the great establishes the mean; being great, it receives it” [?] correct or not? If the mean and the supreme standard are taken as two different things, emperors and kings nevertheless transmit and uphold a single Way. Why, then, did Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang speak of “holding fast to the mean” and “establishing the mean,” whereas King Wu spoke of “establishing the supreme standard”? May we hear an explanation?

Throughout the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, although the institutions of government could attain great splendor, this principle remained unclear. It is therefore no wonder that their government fell short of antiquity. We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao, accomplished in civil and military affairs, sagely and divine, personally annotated the Great Plan and established our multitudinous people, so that none failed to follow his supreme standard. Thus our …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
皇上統天御宇四十三年於茲
仁孝誠敬各協于極而薄海内外咸順帝則
信可謂建其有極歸其有極矣頃者頒
殿堂聿成之詔伏讀
聖製有曰帝王以至敬事
天必順承因革之
命以達孝尊
祖必善通繼述之權更名
正殿及門曰
===
皇極中曰
中極後曰
建極左右閣曰文昭武成左右門曰會極歸極
東西角門曰弘政宣治仰見
皇上敬
天法
祖
大聖人之所作為發自古帝王之所未發爰立
名義允協鴻謨經緯
punctuated: 皇上統天御宇四十三年於茲，仁孝誠敬，各協于極，而薄海内外咸順帝則，信可謂建其有極、歸其有極矣。頃者頒殿堂聿成之詔，伏讀聖製，有曰：「帝王以至敬事天，必順承因革之命；以達孝尊祖，必善通繼述之權。更名正殿及門曰皇極，中曰中極，後曰建極，左右閣曰文昭、武成，左右門曰會極、歸極，東西角門曰弘政、宣治。」仰見皇上敬天法祖，大聖人之所作為，發自古帝王之所未發。爰立名義，允協鴻謨，經緯
translation_en:
…His Majesty has now ruled all under Heaven for forty-three years. His benevolence, filial piety, sincerity, and reverence each accord with the supreme standard, while all within and beyond the seas obey the imperial norm. Truly, this may be called establishing the supreme standard and bringing all to return to it.

Recently, an edict was issued announcing the completion of the palace halls. Reverently reading this imperial composition, we find these words: “When emperors and kings serve Heaven with utmost reverence, they must obediently receive its mandate concerning what to retain and what to change. When they honor their ancestors with consummate filial piety, they must skillfully exercise discretion in carrying on their predecessors’ work. The principal hall and its gate are renamed Huangji [August Ultimate]; the central hall, Zhongji [Central Ultimate]; and the rear hall, Jianji [Establishing the Ultimate]. The pavilions to the left and right are named Wenzhao [Civil Splendor] and Wucheng [Martial Achievement]; the gates to the left and right, Huiji [Converging upon the Ultimate] and Guiji [Returning to the Ultimate]; and the eastern and western corner gates, Hongzheng [Expanding Good Government] and Xuanzhi [Spreading Good Governance].”

We look up and perceive how His Majesty reveres Heaven and models himself upon his ancestors. These deeds of a great sage reveal what emperors and kings since antiquity have never revealed. The meanings embodied in the names thus established fully accord with his grand plan, ordering…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
乾坤光昭
日月莫可尚已其淵微奧旨抑可仰窺其萬
一歟昔孔子翼易曰易有太極是生兩
儀兩儀生四象四象生八卦厥後宋儒
有經世之作凡以極之一言而天地萬
物之理寓焉我
皇上稽古考文
宸衷睿思與
天合一所以衍億萬年無疆之慶端在是矣諸
===
生涵濡
聖化必有獨觀其深者願敬對揚之無略
問孔子刪述六經詩書禮樂皆雅言之惟
於易則韋編三絶至晚年始無大過春
秋志獨在焉雖文學如游夏猶不能贊
一辭信乎天地鬼神之奧史外傳心之
要典也漢魏而下學易春秋者靡不鏘
然以其說鳴於時而得其近似者無幾
是故有為氣朔之說者有為日星之說
punctuated:
乾坤，光昭日月，莫可尚已。其淵微奧旨，抑可仰窺其萬一歟？昔孔子翼易曰：「易有太極，是生兩儀，兩儀生四象，四象生八卦。」厥後宋儒有經世之作，凡以極之一言，而天地萬物之理寓焉。我皇上稽古考文，宸衷睿思，與天合一，所以衍億萬年無疆之慶，端在是矣。諸生涵濡聖化，必有獨觀其深者，願敬對揚之，無略。

問：孔子刪述六經，詩、書、禮、樂皆雅言之，惟於易則韋編三絶，至晚年始無大過。春秋志獨在焉，雖文學如游夏，猶不能贊一辭。信乎天地鬼神之奧，史外傳心之要典也。漢魏而下，學易、春秋者，靡不鏘然以其說鳴於時，而得其近似者無幾。是故有為氣朔之說者，有為日星之說
translation_en:
…Heaven and Earth, shining as brightly as the sun and moon: nothing could surpass this. Yet might we reverently glimpse even a ten-thousandth part of its profound and subtle meaning? In former times, Confucius, in his supplementary commentary to the Changes, said: “The Changes has the Supreme Ultimate, which generates the two modes; the two modes generate the four images; the four images generate the eight trigrams.” Subsequently, scholars of the Song produced works on the ordering of the world. Within the single word “Ultimate” are lodged the principles of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things. Our Emperor investigates antiquity and examines its cultural forms; his sagacious imperial thoughts are one with Heaven. Precisely herein lies the means of extending boundless blessings for hundreds of millions of years. You students, steeped in the sage Emperor’s transforming influence, must have distinctive insights into these depths. We ask you to respond reverently and expound upon them, omitting nothing.

Question: Confucius edited and transmitted the Six Classics. He spoke in the standard language when discussing the Odes, Documents, Rites, and Music. Yet in studying the Changes, he wore through the leather binding thongs three times, and only in his later years did he become free from major errors. In the Spring and Autumn Annals, his purpose found its particular expression. Even men as accomplished in literary learning as Ziyou and Zixia could not contribute a single phrase. Truly these are essential canonical works encompassing the mysteries of Heaven, Earth, ghosts, and spirits, and transmitting the mind beyond the historical record. From the Han and Wei onward, those who studied the Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals all made their doctrines resound in their own age; yet few attained even an approximation of their meaning. Thus some advanced theories concerning solar terms and new moons, while others advanced theories concerning the sun and stars…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
者有為虛氣之說者而其說長矣或善
於理而失之誣或善於讖而失之短或
善於經而失之俗而其失多矣甚則父
子以經術重漢廷者乃為子母之言以
重悖經義又何取於明經也惟朱熹氏
啟蒙綱目之作獨得聖人心法於千載
之上其微辭奧義可得而言之乎夫先
天圖易之本後天圖易之用八卦成列
而象在其中矣啟蒙之所發明其於圖
===
畫之理何者足以盡其蘊說者曰明蓍
策而掛扐之法定考變占而趨避之見
審其占蓍之法可盡言乎春秋之時五
霸迭興天下不知有周久矣夫子因魯
史以尊周而後天王之號始正是尊周
固春秋之權輿也綱目之所載記其於
尊周之意何者足以同其神說者曰歲
周於上而天道明統正於下而人道定
其天人之際可盡言乎朱熹氏闡之徒
punctuated: 者，有為虛氣之說者，而其說長矣。或善於理而失之誣，或善於讖而失之短，或善於經而失之俗，而其失多矣。甚則父子以經術重漢廷者，乃為子母之言，以重悖經義，又何取於明經也？惟朱熹氏《啟蒙》《綱目》之作，獨得聖人心法於千載之上，其微辭奧義可得而言之乎？夫先天圖，易之本；後天圖，易之用。八卦成列，而象在其中矣。《啟蒙》之所發明，其於圖畫之理，何者足以盡其蘊？說者曰：「明蓍策而掛扐之法定，考變占而趨避之見審。」其占蓍之法可盡言乎？春秋之時，五霸迭興，天下不知有周久矣。夫子因魯史以尊周，而後天王之號始正，是尊周固《春秋》之權輿也。《綱目》之所載記，其於尊周之意，何者足以同其神？說者曰：「歲周於上而天道明，統正於下而人道定。」其天人之際可盡言乎？朱熹氏闡之，徒
translation_en:
…and those who advance theories of empty qi; their explanations have become lengthy indeed. Some excel in principle but lapse into unfounded claims; some excel in prognostication but lapse into narrowness; some excel in interpreting the classics but lapse into vulgarity. Their errors are numerous indeed. Worse still, a father and son esteemed at the Han court for their classical learning actually propounded explanations concerning child and mother, thereby further contradicting the meaning of the classics. What value, then, was there in their mastery of the classics?

Only Zhu Xi, in his Introduction to the Study of the Changes (Qimeng) and Outline and Details (Gangmu), uniquely grasped the sages’ teaching of the mind from more than a thousand years before. Can their subtle expressions and profound meanings be articulated? The Earlier Heaven Diagram is the foundation of the Changes; the Later Heaven Diagram is its application. When the eight trigrams are arrayed, the images are contained within them. Of what the Introduction elucidates concerning the principles of these diagrams, what suffices to exhaust their implications? Commentators say: “Once the yarrow stalks are understood, the procedures for setting aside a stalk and placing remainders between the fingers are established; once changing lines and their prognostications are examined, judgments about what to pursue and avoid become precise.” Can its method of divination with yarrow stalks be explained in full?

In the Spring and Autumn period, the Five Hegemons arose in succession, and the world had long ceased to acknowledge Zhou. The Master drew upon the annals of Lu to honor Zhou, and only then was the designation ‘Heavenly King’ properly established. Honoring Zhou is thus indeed the starting point of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Among the records in the Outline and Details, what suffices to embody that same spirit of honoring Zhou? Commentators say: “The years are fully set out above, making the Way of Heaven clear; legitimate succession is rectified below, establishing the Way of humanity.” Can this relationship between Heaven and humanity be explained in full? Zhu Xi elucidated these matters, yet was merely…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
哲也而二書所得於孔氏之家法具在
諸士師孔子以朱熹氏爲正脈計必有
得其真傳者盍相與闡究之
問守令與民最親者在漢拜刺史守令輒
親見問有治理效璽書勉勵增秩賜金
公卿缺選所表以次用之是以一時刺
史如京兆南陽潁川渤海皆以治行稱
第一有以茂陵令而遷刺史以小黃令
而被增秩至今言吏治者歸焉在唐尤
===
重其任不歷刺史不得任侍郎不歷郡
縣不得任臺省是以長吏如冀州瀛州
滄州皆有治行號爲河北三刺史有令
武陽而孳孳惠愛令昌邑而以俸代輸
賦此皆一時之選也在宋慶曆間銳意
治安富弼范仲淹首言守令之稱職在
監司之得人文法多從寬假而守令列
至公卿遂成忠厚立國之治焉之三代
者其制其人可歷數而言之歟今我
punctuated:
哲也，而二書所得於孔氏之家法具在。諸士師孔子，以朱熹氏爲正脈，計必有得其真傳者，盍相與闡究之？

問：守令與民最親者。在漢，拜刺史、守令，輒親見問；有治理效，璽書勉勵，增秩賜金；公卿缺，選所表，以次用之。是以一時刺史，如京兆、南陽、潁川、渤海，皆以治行稱第一。有以茂陵令而遷刺史，以小黃令而被增秩，至今言吏治者歸焉。在唐，尤重其任，不歷刺史，不得任侍郎；不歷郡縣，不得任臺省。是以長吏如冀州、瀛州、滄州，皆有治行，號爲河北三刺史。有令武陽而孳孳惠愛，令昌邑而以俸代輸賦，此皆一時之選也。在宋慶曆間，銳意治安，富弼、范仲淹首言守令之稱職，在監司之得人。文法多從寬假，而守令列至公卿，遂成忠厚立國之治焉。之三代者，其制其人，可歷數而言之歟？今我
translation_en:
…a wise man [?]; and in these two books, what was derived from the interpretive tradition of Confucius remains fully present. You gentlemen take Confucius as your teacher and regard Zhu Xi as the orthodox line of transmission. Surely some among you have grasped the authentic teaching. Why not together elucidate and investigate it?

Question: Prefects and county magistrates are the officials closest to the people. Under the Han, whenever regional inspectors, prefects, and county magistrates were appointed, the emperor would personally receive and question them. Those whose administration produced results were encouraged by letters bearing the imperial seal, advanced in rank, and rewarded with gold. When vacancies arose among the dukes and ministers, selections were made from those recommended, and they were appointed in turn. Thus regional inspectors of the time [?], such as those of Jingzhao, Nanyang, Yingchuan, and Bohai, were all acclaimed as foremost for their administrative performance. One was promoted from magistrate of Maoling to regional inspector; another received an increase in rank while magistrate of Xiaohuang. To this day, those who discuss the administration of officials look to these examples.

Under the Tang, particular weight was given to these appointments. Without having served as a prefect, one could not become a vice minister; without experience in prefectural and county administration, one could not hold office in the central censorial and secretarial agencies. Thus the chief local officials of Jizhou, Yingzhou, and Cangzhou all distinguished themselves in administration and were known as the Three Prefects of Hebei. One, while magistrate of Wuyang, diligently bestowed kindness and care; another, while magistrate of Changyi, used his salary to pay the people's taxes on their behalf. These were all outstanding selections of their time.

During the Qingli reign period of the Song, determined efforts were made to secure good government and peace. Fu Bi and Fan Zhongyan were the first to argue that competent prefects and county magistrates depended on obtaining the right men as circuit supervisors. In applying legal and administrative regulations, leniency was generally preferred, and prefects and county magistrates rose as high as the ranks of dukes and ministers. Thus a form of government was achieved that founded the state upon loyalty and generosity. As for these three dynasties [?], can their institutions and the men who served under them be enumerated and discussed in detail? Now our…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
皇上加惠黎元脩飭吏治乃
詔諸司憲臣條奏不職者黜之更置良吏務和
民人以登諸理媲隆唐虞成周之治而
陋漢唐宋於不足言矣玆欲盡得謹身
帥先居以廉平者出而效用仰副
皇上置吏親民至意果何道以致之歟或者以
久任爲言所以重責成也然卓異無以
自見竟沮其激勸之機以超遷爲言所
以示優異也然吏數易則下不安實開
===
其競進之路二說旣難於竝行則又何
施而後可諸士其悉言之將以轉聞於
上
問八閩稱文獻之邦其名宦鄉賢載諸史
冊者班班可覩記已尚友者論其世居
鄉者淑其人玆舉其表著者與諸士商
焉其宦於玆有鼎建學校而親臨講道
者有申明覲典而累表蒙褒者孰爲得
先務之急有諭强悍以義理而健訟屏
punctuated:
皇上加惠黎元，脩飭吏治，乃詔諸司憲臣條奏不職者，黜之，更置良吏，務和民人，以登諸理，媲隆唐虞成周之治，而陋漢唐宋於不足言矣。玆欲盡得謹身帥先、居以廉平者，出而效用，仰副皇上置吏親民至意，果何道以致之歟？或者以久任爲言，所以重責成也，然卓異無以自見，竟沮其激勸之機；以超遷爲言，所以示優異也，然吏數易則下不安，實開其競進之路。二說旣難於竝行，則又何施而後可？諸士其悉言之，將以轉聞於上。

問：八閩稱文獻之邦，其名宦鄉賢載諸史冊者，班班可覩記已。尚友者論其世，居鄉者淑其人。玆舉其表著者，與諸士商焉。其宦於玆，有鼎建學校而親臨講道者，有申明覲典而累表蒙褒者，孰爲得先務之急？有諭强悍以義理而健訟屏
translation_en:
…His Majesty extends his benevolence to the common people and reforms the administration of officials. He therefore commanded the censorial officials of the various offices to submit itemized reports on those unfit for their duties, dismiss them, and appoint good officials in their place. The aim is to bring harmony to the people and achieve good order, matching the flourishing government of Yao and Shun and the Zhou dynasty at its height, while rendering the achievements of the Han, Tang, and Song too paltry to mention. Now we wish to obtain all those who discipline themselves, lead by example, and conduct themselves with integrity and impartiality, so that they may come forward to serve and fulfill His Majesty’s profound intention in appointing officials to care for the people. By what means can this actually be achieved? Some advocate long tenure, as a way to emphasize responsibility for results. Yet exceptionally able officials would have no means of distinguishing themselves, ultimately frustrating the incentive to excel. Others advocate promotion beyond the usual grades, as a way to show special favor to outstanding officials. Yet frequent changes of officials unsettle those below and open the way to competition for advancement. Since these two proposals are difficult to implement together, what measures would be appropriate? You candidates should state your views fully, so that they may be conveyed to His Majesty.

Question: The Eight Min regions of Fujian are renowned as a land of cultural achievement and learned worthies. Its celebrated officials and local worthies recorded in the histories are plainly evident [?]. Those who seek friendship with the ancients consider the age in which they lived; those who dwell in a locality improve its people. We now select some of the most prominent examples for discussion with you candidates. Among those who served as officials here, some founded schools and personally attended to expound the Way; others reaffirmed the regulations governing court audiences and received praise through repeated memorials [?]. Which best understood the urgency of attending to first things? Some instructed the fierce and unruly in moral principles, so that habitual litigants were driven…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
迹者有挾禁兵之鎮地而海寇悉平者
孰爲得治劇之宜清淨德化所至不煩
節省得民碎碑示禁可謂清矣得無少
鷹鸇之志乎庫牓備安器嚴萬鎧申明
節制措置海防可謂謀矣得無多杞人
之慮乎令行禁止至誠感人保障之體
宏矣而日月爭光木蘭遺愛其人品孰
優築海爲湖捫鐘驗盜其發姦之機熟
矣而庭無留訟力制豪併其治行孰最
===
凡此流風善政固有家傳而人誦者可
得而評品之歟其産於茲有議棄靈州
不奉草制之詔者有召學扶溝不爲世
儒之習者其風裁爲孰著有正學家傳
致松栢獨秀之譽有潭州諭屬切同胞
一體之情其雅致爲孰高朐山治範都
水效能清白名官口義傳世用心勞矣
豈陶侃砥柱中流乎流民繪圖唐相分
軸七人去國萬里還家納忠懇矣豈夷
punctuated:
迹者，有挾禁兵之鎮地而海寇悉平者，孰爲得治劇之宜？清淨德化，所至不煩；節省得民，碎碑示禁，可謂清矣，得無少鷹鸇之志乎？庫牓備安，器嚴萬鎧，申明節制，措置海防，可謂謀矣，得無多杞人之慮乎？令行禁止，至誠感人，保障之體宏矣，而日月爭光、木蘭遺愛，其人品孰優？築海爲湖，捫鐘驗盜，其發姦之機熟矣，而庭無留訟、力制豪併，其治行孰最？

凡此流風善政，固有家傳而人誦者，可得而評品之歟？其産於茲，有議棄靈州、不奉草制之詔者，有召學扶溝、不爲世儒之習者，其風裁爲孰著？有正學家傳，致松栢獨秀之譽；有潭州諭屬，切同胞一體之情，其雅致爲孰高？朐山治範，都水效能，清白名官，口義傳世，用心勞矣，豈陶侃砥柱中流乎？流民繪圖，唐相分軸，七人去國，萬里還家，納忠懇矣，豈夷
translation_en:
…vanished without a trace; another commanded imperial guard troops stationed in the region and completely pacified the sea raiders. Who best understood how to govern a troubled jurisdiction? Through quiet government and moral transformation, they avoided vexing the people wherever they served; through economy they won the people’s support, and by smashing a stele they made a prohibition known. Such conduct may be called pure, but did it perhaps lack the resolve of hawks and falcons? Posting notices at the storehouses to ensure security and rigorously preparing arms and ten thousand suits of armor [?], clarifying military discipline, and arranging coastal defenses—these may be called foresight, but did they perhaps show too much of the man of Qi’s fear that the sky would fall? Their commands were obeyed and their prohibitions observed; their utter sincerity moved others. Their capacity to protect the people was great. Yet, between the one whose glory rivaled the sun and moon and the one whose benevolent legacy endured at Mulan, whose personal character was superior? Building an embankment against the sea to create a lake, and having suspects touch a bell to identify a thief—their devices for uncovering wrongdoing were well practiced. Yet, between the one whose court had no unresolved lawsuits and the one who vigorously restrained powerful engrossers of property, whose administrative achievements were greatest?

All these enduring influences and excellent policies have surely been transmitted within households and celebrated by the people. Can you assess and rank them? Among those born here, one argued for abandoning Lingzhou and refused an imperial order to draft a decree; another summoned students to study at Fugou and shunned the habits of conventional scholars. Whose principled bearing was more distinguished? One transmitted orthodox learning within his family, earning praise as a pine or cypress standing alone in excellence; another admonished his subordinates at Tanzhou, expressing a deep sense that all people were siblings forming a single body. Whose noble aspirations were loftier? Exemplary government at Qushan, effective service in the Directorate of Waterways, a reputation for purity and integrity in office, and Oral Interpretations handed down to posterity—these reflect painstaking devotion. Was he a Tao Kan, a pillar of rock standing firm in midstream? Painting a picture of displaced people, depicting Tang chief councilors on separate scrolls [?], seven men leaving the capital, and returning home over ten thousand li—these reflect earnest devotion in offering loyal counsel. Was he, after Yi…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
齊之後一人乎三朝老成五朝一節當
時之顯相也而徹樂辭花抗言日錄孰
爲善用其剛高麗寄聲洛陽問易一代
之儒碩也而馳聲四諫經理兩河孰爲
善藏其用凡此嘉言善行必有聞風而
興起者可得而論述之歟夫遭遇不同
德業亦異數君子之外抑尚有其人乎
其爲我詳言之用觀嚮往之志
問士之夙抱經濟將期以效用於時也試
===
===
以今閩中所最切而當預計者籌之夫
八郡枕山襟海峒丁盤窟島酋駛舟屢
歲流毒致廑我
皇上軫念元元
頒給內帑調發客兵
天恩浩蕩一時文武效謀旋就厎定卽東南億
萬生靈烝烝然覩太平之象矣然而桑
土之防衣袽之戒當事者未能一日忘
兵食計也計兵者有曰練民壯曰嚴保
punctuated:
齊之後一人乎？三朝老成，五朝一節，當時之顯相也，而徹樂辭花，抗言日錄，孰爲善用其剛？高麗寄聲，洛陽問易，一代之儒碩也，而馳聲四諫，經理兩河，孰爲善藏其用？凡此嘉言善行，必有聞風而興起者，可得而論述之歟？夫遭遇不同，德業亦異，數君子之外，抑尚有其人乎？其爲我詳言之，用觀嚮往之志。
問：士之夙抱經濟，將期以效用於時也。試以今閩中所最切而當預計者籌之。夫八郡枕山襟海，峒丁盤窟，島酋駛舟，屢歲流毒，致廑我皇上軫念元元，頒給內帑，調發客兵。天恩浩蕩，一時文武效謀，旋就厎定，卽東南億萬生靈烝烝然覩太平之象矣。然而桑土之防，衣袽之戒，當事者未能一日忘兵食計也。計兵者，有曰練民壯，曰嚴保
translation_en:
…the one man after Boyi and Shuqi? One was a seasoned statesman through three reigns; another maintained unwavering integrity through five. They were eminent chief councillors of their day. Yet in having music withdrawn and declining flowers, and in speaking out concerning the Daily Record [?], which better employed his firmness? One received messages from Goryeo; another was consulted about the Book of Changes in Luoyang [?]. They were outstanding Confucian scholars of their age. Yet in winning renown among the Four Remonstrators and in administering the two He regions, which better kept his abilities in reserve? Surely these admirable words and good deeds have inspired others who heard of them. Can you discuss and recount them? Their circumstances differed, and so did their virtue and accomplishments. Besides these gentlemen, were there still others? Explain this fully for me, so that I may discern the aspirations toward which you incline.
Question: Scholars have long cherished ambitions for statecraft, hoping to put their abilities to use in their own times. Consider, then, the most pressing matters in Fujian today for which plans should be made in advance. Its eight prefectures have mountains at their backs and the sea along their front. Fighting men from mountain settlements occupy their lairs, while island chieftains ply their vessels. For successive years they spread devastation, causing our Emperor to be deeply concerned for the common people. He bestowed funds from the imperial treasury and dispatched troops from other regions. Imperial grace was boundless; civil and military officials alike contributed their plans, and order was soon restored. The countless inhabitants of the southeast then beheld, in flourishing abundance, the signs of peace.
Nevertheless, mindful of securing the nest with mulberry roots before the storm and keeping rags ready to plug a leaking boat, those responsible cannot let a single day pass without considering troops and provisions. Among proposals concerning troops, some advocate training the local militia; others advocate tightening the bao …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
甲曰簡衛士曰操戰艦皆土著之議也
而寇至萬計不識能備緩急乎萬一不
支客兵可招募否也計食者有曰屯田
曰鬻田曰鹽筴曰錢法皆軍餉之資也
而兵旅繁興不識得免告匱乎萬一不
支積逋可追徵否也說者又謂調客兵
渴者掘井而飲也追積逋罟者竭澤而
漁也則兵食遂無策乎更番敎閱汰去
老弱作其敵愾之勇示以親長之義兵
===
尚可為也獨食之不足君子有隱憂焉
昔人有言天地生財不在官則在民今
一切冗食盡報罷矣甚則官司二簋用
享百度從儉至為權宜補救之術而筦
庫旣絀閭閻之民非有額外之征而財
力亦巳盡矣在官在民之說果不足信
乎抑將復有遠策以濟之乎諸士切時
艱而慨於衷欲起而抒經濟之略素矣
其抵掌談之毋隱
punctuated: 甲，曰簡衛士，曰操戰艦，皆土著之議也。而寇至萬計，不識能備緩急乎？萬一不支，客兵可招募否也？計食者，有曰屯田，曰鬻田，曰鹽筴，曰錢法，皆軍餉之資也。而兵旅繁興，不識得免告匱乎？萬一不支，積逋可追徵否也？說者又謂調客兵，渴者掘井而飲也；追積逋，罟者竭澤而漁也。則兵食遂無策乎？更番敎閱，汰去老弱，作其敵愾之勇，示以親長之義，兵尚可為也。獨食之不足，君子有隱憂焉。昔人有言：「天地生財，不在官則在民。」今一切冗食盡報罷矣，甚則官司二簋用享，百度從儉，至為權宜補救之術。而筦庫旣絀，閭閻之民非有額外之征，而財力亦巳盡矣。在官在民之說，果不足信乎？抑將復有遠策以濟之乎？諸士切時艱而慨於衷，欲起而抒經濟之略素矣。其抵掌談之，毋隱！
translation_en: …jia units [of the baojia system]; others propose selecting guard soldiers or drilling warships. These proposals all rely on the local population. Yet the raiders arrive in their tens of thousands: can such measures meet an emergency? Should they prove inadequate, could troops from elsewhere be recruited? Those planning provisions propose military agricultural colonies, the sale of land, salt administration schemes, and currency measures—all sources of military funding. Yet with military forces being mobilized in great numbers, can shortages be avoided? Should these resources prove inadequate, could accumulated tax arrears be recovered? Some further argue that bringing in outside troops is like a thirsty person digging a well to obtain a drink, and that collecting accumulated arrears is like a fisherman draining a lake to catch fish. Are there, then, no workable plans for troops and provisions? By training and inspecting men in rotation, weeding out the old and weak, rousing their courage against the enemy, and teaching them the duty of loving their parents and respecting their elders, something can still be done about the troops. It is the shortage of provisions alone that causes thoughtful men deep anxiety. Someone of old said: “The wealth produced by Heaven and Earth is either with the government or with the people.” Now all unnecessary recipients of public support have been reported for elimination. Indeed, government offices have reduced their offerings to two baskets of grain and practiced economy in every undertaking, going so far as to devise expedients to remedy the situation. Yet the treasuries are already depleted, and although the common people have not been subjected to levies beyond their regular assessments, their resources too are exhausted. Is the claim that wealth must lie either with the government or with the people truly unworthy of belief? Or might there yet be a far-reaching plan to relieve the situation? You gentlemen keenly feel the difficulties of the times and are stirred in your hearts; you have long wished to come forward and set out your plans for ordering the state and aiding its people. Speak of them with animation, holding nothing back!

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
中庸之爲德也其至矣乎
陳鴻漸
同考試官教諭陳批中庸至德取難發揮諸
卷率騁蔓詞此作敷暢精切蓋究心理學者
同考試官教諭唐批發至字義親切懇到可
觀所養矣宜錄以式
考試官教諭井批詞簡而當知中庸之深者
===
考試官教授王批旨瑩辭文
聖人賛中庸之爲至德欲人知所體也夫中庸
之德率諸性者也而爲德之至焉容可以不體
之乎夫子之意若曰天下之德有至有未至而
夫人之於德也有能有不能若中庸也而人可
以不能乎何者德之有過與不及者皆未可以
言至也惟中庸之爲德也維皇之命畀而爲秉
彜之良渾然全具者有以立大中至正之矩恒
性之眞著而爲倫物之顯秩然有常者有以協
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「中庸之爲德也，其至矣乎！」

陳鴻漸

同考試官教諭陳批：「中庸至德取難發揮，諸卷率騁蔓詞。此作敷暢精切，蓋究心理學者。」

同考試官教諭唐批：「發至字義，親切懇到，可觀所養矣。宜錄以式。」

考試官教諭井批：「詞簡而當，知中庸之深者。」

考試官教授王批：「旨瑩辭文。」

聖人賛中庸之爲至德，欲人知所體也。夫中庸之德，率諸性者也，而爲德之至焉，容可以不體之乎？夫子之意若曰：天下之德，有至，有未至；而夫人之於德也，有能，有不能。若中庸也，而人可以不能乎？何者？德之有過與不及者，皆未可以言至也。惟中庸之爲德也，維皇之命畀而爲秉彜之良，渾然全具者，有以立大中至正之矩；恒性之眞著而爲倫物之顯，秩然有常者，有以協
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“The Mean as a virtue—surely it is supreme!”

Chen Hongjian

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The supreme virtue of the Mean is difficult to expound [?]. Most papers indulge in prolix language. This composition develops the subject fluently, precisely, and pertinently. Its author must have devoted himself to the study of principle.”

Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor, comments: “His exposition of the meaning of ‘supreme’ is closely pertinent, earnest, and thorough; it reveals the fruits of his cultivation. This should be recorded as a model.”

Examiner Jing, Instructor, comments: “Concise and apt in expression: the work of one who deeply understands the Mean.”

Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: “Luminous in meaning and elegant in expression.”

The sage praised the Mean as the supreme virtue because he wished people to understand what they should embody. The virtue of the Mean follows our nature and constitutes the highest perfection of virtue. How could we fail to embody it? The Master's meaning was as if to say: Among the virtues under Heaven, some attain perfection and some do not; and in practicing virtue, people succeed in some respects and fail in others. But where the Mean is concerned, can people permit themselves to fail? Why is this? Any virtue marked by excess or deficiency cannot yet be called supreme. Only the Mean qualifies as such a virtue. Bestowed through August Heaven's mandate, it constitutes the goodness of our inherent moral norms: wholly and integrally present, it establishes the standard of perfect centrality and utmost correctness. The truth of our constant nature becomes manifest in human relationships and affairs: ordered and enduring, it serves to accord with…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
至當不易之規易則易知雖未嘗遠人以爲知
也然切近之理而精微寓焉人之所當知者知
乎此而止矣簡而易能雖未嘗遠人以爲行也
然經常之道而神化備焉人之所當行者行乎
此而止矣將以爲過而損之歟是德也幾微之
不足適以虧其本然之體而理本無過也將以
爲不足而益之歟是德也毫末之有加適以累
其本體之全而理本無不及也一人由之而天
下之大經以立蓋不越乎日用之常而所以盡
===
人物兼帝王者在此矣一時脩之而萬世之常
道以明蓋不外乎躬行之實而所以賛化育參
天地者胥此矣中庸之德何如其至也哉吁知
中庸爲德之至則知其不可須臾離矣神而明
之不存乎其人耶抑此堯舜相傳之心法也堯
舜之執中其功在精一夫子之中庸其功在擇
守所謂心一則道一也人能從事於擇守之學
而上接乎精一之傳則至德亦可幾矣孰謂中
庸不可能耶夫子中行之思蓋示人以與能也
punctuated: 至當不易之規。易則易知，雖未嘗遠人以爲知也，然切近之理而精微寓焉，人之所當知者，知乎此而止矣。簡而易能，雖未嘗遠人以爲行也，然經常之道而神化備焉，人之所當行者，行乎此而止矣。將以爲過而損之歟？是德也，幾微之不足，適以虧其本然之體，而理本無過也。將以爲不足而益之歟？是德也，毫末之有加，適以累其本體之全，而理本無不及也。一人由之，而天下之大經以立，蓋不越乎日用之常，而所以盡人物、兼帝王者在此矣。一時脩之，而萬世之常道以明，蓋不外乎躬行之實，而所以賛化育、參天地者胥此矣。中庸之德，何如其至也哉！吁！知中庸爲德之至，則知其不可須臾離矣。神而明之，不存乎其人耶？抑此堯舜相傳之心法也。堯舜之執中，其功在精一；夫子之中庸，其功在擇守。所謂心一則道一也。人能從事於擇守之學，而上接乎精一之傳，則至德亦可幾矣。孰謂中庸不可能耶？夫子中行之思，蓋示人以與能也。
translation_en:
…the standard of utmost appropriateness that admits of no alteration. Being easy, it is readily understood. Though knowing it never requires going beyond what is accessible to people, subtle profundity resides within its familiar principles. All that people ought to know lies in knowing this, and nothing further. Being simple, it is readily practiced. Though practicing it never requires going beyond what is accessible to people, spiritual transformation is fully present within its constant Way. All that people ought to practice lies in practicing this, and nothing further. Would one regard it as excessive and diminish it? In this virtue, even the slightest deficiency would impair its original substance, while its principle inherently contains no excess. Would one regard it as deficient and add to it? In this virtue, even the smallest addition would burden the wholeness of its original substance, while its principle inherently contains no deficiency. When one person follows it, the great guiding norms of the world are established. It does not go beyond the ordinary affairs of daily life, yet herein lies the means to fulfill the natures of people and things and encompass the achievements of emperors and kings. When it is cultivated in one age, the constant Way for myriad generations is illuminated. It does not go beyond actual personal practice, yet herein lie all the means to assist the transforming and nourishing processes and form a triad with Heaven and Earth. How consummate is the virtue of the Mean!

Ah! Once one knows that the Mean is the highest virtue, one knows that it cannot be departed from even for an instant. Does not making it spiritually efficacious and illuminating it depend upon the person? Moreover, this is the teaching of the mind transmitted from Yao to Shun. In Yao and Shun’s holding fast to the Mean, the work lay in refinement and singleness of mind; in the Master’s practice of the Mean, the work lay in choosing the good and holding firmly to it. This is what is meant by saying that when the mind is one, the Way is one. If people can devote themselves to the learning of choosing and holding firmly, and thereby connect with the earlier transmission of refinement and singleness, then the highest virtue, too, can be approached. Who says that the Mean cannot be practiced? The Master’s longing for those who follow the middle course surely shows people that they can take part in practicing it.

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
善學者當自得之
言而民莫不信行而民莫不說
王大道
同考試官教諭張批聖人言行出之以時故能
極其感應之妙此獨能闡揚之無亦涵泳而有得者耶
同考試官教諭宋批信說二字發明殆盡蓋嘗
究心於聖人之化者
考試官教諭井批善釋時出之義
考試官教授王批文有典則
===
聖人之言行而有以得天下之心焉蓋民心未
易得也言行出而民皆信且說之非天下之至
聖其孰能與於此中庸發明天道至此意以聖
人之德其積中也固極天下之至盛而其感民
也尤極天下之至神以言其時出之妙豈惟見
而民莫不敬已哉是故聖人恭己在上固未嘗
必以言而信天下也然施命以誥四方則時乎
發之爲言而所以彰信兆民者於是矣但見議
道自己而民罔不信焉仰聖人之謨訓奉以爲
punctuated:
善學者當自得之。

「言而民莫不信，行而民莫不說。」
王大道

同考試官教諭張批：「聖人言行，出之以時，故能極其感應之妙。此獨能闡揚之，無亦涵泳而有得者耶？」
同考試官教諭宋批：「信說二字，發明殆盡，蓋嘗究心於聖人之化者。」
考試官教諭井批：「善釋時出之義。」
考試官教授王批：「文有典則。」

聖人之言行，而有以得天下之心焉。蓋民心未易得也，言行出而民皆信且說之，非天下之至聖，其孰能與於此？中庸發明天道至此，意以聖人之德，其積中也固極天下之至盛，而其感民也尤極天下之至神。以言其時出之妙，豈惟見而民莫不敬已哉？是故聖人恭己在上，固未嘗必以言而信天下也。然施命以誥四方，則時乎發之爲言，而所以彰信兆民者於是矣。但見議道自己，而民罔不信焉。仰聖人之謨訓，奉以爲
translation_en:
…Those adept at learning should grasp this for themselves.

“When he speaks, none among the people fail to trust him; when he acts, none among the people fail to delight in him.”
Wang Dadao

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The sage brings forth his words and actions at the proper time, and thus realizes to the utmost the subtle workings of influence and response. This essay alone succeeds in elucidating this. Might its author have gained an understanding through sustained immersion in the text?”
Associate Examiner Song, Instructor, comments: “The meanings of ‘trust’ and ‘delight’ are elucidated almost exhaustively. The author has evidently devoted thought to the sage’s transforming influence.”
Examiner Jing, Instructor, comments: “Skillfully explains the meaning of bringing forth words and actions at the proper time.”
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: “The composition possesses classical standards and order.”

Through his words and actions, the sage wins the hearts of all under Heaven. The people’s hearts are not easily won. When his words and actions emerge, the people all trust and delight in him: who but the consummate sage of all under Heaven could attain this? In elucidating the Way of Heaven at this point, the Doctrine of the Mean means that the sage’s virtue, accumulated within, reaches the utmost fullness under Heaven, while its influence upon the people reaches an especially wondrous efficacy. As for the subtlety of its manifestation at the proper time, how could it consist merely in his appearing and none among the people failing to respect him?

Thus, the sage holds himself reverently in his exalted position; he has never needed to rely on words to win the trust of all under Heaven. Yet when he issues commands to proclaim to the four quarters, he gives expression to them in words at the proper time, and thereby makes his trustworthiness manifest to the myriad people. We see only that pronouncements on the Way proceed from him, and none among the people fail to believe them. They look up to the sage’s counsels and instructions, reverently taking them as…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
定保之徵自尊崇而不倍繹皇極之敷言率以
爲辰告之典悉佩服而不違自朝廷以達之天
下皆是彛是訓而莫有疑於巽命之申者矣卽
民心之有同信也不可以見其言之時出也哉
聖人端拱臨民亦未嘗欲以行而說天下也然
建極以錫庶民則時乎見之爲行而所謂說以
先民者在是矣但見自我作則而民莫不說焉
覩經綸之顯設而順於帝則者莫禦其鼓舞之
機式綱紀之敷張而囿於帝力者均動其媚玆
===
之念自邦國以及於四方皆遵道遵路而莫有
外於從乂之風者矣卽民心之有同說也不可
以見其行之時出也哉是則言行各惟其時民
心克協於一聖德之發見當可如此其尊親於
中外而配天也固宜哉噫時出之義大矣元氣
流行四序運而不積以其宰之者至虛也聖人
如天如淵亦至虛矣故其一言一動與四序並
宣蓋顯仁藏用合內外之道也則夫聖人所以
不勞而成治化與天道無心而成歲功者又何
punctuated:
定保之徵，自尊崇而不倍；繹皇極之敷言，率以爲辰告之典，悉佩服而不違。自朝廷以達之天下，皆是彛是訓，而莫有疑於巽命之申者矣。卽民心之有同信也，不可以見其言之時出也哉？
聖人端拱臨民，亦未嘗欲以行而說天下也。然建極以錫庶民，則時乎見之爲行，而所謂說以先民者在是矣。但見自我作則，而民莫不說焉。覩經綸之顯設，而順於帝則者莫禦其鼓舞之機；式綱紀之敷張，而囿於帝力者均動其媚玆之念。自邦國以及於四方，皆遵道遵路，而莫有外於從乂之風者矣。卽民心之有同說也，不可以見其行之時出也哉？
是則言行各惟其時，民心克協於一，聖德之發見當可如此。其尊親於中外而配天也，固宜哉！噫！時出之義大矣！元氣流行，四序運而不積，以其宰之者至虛也。聖人如天如淵，亦至虛矣。故其一言一動，與四序並宣，蓋顯仁藏用，合內外之道也。則夫聖人所以不勞而成治化，與天道無心而成歲功者，又何
translation_en:
…a sign of lasting security, naturally revering them without turning against them. They ponder the comprehensive pronouncements of the august standard, all taking them as authoritative proclamations suited to the time, embracing and observing them without disobedience. From the court throughout all under Heaven, everyone follows these constant norms and these instructions; none doubts the reiterated commands. Does this common trust in the people’s hearts not show that the sage’s words issue at the proper time?
The sage presides over the people with folded hands, and has never sought to delight all under Heaven through his actions. Yet when he establishes the supreme standard and bestows it upon the common people, his actions manifest themselves at the proper time: herein lies what is meant by leading the people through their delight. We see only that he himself sets the example, and none among the people fails to delight in it. Seeing his ordering of affairs clearly established, those who follow the sovereign’s standards cannot resist the impulse that stirs and inspires them. Taking as their model the extension of his governing principles and regulations, those encompassed by the sovereign’s power are alike moved to cherish his rule. From the states to the four quarters, all follow the Way and its paths; none remains outside the prevailing disposition to submit to good government. Does this common delight in the people’s hearts not show that the sage’s actions emerge at the proper time?
Thus words and actions each accord with their proper time, and the people’s hearts can be brought into unity. The manifestation of sagely virtue should indeed be like this. It is surely fitting that he should be revered and cherished both within and beyond the realm, and be Heaven’s equal! Ah, great indeed is the significance of emerging at the proper time! The primordial vital force circulates, and the four seasons revolve without stagnation, because that which governs them is utterly empty. The sage, like Heaven and like a deep pool, is likewise utterly empty. Thus his every word and movement unfolds together with the four seasons. This is the Way that manifests benevolence while concealing its workings, uniting the inner and the outer. How, then, does the sage’s achievement of orderly government and transforming influence without toil differ from Heaven’s Way, which accomplishes the work of the year without conscious intention …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
異哉故曰聖人天道之極致
可欲之謂善有諸己之謂信充實之謂美
充實而有光輝之謂大大而化之之謂
聖聖而不可知之之謂神
鄭日休
同考試官教諭唐批認題真切發義精醇可以
觀養矣宜錄以式多士
同考試官教諭徐批自善信至聖神上下一理
學之有可依據此作得之
===
考試官教諭𠃔批簡而文
考試官教授王批精到
大賢釋善信之義而因究其極焉夫美大聖神
學問之極功也而善信者可以馴致之豈容以
自畫哉孟子以勵樂正子也意曰道之在天下
也進之固有其漸而詣之必有其極試即克之
所造者推之而道之全體可知矣蓋吾心之善
天下之公好也其爲人也惟見其可欲焉是質
之人心而安者必揆之天理而當矣得不謂之
punctuated:
異哉？故曰：「聖人，天道之極致。」

可欲之謂善，有諸己之謂信，充實之謂美，充實而有光輝之謂大，大而化之之謂聖，聖而不可知之之謂神。

鄭日休

同考試官教諭唐批：「認題真切，發義精醇，可以觀養矣。宜錄以式多士。」

同考試官教諭徐批：「自善信至聖神，上下一理，學之有可依據，此作得之。」

考試官教諭𠃔批：「簡而文。」

考試官教授王批：「精到。」

大賢釋善信之義，而因究其極焉。夫美、大、聖、神，學問之極功也，而善信者可以馴致之，豈容以自畫哉？孟子以勵樂正子也，意曰：「道之在天下也，進之固有其漸，而詣之必有其極。試即克之所造者推之，而道之全體可知矣。蓋吾心之善，天下之公好也。其爲人也，惟見其可欲焉，是質之人心而安者，必揆之天理而當矣，得不謂之
translation_en:
…be different? Thus it is said: “The sage is the ultimate realization of the Way of Heaven.”

“What is desirable is called goodness; possessing it in oneself is called authenticity; being filled with it is called beauty; being filled with it and radiating brilliance is called greatness; being great and transforming others is called sagehood; being a sage beyond comprehension is called spiritual profundity.”

Zheng Rixiu

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: “His grasp of the topic is accurate and penetrating, and his exposition of its meaning is refined and pure. One can discern his self-cultivation here. This should be recorded as a model for the many candidates.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “From goodness and authenticity to sagehood and spiritual profundity, a single principle runs through every level, providing a firm basis for learning. This composition grasps that.”

Comment by Examiner Yun [?], Instructor: “Concise and elegant.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “Refined and thorough.”

The great worthy explains the meaning of goodness and authenticity, and thereby explores their ultimate culmination. Beauty, greatness, sagehood, and spiritual profundity are the highest achievements of learning; yet through goodness and authenticity one can gradually attain them. How could one be permitted to set limits on oneself? Mencius used this to encourage Yuezheng Zi. His meaning was: “As for the Way in the world, progress in it certainly has its successive stages, but attainment must have its ultimate culmination. Let us extend our inquiry from what Ke has achieved, and the Way in its entirety can be understood. For the goodness of our minds is what all under Heaven delight in. In such a person, one sees only what is desirable. Thus, what brings assurance when tested against the human mind must prove fitting when measured against Heaven’s principle. How could this fail to be called…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
善乎天下之理不可以偽為也其於善也能實
有諸已焉是反之於身而誠者即求之於心而
慊矣得不謂之信乎由信而進之蘊諸已者擴
充以盡其量則理得於中無待於外和順積而
體無不裕矣夫是之謂美焉由美而進之充於
內者發越以顯其仁則德以日新業以富有光
輝盛而用無不周矣夫是之謂大焉然大而未
化猶有迹也及涵養益深而內外兩忘則渾然
無迹之可見矣此蓋不思不勉從容中道非天
===
下之至聖其孰能與於此哉然未至於聖猶可
知也玆純粹以精而機緘莫測則杳乎無端之
可求矣此蓋無方無體天載同歸非天下之至
神其孰能與於此哉夫德至於神則固妙於聖
而美大不足言矣然亦孰非善信以基之耶大
抵善信非粗迹神化非絕德皆一理以貫之耳
故善者心之粹也理之原也體之為信積之為
美廓之為大化之為聖神一善之極也彼樂克
之無以優入於聖域者豈善信之弊哉弗學故
punctuated: 善乎？天下之理，不可以偽為也。其於善也，能實有諸已焉，是反之於身而誠者，即求之於心而慊矣，得不謂之信乎？由信而進之，蘊諸已者擴充以盡其量，則理得於中，無待於外，和順積而體無不裕矣，夫是之謂美焉。由美而進之，充於內者發越以顯其仁，則德以日新，業以富有，光輝盛而用無不周矣，夫是之謂大焉。然大而未化，猶有迹也；及涵養益深，而內外兩忘，則渾然無迹之可見矣。此蓋不思不勉，從容中道，非天下之至聖，其孰能與於此哉？然未至於聖，猶可知也；玆純粹以精，而機緘莫測，則杳乎無端之可求矣。此蓋無方無體，天載同歸，非天下之至神，其孰能與於此哉？夫德至於神，則固妙於聖，而美大不足言矣。然亦孰非善信以基之耶？大抵善信非粗迹，神化非絕德，皆一理以貫之耳。故善者，心之粹也，理之原也。體之為信，積之為美，廓之為大，化之為聖神，一善之極也。彼樂克之無以優入於聖域者，豈善信之弊哉？弗學故
translation_en: …good? The principles of the world cannot be realized through pretense. When a person truly possesses goodness within himself, what proves sincere upon examining his own conduct also brings satisfaction when sought within his heart. Could this fail to be called genuineness? Advancing from genuineness, he expands what is stored within himself to its fullest measure. Principle is then attained within, without dependence on anything external; harmony and accord accumulate, and his moral substance becomes ample in every respect. This is called beauty. Advancing from beauty, he brings forth what fills him inwardly to manifest his benevolence. His virtue is renewed daily, his accomplishments grow abundant, and his radiance flourishes, leaving nothing beyond the reach of his moral activity. This is called greatness. Yet greatness without transformation still leaves traces. When cultivation deepens further and the distinction between inner and outer is forgotten, there is an integral wholeness with no visible traces. This is surely to accord effortlessly with the Way, without deliberation or exertion. Who but the utmost sage in the world could attain this? Yet before reaching sagehood, one can still be understood. Here, however, purity reaches its finest perfection and the workings are unfathomable: profound and obscure, they offer no starting point for inquiry. This is surely to have neither fixed direction nor form, sharing in the operations of Heaven. Who but one possessing the utmost spiritual efficacy in the world could attain this? When virtue reaches spiritual efficacy, it indeed becomes more wondrous than sagehood, and beauty and greatness no longer suffice to describe it. Yet which of these does not have goodness and genuineness as its foundation? Generally speaking, goodness and genuineness are not merely crude outward traces, nor is spiritual transformation a separate virtue beyond them. A single principle runs through them all. Thus goodness is the purity of the heart and the source of principle. Embodied, it becomes genuineness; accumulated, beauty; expanded, greatness; transformed, sagehood and spiritual efficacy—all are the consummation of this one goodness. As for Yue Ke, was his inability to enter with ease into the realm of sagehood a failing of goodness and genuineness? It was because he did not study…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
也故下學上達其致一也
易
中正以觀天下
鄭日休
同考試官教諭陳批中正爲觀卽與天地貞觀
一理文能認理發揮如此者非佳士乎錄之
同考試官教諭張批知爲觀大體而詞才足以
發之是經術之最優者宜薦
考試官教諭尹批嚴整可式
===
考試官教授王批精到
彖傳舉卦體而著人君建極之道焉夫惟中正
可以同民心而出治道也卦之九五具焉建極
之道得矣此其所以爲天下觀歟彖傳釋觀之
意若曰人君以一身爲天下之觀則必以一身
立天下之極吾嘗於卦體見之矣蓋九五居中
得正則是大觀在上其位至尊矣而有中正以
履之帝範所昭渾乎太極之全體巽而且順其
德至備矣而有中正以出之王猷所著粹然天
punctuated:
也。故下學上達，其致一也。

易
中正以觀天下
鄭日休

同考試官教諭陳批：「中正爲觀，卽與天地貞觀一理。文能認理發揮如此者，非佳士乎？錄之。」
同考試官教諭張批：「知爲觀大體，而詞才足以發之，是經術之最優者，宜薦。」
考試官教諭尹批：「嚴整可式。」
考試官教授王批：「精到。」

彖傳舉卦體而著人君建極之道焉。夫惟中正，可以同民心而出治道也。卦之九五具焉，建極之道得矣。此其所以爲天下觀歟？彖傳釋觀之意，若曰：人君以一身爲天下之觀，則必以一身立天下之極。吾嘗於卦體見之矣。蓋九五居中得正，則是大觀在上，其位至尊矣，而有中正以履之。帝範所昭，渾乎太極之全體。巽而且順，其德至備矣，而有中正以出之。王猷所著，粹然天
translation_en:
…so it is. Thus, learning below and attaining understanding above have one and the same ultimate aim.

Book of Changes
“Through centrality and correctness, serve as a model for all under Heaven.”
Zheng Rixiu

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Serving as a model through centrality and correctness embodies the same principle as Heaven and Earth displaying their constancy. Is someone whose writing can grasp and expound the principle in this way not an outstanding scholar? Accept him.”
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “He understands the essential meaning of serving as a model, and his literary talent suffices to express it. He is among the very best in classical learning and should be recommended.”
Examiner Yin, Instructor, comments: “Rigorous and well ordered; worthy of emulation.”
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: “Refined and penetrating.”

The Commentary on the Judgments presents the structure of the hexagram and makes manifest the way in which the ruler establishes the supreme standard. Only through centrality and correctness can he unite the people's hearts and bring forth the way of good government. The nine in the fifth place possesses these qualities: the way of establishing the supreme standard is thereby attained. Is this not why he serves as a model for all under Heaven? In explaining the meaning of the hexagram Guan, the Commentary on the Judgments seems to say: If the ruler is personally to serve as a model for all under Heaven, he must personally establish the supreme standard for all under Heaven. I have seen this in the structure of the hexagram.

The nine in the fifth place occupies the central position and attains correctness: thus the great model stands above. His position is supremely honored, and he has centrality and correctness with which to occupy it. What the imperial exemplar reveals is the complete substance of the Supreme Ultimate, whole and undivided. Gentle and compliant, his virtue is supremely complete, and he has centrality and correctness through which to express it. What the kingly way makes manifest is the purity of Heaven…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
道之無私將以定天下之趨非徒聲色以化民
也會之精一以執其中而四方之極以建將以
齊天下之政非徒法制以軌衆也先之無爲以
守其正而萬邦之度以貞本諸躬行而陳之藝
極則無過也無不及也天下皆則而象之而民
心之罔中者咸於是乎取中焉根諸心得而樹
之風聲則不偏也不倚也天下皆仰而望之而
民行之不正者咸於是乎表正焉觀政在朝上
之所以爲道揆者此也式是百辟莫不師師而
===
和德矣大觀之道不由之以益光乎觀俗在野
下之所以爲法守者此也錫厥庶民莫不熈熈
而從乂矣下觀之化不由之以益神乎是知聖
人本中正以爲觀則觀者非飾治而觀之者爲
順治也觀之名義不可識乎抑中正帝王平天
下之要道大觀之治莫踰於此故天地貞觀無
私覆載而萬物咸若聖人大觀無私好惡而萬
國咸寧其道同也然必有憲天之心而後有純
王之道是故中正以爲觀也其諸聖人爲天地
punctuated: 道之無私。將以定天下之趨，非徒聲色以化民也，會之精一以執其中，而四方之極以建；將以齊天下之政，非徒法制以軌衆也，先之無爲以守其正，而萬邦之度以貞。本諸躬行而陳之藝極，則無過也，無不及也，天下皆則而象之，而民心之罔中者，咸於是乎取中焉；根諸心得而樹之風聲，則不偏也，不倚也，天下皆仰而望之，而民行之不正者，咸於是乎表正焉。觀政在朝，上之所以爲道揆者此也，式是百辟，莫不師師而和德矣，大觀之道不由之以益光乎？觀俗在野，下之所以爲法守者此也，錫厥庶民，莫不熈熈而從乂矣，下觀之化不由之以益神乎？是知聖人本中正以爲觀，則觀者非飾治，而觀之者爲順治也，觀之名義不可識乎？抑中正，帝王平天下之要道，大觀之治莫踰於此。故天地貞觀，無私覆載，而萬物咸若；聖人大觀，無私好惡，而萬國咸寧，其道同也。然必有憲天之心，而後有純王之道。是故中正以爲觀也，其諸聖人爲天地
translation_en:
…the impartiality of Heaven’s Way. To establish the direction toward which all under Heaven turn, the ruler does not merely transform the people through proclamations and outward displays. He brings things together through refinement and singleness of purpose, holding fast to the mean, and thereby establishes the supreme standard for the four quarters. To bring order to the government of all under Heaven, he does not merely regulate the multitude through laws and institutions. He leads through nonaction, preserving his correctness, and thereby sets firm the standards of the myriad states. Grounding these standards in his own conduct and displaying them as norms, he neither goes too far nor falls short. All under Heaven take him as their rule and pattern, and those among the people whose hearts lack the mean derive it from him. Rooting his influence in what he has apprehended in his heart and establishing it through his moral example and reputation, he inclines neither to one side nor to the other. All under Heaven look up to him, and those among the people whose conduct is incorrect find in him a model by which to rectify themselves.

In observing government at court, this is what enables those above to assess affairs by the Way. He serves as a model for the many lords, who all emulate one another and harmonize their virtue. Does not the Way of the great exemplar thereby become still more radiant? In observing customs among the people, this is what enables those below to uphold established norms. He bestows this upon the common people, who all joyfully submit to good order. Does not the transforming influence of those below looking up to their ruler thereby become still more wondrous? Thus we know that when the sage bases his exemplary role upon centrality and correctness, the exemplar does not merely adorn his government with appearances, while those who look to him become compliant and well governed. Can we not thus understand the name and meaning of Guan—Contemplation?

Moreover, centrality and correctness are the essential Way by which emperors and kings bring peace to all under Heaven; government through the great exemplar cannot surpass this. Thus Heaven and Earth display their constancy, impartially covering and sustaining all things, and the myriad beings flourish in accordance with their natures. The sage serves as the great exemplar, without partiality in his likes and dislikes, and the myriad states are all at peace. Their Way is the same. Yet only with a heart that takes Heaven as its model can there be the Way of pure kingly rule. Thus, in taking centrality and correctness as the basis of his exemplary role, is the sage perhaps, for Heaven and Earth…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
立心乎
以言乎天地之間則備矣夫乾其靜也專
其動也直是以大生焉夫坤其靜也翕
其動也闢是以廣生焉廣大配天地
雷用龍
同考試官教諭張批發明廣大處詞約意該似
能探易於畫前者可以式矣
同考試官教諭陳批詞理簡潔而天地易書之
奥則粲然指諸掌矣佳士佳士
===
考試官教諭𠦢批筆力雅健可取
考試官教授王批純正
大傳論易理察乎天地而因推其與天地準焉
蓋易之廣大察乎天地者也即其所由生而與
之克配也不亦可見哉大傳贊易之廣大如此
蓋曰易之為書其始也因天地而立本其究也
參天地以成能要之一理而已矣今自其廣大
言之豈惟遠邇之各足已哉至言乎天地之間
殆見法象若是乎無際也而陰陽之實理則彌
punctuated:
立心乎？

以言乎天地之間，則備矣。夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉。夫坤，其靜也翕，其動也闢，是以廣生焉。廣大配天地。

雷用龍

同考試官教諭張批：發明廣大處，詞約意該，似能探易於畫前者，可以式矣。

同考試官教諭陳批：詞理簡潔，而天地易書之奥，則粲然指諸掌矣。佳士！佳士！

考試官教諭𠦢批：筆力雅健，可取。

考試官教授王批：純正。

大傳論易理，察乎天地，而因推其與天地準焉。蓋易之廣大，察乎天地者也，即其所由生，而與之克配也，不亦可見哉？大傳贊易之廣大如此，蓋曰：易之為書，其始也因天地而立本，其究也參天地以成能，要之一理而已矣。今自其廣大言之，豈惟遠邇之各足已哉？至言乎天地之間，殆見法象若是乎無際也，而陰陽之實理則彌
translation_en:
…establish a heart for Heaven and Earth?

“Speaking of what lies between Heaven and Earth, it encompasses everything. Qian in its stillness is concentrated; in its movement it is direct. Thus it brings forth greatness. Kun in its stillness draws together; in its movement it opens out. Thus it brings forth breadth. In breadth and greatness, it matches Heaven and Earth.”

Lei Yonglong

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “In elucidating breadth and greatness, his language is concise and his meaning comprehensive. He seems able to explore the Changes before the drawing of the hexagram lines. This can serve as a model.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The language and reasoning are concise and lucid, while the mysteries of Heaven and Earth and of the Book of Changes are displayed as clearly as something pointed out in one’s palm. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!”

Comment by Examiner 𠦢 [?], Instructor: “His writing is elegant and vigorous, worthy of selection.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “Pure and correct.”

The Great Commentary discusses the principles of the Changes, examining them in Heaven and Earth and thereby inferring that the Changes accords with Heaven and Earth. The breadth and greatness of the Changes can indeed be discerned in Heaven and Earth. By considering whence these arise, can we not also see how they fully match Heaven and Earth? Such is the Great Commentary’s praise of the breadth and greatness of the Changes. Its meaning is this: as a book, the Changes initially establishes its foundation upon Heaven and Earth; in its ultimate reach, it forms a triad with Heaven and Earth to fulfill its powers. In essence, there is but one principle.

Now, speaking of its breadth and greatness, is it merely that it adequately embraces both the distant and the near? When we speak of what lies between Heaven and Earth, we see that its patterns and images are thus boundless, while the substantive principles of yin and yang extend throughout…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
漫於六合而不見其有遺感應若是乎無窮也
而變化之眞機則充塞於兩間而莫知其所止
盈天地而皆備其斯以爲廣大乎然易何以若
是其廣大也蓋易體天地之撰而乾坤則易之
縕也自天之至健而言曰乾大莫踰於斯矣而
其大則由乎靜專動直而生也一機相禪統萬
物而無所不知乾之爲大何如耶夫易有乾道
焉此易之所以大也自地之至順而言曰坤廣
莫踰於斯矣而其廣則由乎靜翕動闢而生也
===
二氣互根含萬物而無所不成坤之爲廣何如
耶夫易有坤道焉此易之所以廣也惟其以乾
之大爲大也故極天所覆而易理無不備大有
以配乎天矣至德至敎不其異象而同神乎惟
其以坤之廣爲廣也故極地所載而易理無不
備廣有以配乎地矣開物成物不其異形而同
體乎夫一理顯設於天地而三極彌綸於易書
信乎易之廣大斯其至矣其容以卜筮小之哉
嗟乎萬物皆備天地一體人心何廣大耶而所
punctuated: 漫於六合而不見其有遺，感應若是乎無窮也，而變化之眞機則充塞於兩間而莫知其所止。盈天地而皆備，其斯以爲廣大乎？然易何以若是其廣大也？蓋易體天地之撰，而乾坤則易之縕也。自天之至健而言曰乾，大莫踰於斯矣，而其大則由乎靜專動直而生也。一機相禪，統萬物而無所不知，乾之爲大何如耶？夫易有乾道焉，此易之所以大也。自地之至順而言曰坤，廣莫踰於斯矣，而其廣則由乎靜翕動闢而生也。二氣互根，含萬物而無所不成，坤之爲廣何如耶？夫易有坤道焉，此易之所以廣也。惟其以乾之大爲大也，故極天所覆而易理無不備，大有以配乎天矣。至德至敎，不其異象而同神乎？惟其以坤之廣爲廣也，故極地所載而易理無不備，廣有以配乎地矣。開物成物，不其異形而同體乎？夫一理顯設於天地，而三極彌綸於易書，信乎易之廣大斯其至矣，其容以卜筮小之哉？嗟乎！萬物皆備，天地一體，人心何廣大耶！而所
translation_en:
…pervades the six directions, leaving nothing out. Its stimulus and response are thus inexhaustible, while the true workings of transformation fill the space between Heaven and Earth, and no one knows their limit. Filling Heaven and Earth, with everything fully present—is this what constitutes its breadth and greatness? Yet how does the Changes possess such breadth and greatness? The Changes embodies the workings of Heaven and Earth, and Qian and Kun are its inner substance. Speaking of Heaven’s utmost vigor, we call it Qian: nothing surpasses its greatness. This greatness arises from its being concentrated in stillness and direct in movement. Its single generative impulse operates in succession, governing the myriad things, with none beyond its knowing. How great, then, is Qian! The Changes contains the way of Qian: this is why the Changes is great. Speaking of Earth’s utmost compliance, we call it Kun: nothing surpasses its breadth. This breadth arises from its being gathered in stillness and open in movement. The two vital forces are rooted in one another; it embraces the myriad things and brings all to completion. How broad, then, is Kun! The Changes contains the way of Kun: this is why the Changes is broad.

Precisely because its greatness is the greatness of Qian, the principles of the Changes are fully present throughout everything Heaven covers; in greatness it can thus match Heaven. In their supreme virtue and supreme teaching, do they not differ in manifestation yet share the same spiritual efficacy? Precisely because its breadth is the breadth of Kun, the principles of the Changes are fully present throughout everything Earth bears; in breadth it can thus match Earth. In bringing things forth and completing them, do they not differ in form yet share the same substance? The single principle is manifestly arrayed in Heaven and Earth, while the three ultimates—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—are comprehensively embraced in the book of Changes. Truly, the breadth and greatness of the Changes here reach their utmost! How could one belittle it as merely divination by tortoise shell and milfoil? Ah! The myriad things are all fully present, and Heaven and Earth form one body: how broad and great is the human mind! Yet the means by which…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
以致其廣大則莫要於主靜立極之義焉何者
天以專而直地以翕而闢可知也觀天地見人
心廣大之體觀動靜識人心出入之機故曰易
也者性命之書也
書
惟帝時克益曰都帝德廣運乃聖乃神乃
武乃文
王大道
同考試官敎諭宋批近作將時克句看輕子
獨得旨虞廷君臣都俞氣象宛在心目可敬可敬
===
同考試官敎諭唐批不襲時套不尚浮詞確
然之見泠然之思佳作也
考試官敎諭芉批清潔可愛
考試官敎授王批明淨
聖君以克艱歸前聖而大臣復推本其德之盛
焉蓋克艱必本於盛德也聖神文武廣運之德
著矣非帝堯孰能之哉且夫唐虞之文命已敷
而君臣之交儆惓切舜聞大禹之謨俞而歸諸
punctuated:
以致其廣大，則莫要於主靜立極之義焉。何者？天以專而直，地以翕而闢，可知也。觀天地，見人心廣大之體；觀動靜，識人心出入之機。故曰：「易也者，性命之書也。」

書
「惟帝時克。」益曰：「都！帝德廣運，乃聖乃神，乃武乃文。」
王大道

同考試官敎諭宋批：「近作將時克句看輕，子獨得旨，虞廷君臣都俞氣象，宛在心目，可敬可敬！」
同考試官敎諭唐批：「不襲時套，不尚浮詞，確然之見，泠然之思，佳作也。」
考試官敎諭芉批：「清潔可愛。」
考試官敎授王批：「明淨。」

聖君以克艱歸前聖，而大臣復推本其德之盛焉。蓋克艱必本於盛德也，聖神文武，廣運之德著矣，非帝堯孰能之哉？且夫唐虞之文命已敷，而君臣之交儆惓切。舜聞大禹之謨，俞而歸諸
translation_en:
…as for realizing that breadth and greatness, nothing is more essential than the principle of making stillness primary and establishing the Supreme Ultimate. Why is this? We can understand it from Heaven, which through concentration is direct, and Earth, which through gathering inward opens outward. By observing Heaven and Earth, we perceive the broad and great substance of the human mind; by observing movement and stillness, we discern the incipient workings of the mind’s going out and coming in. Thus it is said: “The Changes is a book of human nature and destiny.”

Book of Documents
“Only the emperor could accomplish this.” Yi said: “Ah! The emperor’s virtue extends broadly and operates far and wide: sagely and spiritually perceptive, martial and cultured.”
Wang Dadao

Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: “Recent essays have treated the phrase ‘could accomplish this’ lightly. You alone have grasped its purport. The atmosphere of ruler and ministers exchanging exclamations of approval at the court of Shun stands vividly before the mind’s eye. Admirable, admirable!”
Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: “It neither copies fashionable formulas nor prizes empty language. Its judgments are firm, its thought lucid. An excellent composition.”
Comment by Examiner Gan 芉 [?], Instructor: “Pure and clean; delightful.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “Clear and lucid.”

The sage ruler credits the earlier sage with overcoming difficulties, and the great minister in turn traces this achievement to the fullness of his virtue. For overcoming difficulties must be rooted in abundant virtue. Sagely, spiritually perceptive, cultured, and martial: his broadly extending and far-reaching virtue was manifest. Who but Emperor Yao could have achieved this?
