Moreover, although the civilizing influence of Yao and Shun had already spread abroad, ruler and ministers remained earnest and heartfelt in their mutual admonitions. When Shun heard the counsels of Yu the Great, he assented and attributed this to…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
帝曰克艱之事豈易能哉惟帝也兢業存心而
保泰之圖能兼體而無遺時幾立政而持盈之
計能各盡而無忝於求言有總章之訪於愛民
有如天之仁於好士有側陋之揚是雖君道之
當然非帝莫能爲也豈他人之可與乎衆論可
延也萬邦可寧也羣賢可致也是雖治道之極
致非帝莫克舉耳又豈予之可及乎然益之心
卽舜之心也嘆而美諸堯曰帝之克艱豈無本
哉蓋中涵萬物之情而全體時出又混闢而不
===
已統會太極之妙而至誠默運且循環之無端
是以從容而聖微妙而神變化非心思之能測
天下不得而知也乾剛而武經緯而文流動非
意象之能拘帝亦不得而知也此其所以能克
艱與吁堯一也舜美之以自勉焉君盡君道也
益誦之以勉君焉臣盡臣道也君臣各盡其道
有虞之治所以不可及歟抑堯之德天德也易
以元亨利貞而獨歸於乾者惟其不息也帝德
廣運此之謂耳故曰惟天爲大惟堯則之雖然
punctuated: 帝，曰：「克艱之事，豈易能哉！惟帝也，兢業存心，而保泰之圖能兼體而無遺；時幾立政，而持盈之計能各盡而無忝。於求言，有總章之訪；於愛民，有如天之仁；於好士，有側陋之揚。是雖君道之當然，非帝莫能爲也，豈他人之可與乎！衆論可延也，萬邦可寧也，羣賢可致也。是雖治道之極致，非帝莫克舉耳，又豈予之可及乎！」然益之心，卽舜之心也。嘆而美諸堯，曰：「帝之克艱，豈無本哉！蓋中涵萬物之情，而全體時出，又混闢而不已；統會太極之妙，而至誠默運，且循環之無端。是以從容而聖，微妙而神，變化非心思之能測，天下不得而知也；乾剛而武，經緯而文，流動非意象之能拘，帝亦不得而知也。此其所以能克艱與！」吁！堯一也，舜美之以自勉焉，君盡君道也；益誦之以勉君焉，臣盡臣道也。君臣各盡其道，有虞之治所以不可及歟！抑堯之德，天德也。《易》以元亨利貞而獨歸於乾者，惟其不息也。帝德廣運，此之謂耳。故曰：「惟天爲大，惟堯則之。」雖然，
translation_en:
…Emperor Yao, saying: “How could overcoming difficulties be easy? Only the Emperor could do it. He maintained vigilance and reverence in his heart, and his plans for preserving peace embraced every aspect without omission. He established government with timely attention to incipient developments, and his measures for sustaining prosperity were each fully realized without failing his responsibilities. In seeking advice, he consulted in the Hall of General Regulations; in loving the people, he showed benevolence like Heaven’s; in valuing worthy men, he raised up those living in obscurity. Although these are the proper duties of a ruler, none but the Emperor could perform them. How could anyone else compare? The opinions of the multitude could be invited, the myriad states brought to peace, and worthy men gathered together. Although these represent the highest attainment in government, none but the Emperor could accomplish them. How could I attain to them?”

Yet Yi’s heart was precisely Shun’s heart. Sighing in admiration of Yao, he said: “Could the Emperor’s ability to overcome difficulties have lacked a foundation? Within, he encompassed the true dispositions of the myriad things, and their complete substance manifested itself in due season, with ceaseless merging and opening [?]. He comprehended and united the subtleties of the Supreme Ultimate, while his utmost sincerity worked silently in an endless cycle. Thus he was a sage in his effortless composure, and spirit-like in his subtlety. His transformations could not be fathomed by thought; none under Heaven could comprehend them. Firm as Heaven, he possessed martial prowess; ordering the world’s warp and weft, he possessed civil refinement. His flowing activity could not be confined by mental images; even the Emperor himself could not comprehend it. Was this not what enabled him to overcome difficulties?”

Ah! Yao was one and the same exemplar. Shun praised him to encourage himself: thus the ruler fulfilled the ruler’s Way. Yi extolled him to encourage his ruler: thus the minister fulfilled the minister’s Way. Ruler and minister each fulfilled his own Way—was this not why the government of Youyu could not be equaled? Moreover, Yao’s virtue was the virtue of Heaven. The Book of Changes attributes origination, success, benefit, and constancy uniquely to Qian, the Creative, because its activity never ceases. This is precisely what is meant by the vast and far-reaching operation of the Emperor’s virtue. Thus it is said: “Heaven alone is great; Yao alone modeled himself upon it.” Nevertheless …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
堯固不自聖也求其心欽而已矣舜不自聖而
歸美之禹益又不以舜爲已聖而交勉之亦卽
堯之心也上下一心此其爲明良之至乎
皇建其有極斂時五福用敷錫厥庶民
□□冕
同考試官教諭唐批規模宏壯意語超脫出
是題正欲得是文耳
同考試官教諭宋批文從理順見由心得本題
福極相須與王者保民之旨發明盡矣又何加焉
===
考試官教諭甘批典雅
考試官教授王批精練
王者立極以獲福而因公其福於民焉蓋極之
所建福之所集也王者之福集於已而錫於民
非建極何以有此箕子衍皇極之疇意謂人君
與天同一道也庶民則君同一心也惟極有不
建則無以獲福於天而錫福於民耳故爲之皇
者必中天地而盡性懋昭清表正之原配乾坤
以立德愼脩樹元良之範綱常倫理定其則焉
punctuated:
堯固不自聖也，求其心，欽而已矣。舜不自聖而歸美之，禹益又不以舜爲已聖而交勉之，亦卽堯之心也。上下一心，此其爲明良之至乎？

皇建其有極，斂時五福，用敷錫厥庶民。
□□冕

同考試官教諭唐批：規模宏壯，意語超脫。出是題，正欲得是文耳。
同考試官教諭宋批：文從理順，見由心得。本題福極相須與王者保民之旨，發明盡矣，又何加焉？

考試官教諭甘批：典雅。
考試官教授王批：精練。

王者立極以獲福，而因公其福於民焉。蓋極之所建，福之所集也。王者之福集於已而錫於民，非建極何以有此？箕子衍皇極之疇，意謂人君與天同一道也，庶民則君同一心也。惟極有不建，則無以獲福於天而錫福於民耳。故爲之皇者，必中天地而盡性，懋昭清表正之原，配乾坤以立德，愼脩樹元良之範。綱常倫理，定其則焉，
translation_en:
…Yao certainly did not regard himself as a sage. If we seek what lay in his heart, it was reverence alone. Shun did not regard himself as a sage but attributed excellence to Yao; Yu and Yi, in turn, did not consider Shun already a perfected sage, but joined in encouraging him. This, too, was precisely Yao’s intention. With those above and below united in purpose, was this not the utmost realization of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers?

“The sovereign establishes his supreme standard, gathers these five blessings, and thereby distributes them widely among his common people.”
□□ Mian [name partly illegible]

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: “Grand and imposing in scope, with ideas and language that rise above the ordinary. In setting this topic, precisely such an essay was sought.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: “The writing flows naturally and the reasoning is coherent; its insights come from personal understanding. The topic’s meaning—the mutual dependence of blessings and the supreme standard, and the king’s duty to protect the people—is fully elucidated. What more could be added?”

Comment by Examiner Gan, Instructor: “Classical and elegant.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “Refined and concise.”

The king establishes the supreme standard to obtain blessings and consequently shares those blessings with the people. For where the standard is established, blessings gather. The king’s blessings gather upon himself and are bestowed upon the people: without establishing the standard, how could this come about? When Jizi elaborated the category of the Sovereign’s Supreme Standard, his meaning was that the ruler shares one Way with Heaven, while the common people model themselves upon the ruler and share one purpose with him. Only when the standard is not established is there no means of obtaining blessings from Heaven and bestowing blessings upon the people. Thus, whoever acts as sovereign must embody the centrality of Heaven and Earth and fully realize his nature, diligently manifesting the pure source of exemplary rectitude [?]; he must match Heaven and Earth in establishing virtue, carefully cultivating himself and setting a model of supreme goodness. For the fundamental bonds, enduring norms, and ethical relationships, he establishes their standards…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
而天下之人紀脩矣言動事物循其理焉而萬
國之儀刑定矣是自盡其爲皇之義初無心於
五福之集也然極者大順之理順以召順而福
履自臻極者太和之道和以感和而繁祉自錫
福壽康寧莫不備至原其所感若招之而來也
好德永命於玆純祐揆其所致若斂之而集也
天之所以厚君者至矣天旣以是厚乎君君可
不以是厚乎民哉又必化導盡其術使會極均
而大順之福亦均焉裁成盡其方使歸極同而
===
太和之福亦同焉雖民自有極民自趨之而惟
大君之成能然後有百姓之與能極非君錫而
誰錫耶雖民自有福民自斂之而有大觀之神
然後有下觀之化福非君與而誰與耶吁建極
而福斂天之心通於君也斂福而敷錫君之心
通於民也王者之責如此君其以是取法也哉
抑一人之極莫非天下之極天下之福皆爲一
人之福故祿位名壽畢集於執中之舜而當時
之民風動爲休此福之所以爲大也建極敷錫
punctuated: 而天下之人紀脩矣。言動事物循其理焉，而萬國之儀刑定矣。是自盡其爲皇之義，初無心於五福之集也。然極者，大順之理；順以召順，而福履自臻。極者，太和之道；和以感和，而繁祉自錫。福壽康寧，莫不備至；原其所感，若招之而來也。好德永命，於玆純祐；揆其所致，若斂之而集也。天之所以厚君者至矣！天旣以是厚乎君，君可不以是厚乎民哉？又必化導盡其術，使會極均，而大順之福亦均焉；裁成盡其方，使歸極同，而太和之福亦同焉。雖民自有極，民自趨之，而惟大君之成能，然後有百姓之與能，極非君錫而誰錫耶？雖民自有福，民自斂之，而有大觀之神，然後有下觀之化，福非君與而誰與耶？吁！建極而福斂，天之心通於君也；斂福而敷錫，君之心通於民也。王者之責如此，君其以是取法也哉！抑一人之極，莫非天下之極；天下之福，皆爲一人之福。故祿位名壽畢集於執中之舜，而當時之民風動爲休，此福之所以爲大也。建極敷錫
translation_en:
…and the bonds of human relations throughout the realm are cultivated. Words and actions, affairs and things all follow their proper principles, and the exemplary standards of the myriad states are established. This is simply to fulfill one’s duty as sovereign, with no initial thought of gathering the Five Blessings. Yet the supreme standard embodies the principle of perfect accord: accord summons accord, and blessings arrive of themselves. The supreme standard embodies the Way of great harmony: harmony evokes harmony, and abundant blessings are bestowed of themselves. Blessings, longevity, health, and peace all arrive in full measure. Tracing what calls them forth, it is as though they had been summoned and had come. Love of virtue and enduring life receive Heaven’s abundant aid in this; considering how they are brought about, it is as though they had been gathered and had assembled. Heaven’s generosity toward the ruler is utmost! Since Heaven thus treats the ruler generously, can the ruler fail to treat the people with the same generosity?

He must also employ to the fullest the arts of moral transformation and guidance, enabling all equally to converge upon the supreme standard, so that the blessings of perfect accord are likewise shared equally. He must fully employ the means of shaping and perfecting them, enabling all alike to return to the supreme standard, so that the blessings of great harmony are likewise shared by all. Although the people possess the supreme standard within themselves and move toward it themselves, only when the great ruler fully realizes his capacity can the common people share in that capacity. If it is not the ruler who bestows the supreme standard, who does? Although the people possess blessings of their own and gather them themselves, only through the spiritual efficacy of the great exemplar above can those who look up from below be transformed. If it is not the ruler who grants blessings, who does?

Ah! When the supreme standard is established and blessings gather, Heaven’s heart communicates with the ruler. When blessings are gathered and widely bestowed, the ruler’s heart communicates with the people. Such is the responsibility of a true king. Should the ruler not take this as his model? Moreover, the supreme standard of the One Man, the sovereign, is nothing other than the supreme standard of all under Heaven; the blessings of all under Heaven are all the blessings of the One Man. Thus emolument, rank, renown, and longevity all gathered around Shun, who held fast to the Mean, while the people of his time were moved as by the wind and became good. This is what makes these blessings great. The words concerning establishing the supreme standard and widely bestowing blessings…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
之言不有得於執中風動之旨乎
詩
君子萬年福祿綏之
陳鴻漸
同考試官敎諭徐批格調莊重詞意淸婉得
詩人忠愛之旨宜錄以式多士
同考試官敎授王批理明詞暢講福祿處有
久安長治氣象得祝頌之體
考試官敎諭ヰ批涵蓄有味
===
考試官敎授王批順暢
周臣之祝君必願以久安之慶焉夫福祿永綏
君之大慶也周臣祝君以之忠愛寧有旣乎此
諸侯所以答桑扈也若曰人君之得天也固以
福祿爲備尤以悠久爲極我之所願於君者果
何如哉今夫運撫盈成而端居五位之崇業隆
熈洽而玉食萬方之貢福祿旣綏之矣然豈特
自今爲然哉其必備天地中和之至而於萬斯
年長享安貞之吉適造化貞元之合而萬有千
punctuated:
之言，不有得於執中風動之旨乎？

詩
君子萬年，福祿綏之。
陳鴻漸

同考試官敎諭徐批：格調莊重，詞意淸婉，得詩人忠愛之旨，宜錄以式多士。
同考試官敎授王批：理明詞暢，講福祿處，有久安長治氣象，得祝頌之體。
考試官敎諭ヰ批：涵蓄有味。
考試官敎授王批：順暢。

周臣之祝君，必願以久安之慶焉。夫福祿永綏，君之大慶也。周臣祝君以之，忠愛寧有旣乎？此諸侯所以答《桑扈》也。若曰：人君之得天也，固以福祿爲備，尤以悠久爲極。我之所願於君者，果何如哉？今夫運撫盈成，而端居五位之崇；業隆熈洽，而玉食萬方之貢。福祿旣綏之矣，然豈特自今爲然哉？其必備天地中和之至，而於萬斯年長享安貞之吉；適造化貞元之合，而萬有千
translation_en:
…do not these words grasp the import of holding fast to the mean and transforming the people as wind moves them?

Book of Odes
“May the lord live ten thousand years; may blessings and emoluments bring him peace.”
Chen Hongjian

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “The style is dignified and the expression and sense are limpid and graceful. It captures the poet’s loyal affection. It should be selected to serve as a model for the candidates.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Professor: “The reasoning is clear and the language fluent. The discussion of blessings and emoluments conveys a vision of enduring peace and lasting good government, fitting the form of a benediction.”
Comment by Examiner ヰ [?], Instructor: “Rich in implication and savor.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “Smooth and fluent.”

When the ministers of Zhou blessed their ruler, they invariably wished him the felicity of enduring peace. For blessings and emoluments that forever bring repose are a ruler’s great felicity. When Zhou’s ministers blessed their ruler with these, could their loyal affection ever be exhausted? This is why the feudal lords responded to “Sanghu” in this way. It is as though they said: A ruler’s receipt of Heaven’s favor is indeed made complete by blessings and emoluments, but its highest fulfillment lies above all in their enduring perpetuity. What, then, is it that we wish for our ruler?

Now, presiding over an age of fullness and accomplishment, he occupies with dignity the exalted fifth position, the sovereign’s seat. His achievements have brought abundant prosperity and harmony, and he enjoys precious fare from the tribute of all regions. Blessings and emoluments have already brought him peace. Yet how could this be true only of the present? Surely he must embody the utmost equilibrium and harmony of Heaven and Earth, and for ten thousand years continually enjoy the good fortune of repose and steadfastness; accord with the conjunction of completion and renewal in the workings of creation, and for ten thousand and a thousand…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
歲永膺保定之祥不但萬福之攸同而已也以
天命則常凝焉以人心則常附焉保豐泰於日
中而萬世太平之業蓋有合帝王之全曆而不
可以限量者矣不但百祿之是荷而已也以中
國則奠安焉以四夷則賓服焉繼離明於天下
而萬年無疆之休蓋有歷天地之全數而無有
乎紀極者矣雖曰吾君之福自天命之然君道
不息則福履之綏亦不息天之所以安全之者
將萬年如一日也則夫藉屏翰之寄者豈獨今
===
日之承其休哉雖曰吾君之祿自天申之然君
德有常則後祿之綏亦有常天之所以底定之
者將萬世所永賴也則夫蒙樂胥之燕者豈直
于今之與有榮哉夫如是則君之所以得天者
始全臣之所以願君者始慰矣詩人之忠愛亦
何至哉雖然德以基福人以合天此理之不可
誣者彼獨言福祿而不及所以綏之者何哉蓋
人臣之進言無樂乎費辭而明良之交則有不
言而信者先儒謂下之祝上不敢擬議其德者
punctuated: 歲，永膺保定之祥，不但萬福之攸同而已也。以天命則常凝焉，以人心則常附焉，保豐泰於日中，而萬世太平之業，蓋有合帝王之全曆而不可以限量者矣。不但百祿之是荷而已也。以中國則奠安焉，以四夷則賓服焉，繼離明於天下，而萬年無疆之休，蓋有歷天地之全數而無有乎紀極者矣。雖曰吾君之福自天命之，然君道不息，則福履之綏亦不息。天之所以安全之者，將萬年如一日也。則夫藉屏翰之寄者，豈獨今日之承其休哉？雖曰吾君之祿自天申之，然君德有常，則後祿之綏亦有常。天之所以底定之者，將萬世所永賴也。則夫蒙樂胥之燕者，豈直于今之與有榮哉？夫如是，則君之所以得天者始全，臣之所以願君者始慰矣。詩人之忠愛，亦何至哉！雖然，德以基福，人以合天，此理之不可誣者。彼獨言福祿而不及所以綏之者，何哉？蓋人臣之進言，無樂乎費辭，而明良之交，則有不言而信者。先儒謂下之祝上不敢擬議其德者，
translation_en:
…years, forever receiving the auspicious blessings of protection and stability. This is more than merely being the gathering place of myriad blessings. Heaven’s mandate will remain firmly established; the people’s hearts will remain attached to him. Preserving abundance and peace at their noonday height, his achievement of peace for ten thousand generations will encompass the entire span of emperors and kings and admit of no measure. Nor is this merely bearing a hundred forms of good fortune. The central realm will be settled in peace, and the peoples of the four quarters will submit as guests. Perpetuating radiant brightness throughout the world, his boundless glory for ten thousand years will extend through the full allotted span of Heaven and Earth, without limit or end.

Though we say that our ruler’s blessings are bestowed by Heaven, if his practice of the ruler’s Way never ceases, neither will the blessings that bring him well-being. Heaven will keep him safe for ten thousand years as consistently as for a single day. Could those entrusted with serving as his protective bulwarks enjoy his beneficence only today? Though we say that our ruler’s good fortune is repeatedly granted by Heaven, if his virtue remains constant, so too will the assurance of good fortune to come. The stability Heaven grants him will be something upon which ten thousand generations may forever depend. Could those favored with his joyous banquet share in his glory only now? Only thus will the ruler’s attainment of Heaven’s favor be complete, and only thus will his ministers’ wishes for him be fulfilled. How profound is the poet’s loyal affection!

Yet virtue is the foundation of blessings, and human conduct brings accord with Heaven: this is a principle that cannot be denied. Why, then, does the poet speak only of blessings and good fortune without addressing how they are secured? Ministers, when offering counsel, take no pleasure in multiplying words; and between an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers there is a trust that needs no words. Earlier Confucian scholars said that when those below offer blessings to those above, their not daring to assess and discuss the ruler’s virtue…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
敬之至也此其得祝君之體歟
鳳凰于飛翽翽其羽亦集爰止藹藹王多
吉士維君子使媚于天子鳳凰于飛翽
翽其羽亦傅于天藹藹王多吉人維君
子命媚于庶人鳳凰鳴矣于彼高岡梧
桐生矣于彼朝陽菶菶萋萋雝雝喈喈
黃如金
同考試官教諭徐批發出賢才願忠之意甚切
至君臣感遇處詞不煩而意獨至蓋深於詩者也佳士佳士
===
同考試官教授王批召公告君求賢與比意
甚婉此作得之蓋長於諷諭者錄之
考試官教諭甘批冲融古雅
考試官教授王批得體
大臣爾興賢才效用之忠而因喻相感之機焉
蓋賢才以效用爲忠而所以感之者則在上也
圖治者無亦是務乎此召公告成王意也若曰
吾君建極於一人而錫極於天下其得賢之益
彰彰矣亦知賢才之忠於所用而不偶於所遇
punctuated:
敬之至也，此其得祝君之體歟？

「鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦集爰止。藹藹王多吉士，維君子使，媚于天子。鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦傅于天。藹藹王多吉人，維君子命，媚于庶人。鳳凰鳴矣，于彼高岡；梧桐生矣，于彼朝陽。菶菶萋萋，雝雝喈喈。」
黃如金

同考試官教諭徐批：發出賢才願忠之意甚切，至君臣感遇處，詞不煩而意獨至，蓋深於詩者也。佳士！佳士！
同考試官教授王批：召公告君求賢與比，意甚婉，此作得之，蓋長於諷諭者，錄之。
考試官教諭甘批：冲融古雅。
考試官教授王批：得體。

大臣爾興賢才效用之忠，而因喻相感之機焉。蓋賢才以效用爲忠，而所以感之者則在上也。圖治者，無亦是務乎？此召公告成王意也。若曰：吾君建極於一人，而錫極於天下，其得賢之益彰彰矣。亦知賢才之忠於所用，而不偶於所遇
translation_en:
…is the utmost reverence. Does this not exemplify the proper manner of offering blessings to one's ruler?

“The phoenixes fly, their wings rustling; they gather where they alight. In abundant numbers the king has worthy officers: the lord employs them, and they show their devotion to the Son of Heaven. The phoenixes fly, their wings rustling; they rise to heaven. In abundant numbers the king has worthy men: the lord commissions them, and they show their love for the common people. The phoenixes call upon that high ridge; the wutong trees grow on its sunward slope. Luxuriant and flourishing are the trees; harmonious and melodious are the calls.”
Huang Rujin

Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “The essay brings out most earnestly the worthy men's desire to serve loyally. Where it treats the mutual responsiveness of ruler and ministers, its language is concise yet its meaning exceptionally profound. This is surely someone with a deep understanding of the Odes. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!”
Associate Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: “The Duke of Shao's exhortation to his ruler to seek worthy men and associate with them [?] is most tactful in its intent. This essay captures that quality. Its author excels at indirect admonition. Accept it.”
Examiner Gan, Instructor, comments: “Harmonious and expansive, antique and elegant.”
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: “Appropriate in form and manner.”

The great minister evokes [?] the loyalty with which worthy men offer their service, and thereby explains the workings of mutual responsiveness. Worthy men indeed express their loyalty through service, but it is the ruler above who must inspire them. Should not those who seek good government devote themselves to this? Such was the intent of the Duke of Shao's admonition to King Cheng. It is as though he said: Our ruler establishes the supreme standard in his own person and bestows it upon all under Heaven. The benefits he gains from obtaining worthy men are abundantly clear. Does he also understand that worthy men are loyal in the service to which they are appointed, yet may not find a fitting reception …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
者哉彼鳳凰之振羽而飛也旣集所止矣況此
藹藹之吉士也寧無致主之忠乎玆惟君子使
之以夾輔王室焉則凡左右賛襄以盡其愛戴
之忱者有不容已矣而敢負吾君也哉鳳凰之
振羽而飛也旣傅于天矣況此藹藹之吉人也
寧無庇民之益乎玆惟君子命之以保釐四方
焉則凡經綸康濟以普其輯和之澤者有不容
已矣而忍負吾民也哉然此特臣之忠於事耳
抑孰非君之妙於感乎蓋鳳凰不徒鳴也于彼
===
高岡梧桐不徒生也于彼朝陽則有擇而處有
待而生固相須之甚殷者矣然必梧桐之生也
蓁萋極其盛而後鳳凰之鳴也雝喈宣其和則
所以招徠所以響應若相遇之有機者矣然則
明良之相會於治朝其高岡之鳳凰朝陽之梧
桐乎賢才之樂用於明君其梧桐生之盛而後
鳳凰鳴之和乎故觀於鳳凰則賢才之有所托
而止焉者可知也觀於梧桐則人君之有所禮
而致焉者可知也君其念哉噫老成告君其相
punctuated: 者哉？彼鳳凰之振羽而飛也，旣集所止矣，況此藹藹之吉士也，寧無致主之忠乎？玆惟君子使之以夾輔王室焉，則凡左右賛襄以盡其愛戴之忱者，有不容已矣，而敢負吾君也哉？鳳凰之振羽而飛也，旣傅于天矣，況此藹藹之吉人也，寧無庇民之益乎？玆惟君子命之以保釐四方焉，則凡經綸康濟以普其輯和之澤者，有不容已矣，而忍負吾民也哉？然此特臣之忠於事耳，抑孰非君之妙於感乎？蓋鳳凰不徒鳴也，于彼高岡；梧桐不徒生也，于彼朝陽。則有擇而處，有待而生，固相須之甚殷者矣。然必梧桐之生也，蓁萋極其盛，而後鳳凰之鳴也，雝喈宣其和，則所以招徠、所以響應，若相遇之有機者矣。然則明良之相會於治朝，其高岡之鳳凰、朝陽之梧桐乎？賢才之樂用於明君，其梧桐生之盛而後鳳凰鳴之和乎？故觀於鳳凰，則賢才之有所托而止焉者可知也；觀於梧桐，則人君之有所禮而致焉者可知也。君其念哉！噫！老成告君，其相
translation_en:
…is this understood? When those phoenixes spread their wings and fly, they have already found a place to alight. How much more, then, must this abundant company of worthy men possess the loyalty that brings their ruler to greatness? If the sovereign employs them to assist the royal house, they cannot restrain themselves from offering aid on every side, fully expressing their heartfelt love and devotion. Would they dare fail their ruler? When the phoenixes spread their wings and fly, they have already reached the heavens. How much more, then, must this abundant company of worthy men bring benefits that shelter the people? If the sovereign commands them to preserve order throughout the realm, they cannot restrain themselves from ordering affairs and bringing peace and relief, extending everywhere the blessings of concord. Could they bear to fail their people?

Yet this is merely the minister’s loyalty in service. Is it not all also the ruler’s subtle skill in moving others to respond? For the phoenix does not cry just anywhere: it cries upon that high ridge. The wutong tree does not grow just anywhere: it grows upon that slope facing the morning sun. Thus one chooses where to dwell, and the other awaits the right conditions to grow: their mutual dependence is indeed profound. Yet only when the wutong grows in the fullest luxuriance does the phoenix give voice to its harmonious cries. What draws it forth and what responds seem to depend upon a timely conjunction.

Thus, when an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers meet in a well-governed court, are they not like the phoenix upon the high ridge and the wutong facing the morning sun? When worthy and talented men delight in serving an enlightened ruler, is this not like the phoenix sounding its harmonious cries only after the wutong has grown luxuriantly? Therefore, by observing the phoenix, we can understand that worthy and talented men settle where they can entrust themselves; by observing the wutong, we can understand that a ruler attracts such men by treating them with ritual respect. May the ruler ponder this! Ah! When seasoned elders counsel their ruler, their mutual…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
與有成者類此雖然人臣忠義天植其性無所
待而興者也若必視所以禮之者非性忠義者
也召公得無過計乎蓋賢者難進易退所以長
養而汲引之者大臣事也此即周公吐哺握髮
之風而亦大臣以人事君之義
春秋
冬十有二月會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯
許男滑伯滕子同盟于幽〔莊公十有六年〕
===
同考試官教諭王批此作知聖人予奪書法無
非衛世道以尊王意宜錄以式
同考試官教諭朱批發明罪魯與諸侯而予
伯之意昭然
考試官教諭毋批雄渾峻潔
考試官教授王批得旨謹嚴
經於霸信諱內之疑而志外之協焉此于幽之
盟齊桓仗義以圖霸也而諸侯有從違焉春秋
banxin: 鄉試錄 四十四 周良賓
punctuated:
與有成者類此。雖然，人臣忠義，天植其性，無所待而興者也。若必視所以禮之者，非性忠義者也。召公得無過計乎？蓋賢者難進易退，所以長養而汲引之者，大臣事也。此即周公吐哺握髮之風，而亦大臣以人事君之義。

春秋
冬十有二月，會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、滑伯、滕子，同盟于幽。〔莊公十有六年〕

同考試官教諭王批：此作知聖人予奪書法，無非衛世道以尊王意，宜錄以式。
同考試官教諭朱批：發明罪魯與諸侯而予伯之意昭然。
考試官教諭毋批：雄渾峻潔。
考試官教授王批：得旨謹嚴。

經於霸信，諱內之疑，而志外之協焉。此于幽之盟，齊桓仗義以圖霸也，而諸侯有從違焉。春秋
translation_en:
…such are the ways in which they help their ruler achieve success. Nevertheless, loyalty and righteousness in a minister are implanted in his nature by Heaven and arise without awaiting anything external. If he must first consider the courtesy shown him, his loyalty and righteousness are not innate. Was the Duke of Shao not being overly calculating? Worthy men, however, are reluctant to enter service and quick to withdraw; nurturing and drawing them into service is the duty of great ministers. This is precisely the spirit of the Duke of Zhou, who spat out his food or gathered up his unbound hair to receive worthy men, and likewise accords with the principle that great ministers serve their ruler by bringing him men of worth.

Spring and Autumn Annals
“In winter, in the twelfth month, [the Duke] met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Hua, and the Viscount of Teng; they jointly covenanted at You.” 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “This composition understands that the Sage’s manner of writing, in granting approval or withholding it, invariably aims to safeguard the moral order and honor the king. It should be included as a model.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “It clearly elucidates the intention to condemn Lu and the other feudal lords while approving the hegemon.”
Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: “Powerful and ample, lofty and pure.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “It grasps the purport and is careful and rigorous.”

In treating the credibility of the hegemon, the Classic conceals the doubts within our own state while recording the concord of the other states. At this covenant at You, Duke Huan of Qi relied on righteousness in seeking hegemony, yet among the feudal lords some followed him and others did not. The Spring and Autumn Annals…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
所以深致意歟昔者齊霸而以尊周為名鄭成
而有盟幽之舉桓為是以合諸侯也我公甞在
列矣經不書公者何君子曰惡失信也蓋自于
柯以來齊魯言歸于好矣使莊而能堅齊之從
失信之愆誰得而議之今是盟也衆從而我獨
違焉雖逋逃之受尚在于討詹之日而其與桓
異同謂非始于今日之盟不可也噫維時協謀
推戴宜桓之盟可與矣矧我魯人望之國而乃
首貳此盟易食易生之重於齊受盟而若罔聞
===
也則信義之崇其亦奚取乎聖人以為桓之圖
霸雖非一魯所能撓而魯之失信則固於桓為
自外矣故諱不書公使若公未與盟者然所以
諱內之疑也夫然則魯不能無異矣而又書同
盟者何君子曰志同欲也蓋自北杏以來人心
歸齊有日矣使諸侯而亦如魯之貳桓霸之義
孰從而成之今是盟也一人倡而天下應焉雖
諸侯之授尚在于再盟之時而其與桓同志謂
非肇于今日之盟不可也噫以魯方信忽疑似
punctuated:
所以深致意歟！昔者齊霸而以尊周為名，鄭成而有盟幽之舉，桓為是以合諸侯也。我公甞在列矣。經不書公者何？君子曰：「惡失信也。」蓋自于柯以來，齊魯言歸于好矣。使莊而能堅齊之從，失信之愆誰得而議之？今是盟也，衆從而我獨違焉。雖逋逃之受尚在于討詹之日，而其與桓異同，謂非始于今日之盟不可也。噫！維時協謀推戴，宜桓之盟可與矣。矧我魯，人望之國，而乃首貳此盟。易食易生之重，於齊受盟而若罔聞也，則信義之崇，其亦奚取乎？聖人以為桓之圖霸，雖非一魯所能撓，而魯之失信，則固於桓為自外矣。故諱不書公，使若公未與盟者然，所以諱內之疑也。
夫然則魯不能無異矣，而又書同盟者何？君子曰：「志同欲也。」蓋自北杏以來，人心歸齊有日矣。使諸侯而亦如魯之貳桓，霸之義孰從而成之？今是盟也，一人倡而天下應焉。雖諸侯之授尚在于再盟之時，而其與桓同志，謂非肇于今日之盟不可也。噫！以魯方信忽疑，似
translation_en:
…is this why the Spring and Autumn Annals gives the matter such particular attention? Formerly, Qi pursued hegemony in the name of honoring Zhou. When Zheng made peace, the covenant at You followed: Duke Huan used it to unite the regional lords. Our duke was once among their ranks. Why, then, does the Classic not record him? The gentleman says: “It condemns his breach of faith.” Since the meeting at Ke, Qi and Lu had returned to friendly relations. Had Duke Zhuang remained steadfast in following Qi, who could have charged him with breaking faith? At this covenant, however, the others followed, while we alone departed from that course. Although the harboring of a fugitive came only later, when the surrender of Zhan was demanded, one cannot deny that Lu’s divergence from Duke Huan began with this very covenant. Alas! At a time when the lords joined in deliberation and upheld his leadership, Duke Huan’s covenant surely deserved participation. Moreover, our Lu was a state to which others looked, yet it was the first to waver in its commitment to this covenant. Despite the gravity of “changing food and changing life” [?], it received the covenant from Qi as though it had heard nothing. What claim, then, could it have to esteem for good faith and righteousness? The Sage considered that, although Lu alone could not thwart Duke Huan’s pursuit of hegemony, Lu’s breach of faith certainly placed it outside his fellowship. He therefore concealed the matter by omitting the duke, making it appear that the duke had not participated in the covenant. This is how he concealed the wavering of his own state.
If so, Lu could not be free of dissent. Why, then, does the text also record a “joint covenant”? The gentleman says: “It records their common purpose.” Since the meeting at Beixing, people’s hearts had long been turning toward Qi. Had the regional lords also wavered toward Duke Huan as Lu did, through whose support could the righteous undertaking of hegemony have been accomplished? At this covenant, one man took the lead and all under Heaven responded. Although the regional lords’ bestowal [of authority?] came only at the renewed covenant, one cannot deny that their shared purpose with Duke Huan originated in this very covenant. Alas! With Lu suddenly turning from trust to doubt, it seemed…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
桓之從難必矣矧列國交爭之際而能共爲此
盟曰安曰攘之同自魯之外而無有二也則尊
奬之協其不有賴乎聖人以爲霸業垂就雖由
於桓之自振而眾志允孚實賴夫諸侯之多助
矣故特書同盟使若合異爲同者然所以志外
之協也噫諱內貳則背霸者在所非志外協則
從霸者在所予春秋之作何莫而非爲世道計
乎雖然桓非受命之霸也而春秋予之又欲諸
侯之從之也則王室將不足慮乎噫此正春秋
===
所以爲王室慮也桓雖未命於王然亦有功於
王室者觀首止歃而王儲定葵丘合而王禁明
他凡爲王室謀者蓋皆自兩幽之盟始之春秋
於此而予諸侯且諱魯公之失信也乃聖人不
得已而予桓也不然平丘之役亦霸者事也何
旣罪諸侯之同又以魯不與盟爲幸耶故於是
而知春秋之予桓爲世道慮亦猶爲王道慮也
晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕夏曹公孫會
自鄸出奔宋〔昭公二十年〕
punctuated:
桓之從難必矣。矧列國交爭之際，而能共爲此盟，曰安曰攘之同，自魯之外而無有二也，則尊奬之協，其不有賴乎？聖人以爲霸業垂就，雖由於桓之自振，而眾志允孚，實賴夫諸侯之多助矣。故特書同盟，使若合異爲同者然，所以志外之協也。噫！諱內貳，則背霸者在所非；志外協，則從霸者在所予。《春秋》之作，何莫而非爲世道計乎？雖然，桓非受命之霸也，而《春秋》予之，又欲諸侯之從之也，則王室將不足慮乎？噫！此正《春秋》所以爲王室慮也。桓雖未命於王，然亦有功於王室者。觀首止歃而王儲定，葵丘合而王禁明，他凡爲王室謀者，蓋皆自兩幽之盟始之。《春秋》於此而予諸侯，且諱魯公之失信也，乃聖人不得已而予桓也。不然，平丘之役，亦霸者事也，何旣罪諸侯之同，又以魯不與盟爲幸耶？故於是而知《春秋》之予桓，爲世道慮，亦猶爲王道慮也。
晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕。夏，曹公孫會自鄸出奔宋〔昭公二十年〕。
translation_en:
…whether Lu would follow Duke Huan was difficult to be certain. Moreover, at a time when the various states contended with one another, they were able to join together in this covenant. In their shared purpose of bringing peace and repelling threats, none apart from Lu was of two minds. Did not their cooperation in honoring and supporting the royal house provide essential support? The Sage considered that, although the near accomplishment of the hegemonic enterprise arose from Huan’s own exertions, the genuine concord of the assembled rulers’ intentions depended indeed upon the considerable assistance of the regional lords. Thus he specifically wrote “covenanted together,” presenting them as though they had united their differences into agreement, thereby recording the cooperation of the states outside Lu. Ah! Concealing disloyalty within Lu condemns those who turn against the hegemon; recording cooperation outside Lu approves those who follow him. What part of the composition of the Spring and Autumn Annals was not intended for the sake of order in the world?
Even so, Huan was not a hegemon commissioned by the king. If the Spring and Autumn Annals approves him and also wishes the regional lords to follow him, should this not give cause for concern about the royal house? Ah! This is precisely how the Spring and Autumn Annals expresses its concern for the royal house. Although Huan had not been commissioned by the king, he nevertheless rendered service to the royal house. Consider how the blood oath at Shouzhi secured the royal heir’s position, and how the assembly at Kuiqiu made the royal prohibitions clear. These and all his other undertakings on behalf of the royal house began with the two covenants at You. That the Spring and Autumn Annals here approves the regional lords and also conceals the Duke of Lu’s breach of faith means that the Sage had no choice but to approve Huan. Otherwise, the gathering at Pingqiu was also the work of a hegemon: why, in that case, did he condemn the regional lords’ joining together, yet regard Lu’s nonparticipation in the covenant as fortunate? From this we therefore understand that the approval of Huan in the Spring and Autumn Annals expresses concern for order in the world, just as it expresses concern for the Way of true kingship.
“Luan Shu of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng.” 〔Sixth year of Duke Cheng.〕 “In summer, Gongsun Hui of Cao fled from Meng to Song.” 〔Twentieth year of Duke Zhao.〕

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
顧應龍
同考試官教諭朱批序功序賢雖延賞之典
而亦不失公選之意此作得之
同考試官教諭王批以書會推出枝臧為功
賢裔由月場中發多費詞此作約而盡
考試官教諭甘批得春秋重世臣之旨
考試官教授王批簡嚴典雅
經紀世官有示功臣當錄其後者有示賢臣當
錄其後者此見官不可世而惟功惟賢其後人
===
有足錄焉則晉之書曹之會其猶春秋所取歟
且夫故國雖以世臣而得名官人則必公選而
始善春秋之季官世授而事專行若華孫之來
魯也斯固春秋之所禁矣然則人君當如何而
可乎君子曰國家以報功為大典欒書之救鄭
固春秋所予也而書之先有枝焉謀行於戰楚
忠效於禦秦勳在旂常舊矣書也為枝後人則
固功臣之胄也有報功之思者即後嗣苟無失
德猶當以與國之休共之况書於鄭之救也下
punctuated:
顧應龍

同考試官教諭朱批：序功序賢，雖延賞之典，而亦不失公選之意，此作得之。
同考試官教諭王批：以書、會推出枝、臧為功賢裔，由月場中發，多費詞，此作約而盡。
考試官教諭甘批：得《春秋》重世臣之旨。
考試官教授王批：簡嚴典雅。

經紀世官，有示功臣當錄其後者，有示賢臣當錄其後者。此見官不可世，而惟功惟賢，其後人有足錄焉，則晉之書、曹之會，其猶《春秋》所取歟？

且夫故國雖以世臣而得名，官人則必公選而始善。《春秋》之季，官世授而事專行，若華孫之來魯也，斯固《春秋》之所禁矣。然則人君當如何而可乎？君子曰：國家以報功為大典。欒書之救鄭，固《春秋》所予也。而書之先有枝焉，謀行於戰楚，忠效於禦秦，勳在旂常舊矣。書也為枝後人，則固功臣之胄也。有報功之思者，即後嗣苟無失德，猶當以與國之休共之。况書於鄭之救也，下
translation_en:
Gu Yinglong

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “Ranking men by merit and worthiness, although a means of extending rewards to their descendants, also preserves the intention of impartial selection. This composition grasps that point.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “Through Shu and Hui, the essay traces back to Zhi and Zang, establishing descent from men of merit and worthiness. The passage transcribed as ‘由月場中發’ is doubtful [?]. Expounding this often requires many words; this composition is concise yet exhaustive.”
Comment by Examiner Gan, Instructor: “It captures the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals in valuing hereditary ministerial families.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “Concise, rigorous, dignified, and elegant.”

When the Classic records hereditary officeholders, some entries show that the descendants of meritorious ministers should receive consideration, and others that the descendants of worthy ministers should receive consideration. This shows that offices must not be hereditary; yet where a forebear possessed merit or worthiness, his descendants may have qualities deserving recognition. Are not Shu of Jin and Hui of Cao, then, among those approved by the Spring and Autumn Annals?

An ancient state indeed owes its reputation to its hereditary ministerial families, but the appointment of officials becomes sound only through impartial selection. Toward the end of the Spring and Autumn period, offices were transmitted hereditarily and affairs conducted arbitrarily. The arrival of Huasun in Lu exemplifies precisely what the Spring and Autumn Annals condemns. What, then, should a ruler do to act properly? The gentleman says: A state regards rewarding merit as a great institution. Luan Shu’s rescue of Zheng is certainly approved by the Spring and Autumn Annals. Among Shu’s forebears was Zhi, whose plans were put into effect in fighting Chu and whose loyalty was demonstrated in resisting Qin. His achievements had long been recorded on the banners of merit. As Zhi’s descendant, Shu was indeed the scion of a meritorious minister. A ruler intent on rewarding merit should allow such descendants to share in the blessings of the state, provided they have not failed in virtue. How much more so in Shu’s case, when, in rescuing Zheng, he issued …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
班師之令得專制之宜繩祖武而光前烈有足
多乎噫先世之功固不因書而始著而後人之
善實維以枝而益彰使世臣而皆若人也世濟
其勳雖錄功臣之後而亦莫非公選也授之以
政豈曰過哉人君以勸賢爲首務公孫會之奔
宋固春秋所取也而會之先有子臧焉附守節
之賢高讓國之義名聞諸侯久矣會也爲臧後
人則固賢者之類也有勸賢之心者即子孫雖
皆中才猶當以延世之賞及之况會於宋之奔
===
也待放以爲請賜玦而後去昭世德而著令名
有足取乎噫揖遜之高風既未泯於後裔而去
就之有禮又無忝於前人使世臣而皆若人也
世濟其美雖錄賢者之後而亦莫非公選也委
之以政又豈曰過哉是知必功臣之後而後官
可世也非功而世則私矣必賢者之後而後官
可世也非賢而世則私矣若華孫之先世何功
何賢而使之兵權繼掌乎吁此其所以專行而
無足取也雖然書沒而後嗣日微會奔而爵祿
punctuated:
班師之令，得專制之宜，繩祖武而光前烈，有足多乎！噫！先世之功固不因書而始著，而後人之善實維以枝而益彰。使世臣而皆若人也，世濟其勳，雖錄功臣之後，而亦莫非公選也。授之以政，豈曰過哉？
人君以勸賢爲首務，公孫會之奔宋，固《春秋》所取也。而會之先有子臧焉，附守節之賢，高讓國之義，名聞諸侯久矣。會也爲臧後人，則固賢者之類也。有勸賢之心者，即子孫雖皆中才，猶當以延世之賞及之。况會於宋之奔也，待放以爲請，賜玦而後去，昭世德而著令名，有足取乎！噫！揖遜之高風既未泯於後裔，而去就之有禮又無忝於前人。使世臣而皆若人也，世濟其美，雖錄賢者之後，而亦莫非公選也。委之以政，又豈曰過哉？
是知必功臣之後，而後官可世也；非功而世，則私矣。必賢者之後，而後官可世也；非賢而世，則私矣。若華孫之先世，何功何賢，而使之兵權繼掌乎？吁！此其所以專行而無足取也。雖然，書沒而後嗣日微，會奔而爵祿
translation_en:
…an order to withdraw the army, exercising independent authority as circumstances warranted, following his ancestor’s footsteps and bringing glory to his earlier achievements—was this not worthy of praise! Ah! The achievements of his forebears certainly did not first become illustrious through Shu; yet the excellence of their descendant was indeed made still more conspicuous by Zhi. If hereditary ministers were all such men, perpetuating their meritorious achievements from generation to generation, then even appointing the descendants of meritorious ministers would invariably constitute impartial selection. Could entrusting them with government be called a mistake?
A ruler’s foremost duty is to encourage the worthy. Gongsun Hui’s flight to Song was certainly approved by the Spring and Autumn Annals. Among Hui’s forebears was Zizang, long renowned among the feudal lords for his worthiness in upholding his principles [?] and the lofty righteousness of his refusal of rulership. As Zizang’s descendant, Hui certainly belonged to the lineage of a worthy man. Anyone intent on encouraging the worthy should extend rewards lasting across generations to their descendants, even if those descendants were all merely of middling ability. How much more so in Hui’s case: when he fled to Song, he requested permission to await dismissal and departed only after being granted a broken jade ring, the token of severance. In displaying his lineage’s virtue and establishing a fine reputation, was he not worthy of approval! Ah! The noble example of yielding rulership had not faded among later descendants, while his observance of propriety in leaving or remaining in service brought no disgrace upon his predecessor. If hereditary ministers were all such men, perpetuating their excellence from generation to generation, then even appointing the descendants of worthy men would invariably constitute impartial selection. Could entrusting them with government be called a mistake?
From this we know that only for descendants of meritorious ministers may office be hereditary; hereditary succession without merit is favoritism. Only for descendants of worthy men may office be hereditary; hereditary succession without worthiness is favoritism. As for the ancestors of Hua Sun, what merit or worthiness did they possess that he should be allowed to inherit command of the armed forces? Alas! This is why his independent action merits no approval. Nevertheless, after Shu died, his descendants declined day by day; after Hui fled, his rank and emoluments…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
無列晉侯曹伯非眞能用人者蓋春秋因此以
立義爾督與耦其行事亦若世濟焉顧得以世
其官而不疑也用舍如此此春秋所以作歟噫
後世官人者能明於春秋之義則崇報勳賢而
不爲私裁抑僥倖而不爲過世官公選其法固
可以並行而不悖矣
禮記
久則天天則神天則不言而信神則不怒
而威
===
周仕堦
同考試官教諭朱 批 詞精理當而發明天神
威信甚切非心通樂理者不能也允宜高薦
同考試官教諭王 批 天神之妙由久而得此作
足以發之是始知治心者
考試官教諭甘 批 順理之作
考試官教授王 批 和暢
記者推善心有恒之妙而必極言之也蓋善心
必久而彌章也馴致於天神則已極其妙矣而
punctuated:
無列，晉侯、曹伯非眞能用人者，蓋《春秋》因此以立義爾。督與耦，其行事亦若世濟焉，顧得以世其官而不疑也。用舍如此，此《春秋》所以作歟？噫！後世官人者能明於《春秋》之義，則崇報勳賢而不爲私，裁抑僥倖而不爲過，世官、公選，其法固可以並行而不悖矣。
禮記
久則天，天則神。天則不言而信，神則不怒而威。
周仕堦
同考試官教諭朱批：詞精理當，而發明天神威信甚切，非心通樂理者不能也。允宜高薦。
同考試官教諭王批：天神之妙，由久而得，此作足以發之，是始知治心者。
考試官教諭甘批：順理之作。
考試官教授王批：和暢。
記者推善心有恒之妙，而必極言之也。蓋善心必久而彌章也，馴致於天神，則已極其妙矣，而
translation_en:
…no place among the ranked nobility. The Marquis of Jin and the Earl of Cao were not truly adept at employing men; rather, the Spring and Autumn Annals used these cases to establish its moral principles. As for Du and Ou, their conduct likewise seemed to perpetuate their forebears’ ways, yet they were allowed to inherit their offices without question. With men employed and rejected in this fashion, was this not why the Spring and Autumn Annals was written? Ah! If those who appoint officials in later ages can understand the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals, they can honor and reward the meritorious and worthy without favoritism, and restrain those who obtain advancement through undeserved good fortune without going too far. Hereditary officeholding and impartial selection can indeed operate together without conflict.
Record of Rites
“When sustained, it becomes like Heaven; when like Heaven, it becomes numinous. Like Heaven, it commands trust without speaking; numinous, it inspires awe without anger.”
Zhou Shijie
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, an Instructor: “The wording is refined and the reasoning sound. Its elucidation of Heaven, the numinous, awe, and trust is especially apt. Only someone whose heart comprehends the principles of music could achieve this. It fully deserves recommendation for a high ranking.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, an Instructor: “The subtle workings of Heaven and the numinous are attained through sustained practice. This composition adequately brings them to light. Here is someone who has begun to understand how to govern the heart.”
Comment by Examiner Gan, an Instructor: “A composition that accords with principle.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, a Professor: “Harmonious and fluent.”
The compiler of the Record probes the subtle workings of constancy in a good heart, necessarily carrying his explanation to its fullest extent. For a good heart must endure if its goodness is to become ever more manifest. When it gradually attains the qualities of Heaven and the numinous, its subtle workings have already reached their utmost perfection, and …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
其信其威豈非出於自然者哉記者言此以明
致樂之功也意曰善端各足于吾人之心而養
心貴窮乎大樂之理君子致樂以治心則易直
子諒之生夫固由樂而安而久矣是其涵養純
而性真益固和順之積中持之以恒永而不渝
操存熟而良心有常至和之保合守之以貞固
而不失如是寧無馴致之妙乎蓋未至於久固
難以語天也既曰久矣吾知養盛之有素則至
理之愈融一真自如渾化其矜持之迹本原澄
===
澈從容於性分之安而久不足以名之矣豈不
謂之天乎未至於天固難以語神也既曰天矣
吾知天德之渾全則神應之自妙變化無方殆
非心思之所能窺流動不居亦非見聞之所能
及而天亦不足以名之矣豈不謂之神乎夫心
曰天神善之極也其妙豈但已耶彼信以實言
必言而後信非天也天則至誠以立其體中孚
以妙其用蓋不必脩詞於擬議而由衷之信夫
固默而成之者矣亦何俟於言耶威以飾怒必
punctuated: 其信其威，豈非出於自然者哉？記者言此以明致樂之功也。意曰：善端各足于吾人之心，而養心貴窮乎大樂之理。君子致樂以治心，則易直子諒之生，夫固由樂而安而久矣。是其涵養純而性真益固，和順之積中，持之以恒永而不渝；操存熟而良心有常，至和之保合，守之以貞固而不失。如是，寧無馴致之妙乎？蓋未至於久，固難以語天也。既曰久矣，吾知養盛之有素，則至理之愈融，一真自如，渾化其矜持之迹，本原澄澈，從容於性分之安，而久不足以名之矣，豈不謂之天乎？未至於天，固難以語神也。既曰天矣，吾知天德之渾全，則神應之自妙，變化無方，殆非心思之所能窺；流動不居，亦非見聞之所能及，而天亦不足以名之矣，豈不謂之神乎？夫心曰天神，善之極也，其妙豈但已耶？彼信以實言，必言而後信，非天也。天則至誠以立其體，中孚以妙其用，蓋不必脩詞於擬議，而由衷之信，夫固默而成之者矣，亦何俟於言耶？威以飾怒，必
translation_en:
…Its trustworthiness and its awe-inspiring power—do these not arise spontaneously? The author of the Record says this to illuminate the efficacy of bringing music to its fullest realization. His meaning is this: the beginnings of goodness are fully present in each of our hearts, and nurturing the heart depends upon thoroughly comprehending the principles of great music. When the gentleman brings music to its fullest realization to govern his heart, the ease, uprightness, kindness, and sincerity that arise thereby surely proceed through music to settled ease and then to enduring constancy. His inward cultivation becomes pure, and the genuineness of his nature grows ever more firmly established. Harmony and compliance with principle accumulate within, sustained with unchanging constancy. He becomes practiced in preserving his heart, and his good heart remains constant. Perfect harmony is preserved intact, guarded with steadfastness against loss. With things thus, could there fail to be the subtle efficacy of gradual attainment?

Before enduring constancy has been attained, one certainly cannot speak of the heavenly. Once we speak of enduring constancy, however, we know that abundant cultivation, long sustained, brings the highest principles into ever fuller integration. Undivided genuineness operates freely, wholly dissolving the traces of deliberate restraint. The source becomes clear and limpid; one rests at ease within the proper bounds of one's nature. “Enduring constancy” is then insufficient to name this state. Should it not be called “heavenly”? Before the heavenly has been attained, one certainly cannot speak of the numinous. Once we speak of the heavenly, however, we know that the integral wholeness of heavenly virtue makes its numinous responsiveness spontaneously wondrous. Its transformations have no fixed direction and can scarcely be fathomed by thought; it flows without remaining anywhere and cannot be reached through seeing and hearing. Even “heavenly” is then insufficient to name it. Should it not be called “numinous”?

When the heart is called heavenly and numinous, this is the utmost of goodness. Could its wondrous efficacy stop there? As for trustworthiness expressed through truthful words, if one must speak before being trusted, this is not the heavenly. In the heavenly, perfect sincerity establishes its substance, and inward trustworthiness makes its functioning wondrous. There is no need to refine one's words through deliberation: trustworthiness arising from within is surely accomplished in silence. Why should it await speech? As for awe-inspiring power lending force to anger, if one must…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
怒而後威非神也神則嚴毅存於中靈爽達於
外蓋不必大之以聲色而可畏之威夫固幾微
莫測者矣亦何假於怒耶是則致樂治心之妙
至於如此君子其可以斯須去樂哉雖然樂由
心作者也樂之理即吾心之和也君子苟能存
省以致吾心之和則安久天神一無所爲而然
矣由是而出之不言而信而天下莫不悅不怒
而威而天下莫不服以之協和萬邦昭宣化育
亦不外此否則器數聲容之末耳如善心何是
===
故君子致樂非難致吾心之樂爲難
外無敵內順治此之謂盛德
林如楚
同考試官教諭王批此題多著勇敢說而子
獨能歸諸聖王可謂知本之學矣錄之
同考試官教諭朱批發明內外成功歸重聖
王盛德深得本旨
考試官教諭芉批讀之令人奮發
考試官教授王批詞正義嚴
punctuated:
怒而後威，非神也。神則嚴毅存於中，靈爽達於外，蓋不必大之以聲色，而可畏之威，夫固幾微莫測者矣，亦何假於怒耶？是則致樂治心之妙，至於如此，君子其可以斯須去樂哉？雖然，樂由心作者也，樂之理即吾心之和也。君子苟能存省以致吾心之和，則安、久、天、神，一無所爲而然矣。由是而出之，不言而信，而天下莫不悅；不怒而威，而天下莫不服。以之協和萬邦，昭宣化育，亦不外此。否則器數聲容之末耳，如善心何？是故君子致樂非難，致吾心之樂爲難。
「外無敵，內順治，此之謂盛德。」
林如楚
同考試官教諭王批：「此題多著勇敢說，而子獨能歸諸聖王，可謂知本之學矣。錄之。」
同考試官教諭朱批：「發明內外成功，歸重聖王盛德，深得本旨。」
考試官教諭芉批：「讀之令人奮發。」
考試官教授王批：「詞正義嚴。」
translation_en:
…to become angry before inspiring awe is not numinous. In the numinous state, stern resolve abides within and spiritual clarity manifests outwardly. There is no need to magnify it through voice or expression: its awe-inspiring authority is already imperceptibly subtle and unfathomable. Why should it depend upon anger? Such is the wondrous efficacy of bringing music to fulfillment and ordering the heart. Can the gentleman dispense with music even for an instant? Yet music arises from the heart, and the principle of music is precisely the harmony of our own hearts. If the gentleman can preserve and examine his heart so as to realize its harmony, then tranquility, constancy, Heavenliness, and numinousness all arise without deliberate effort. When this manifests outwardly, he is trusted without speaking, and everyone under Heaven rejoices; he inspires awe without anger, and everyone under Heaven submits. Bringing the myriad states into harmony and manifesting transformative nurture likewise proceed from this alone. Otherwise, there are merely the incidental details of instruments, numerical arrangements, sounds, and ceremonial movements. What can these do to make the heart good? Thus, for the gentleman, bringing music to fulfillment is not difficult; bringing the music of his own heart to fulfillment is difficult.
“Without, there are no enemies; within, there is obedience and good order: this is called consummate virtue.”
Lin Ruchu 林如楚
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “Most treatments of this topic dwell on courage, but you alone can trace it back to the sage king. This may indeed be called learning that understands the root. Selected for inclusion.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “He elucidates the achievements accomplished within and without, placing the emphasis on the sage king’s consummate virtue. He has profoundly grasped the original purport.”
Comment by Examiner Gan 芉 [?], Instructor: “Reading this stirs one to vigorous effort.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “The language is correct and the meaning rigorous.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
天下成一統之功聖王之德至矣蓋治功之建
德其本也聖王用勇敢而靖外安內之功成焉
不可以觀至德矣乎記聘義者意曰王者以一
人而統天下之治則必任賢以成天下之功嘗
觀諸用勇敢而知之矣今夫天下有遠而在外
者焉外而敢於稱敵者以威不能懾之耳玆惟
用勇敢於戰勝而外無敵則是壯猷宣於閫外
每貴謀以制師之勝威信結於邊圉恒不戰而
屈人之兵觀之於外莫不來享而來王也有近
===
而在內者焉內而敢於梗化者以禮不能導之
耳玆惟用勇敢於禮義而內順治則是脩禮以
明民自各安其分而不悖達義以齊衆自各守
其度而不踰觀之於內蓋皆相率以成風也若
此者謂不可以觀聖王之盛德乎蓋有明作之
治功者必有惇大之治體以為之基有富有之
大業者必有日新之盛德以為之運得人以仁
天下帝德之被殆將無遠而弗屆蓋其德之所
施者博故其威之所制者廣矣致賢以及萬民
punctuated:
天下成一統之功，聖王之德至矣。蓋治功之建，德其本也。聖王用勇敢，而靖外安內之功成焉，不可以觀至德矣乎？記《聘義》者意曰：王者以一人而統天下之治，則必任賢以成天下之功。嘗觀諸用勇敢而知之矣。

今夫天下有遠而在外者焉。外而敢於稱敵者，以威不能懾之耳。玆惟用勇敢於戰勝，而外無敵，則是壯猷宣於閫外，每貴謀以制師之勝；威信結於邊圉，恒不戰而屈人之兵。觀之於外，莫不來享而來王也。有近而在內者焉。內而敢於梗化者，以禮不能導之耳。玆惟用勇敢於禮義，而內順治，則是脩禮以明民，自各安其分而不悖；達義以齊衆，自各守其度而不踰。觀之於內，蓋皆相率以成風也。若此者，謂不可以觀聖王之盛德乎？

蓋有明作之治功者，必有惇大之治體以為之基；有富有之大業者，必有日新之盛德以為之運。得人以仁天下，帝德之被，殆將無遠而弗屆。蓋其德之所施者博，故其威之所制者廣矣。致賢以及萬民，
translation_en:
When the achievement of unifying All under Heaven is complete, the virtue of the sage king has reached its utmost. For virtue is the foundation upon which the achievements of government are built. When the sage king employs the brave and courageous, he succeeds in pacifying the exterior and securing the interior. Can we not behold his consummate virtue in this? The meaning intended by the author of “The Meaning of Diplomatic Missions” (Pin yi) is this: since the king, as a single person, directs the government of All under Heaven, he must entrust worthy men with office to accomplish its affairs. We can understand this by observing his employment of the brave and courageous.

Now, within All under Heaven there are distant regions beyond the realm. Those outside who dare to set themselves up as enemies do so only because authority has failed to overawe them. When bravery and courage are employed to secure victory in battle, leaving no enemies outside, mighty plans are put into effect beyond the military commander's gates, and strategy is always prized as the means of securing the army's victory. Authority and trust are established along the frontiers, and the enemy's troops are regularly subdued without battle. Looking to the exterior, we see that none fail to come with offerings and acknowledge the king's sovereignty. There are also nearby regions within the realm. Those within who dare to obstruct the ruler's transforming influence do so only because ritual has failed to guide them. When bravery and courage are employed in the service of ritual and righteousness, bringing obedience and good order within, ritual is cultivated to enlighten the people, so that each rests content in his allotted station without rebellion; righteousness is made manifest to bring the multitude into order, so that each observes his proper bounds without overstepping them. Looking to the interior, we see that all lead one another toward good customs. In circumstances such as these, can one say that the sage king's abundant virtue cannot be discerned?

Achievements in government marked by enlightened action must have a substantial and generous governing foundation to sustain them. Great undertakings of ample scope must have abundant virtue, renewed daily, to keep them in motion. By obtaining the right men, the ruler extends benevolence throughout All under Heaven; the influence of imperial virtue will surely reach even the most distant places. Because his virtue is broadly extended, his authority exercises control over a wide expanse. By attracting worthy men, he reaches the myriad people…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
王澤之施殆將無近而不悅蓋其德之所積者
厚故其政之入人也深矣允文允武協和乎萬
邦之化克剛克柔弼成乎五服之治非盛德孰
能如此乎吁觀內外之功而見聖德之盛如此
然則勇敢之用豈可忽諸雖然任人圖治者人
君之知也精白承休者人臣之忠也使勇敢之
士匪由於敢行禮義則不過血氣之強而已其
能成內外之功者幾希故必有呂望之忠而後
可以成鷹揚之勳有方叔之忠而後得以建于
===
襄之績此又人臣所當知
第貳場
論
聖人太極之全體
蔡乾釜
同考試官教諭陳 批 人心本具太極惟聖人能
心會之此作發揮透徹末歸主靜尤知聖學之要錄之
同考試官教諭宋 批 此題作者類以陰陽動靜
敷演漫無歸宿子獨以心極立論深得本旨
punctuated:
王澤之施，殆將無近而不悅。蓋其德之所積者厚，故其政之入人也深矣。允文允武，協和乎萬邦之化；克剛克柔，弼成乎五服之治。非盛德，孰能如此乎？吁！觀內外之功，而見聖德之盛如此，然則勇敢之用豈可忽諸？雖然，任人圖治者，人君之知也；精白承休者，人臣之忠也。使勇敢之士匪由於敢行禮義，則不過血氣之強而已，其能成內外之功者幾希。故必有呂望之忠，而後可以成鷹揚之勳；有方叔之忠，而後得以建于襄之績。此又人臣所當知。
第貳場
論
聖人太極之全體
蔡乾釜
同考試官教諭陳批：人心本具太極，惟聖人能心會之。此作發揮透徹，末歸主靜，尤知聖學之要，錄之。
同考試官教諭宋批：此題作者類以陰陽動靜敷演，漫無歸宿。子獨以心極立論，深得本旨。
translation_en:
…Where the king’s beneficence extends, surely none nearby will fail to rejoice. Because his accumulated virtue is profound, his government enters deeply into people’s hearts. Truly accomplished in both civil and martial affairs, he harmonizes the myriad states through his transforming influence; capable of both firmness and gentleness, he brings to completion the governance of the five service zones. Who could accomplish this without abundant virtue? Ah! Observing these achievements within and without, we see how abundant the sage’s virtue is. How, then, could the employment of courageous men be neglected? Nevertheless, appointing men to pursue good government manifests a ruler’s wisdom; serving with purified sincerity to uphold his beneficent rule manifests a minister’s loyalty. If courageous men do not proceed from the resolve to practice ritual propriety and righteousness, theirs is merely the strength of blood and vital energy. Few indeed could achieve anything within or without. Thus only with the loyalty of Lü Wang can one achieve exploits like his soaring eagle’s might; only with the loyalty of Fang Shu can one establish achievements like his majestic advance. This, too, ministers ought to understand.
Second Session
Discourse
“The Sage Embodies the Supreme Ultimate in Its Entirety”
Cai Qianfu
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: The human mind inherently possesses the Supreme Ultimate, but only the sage can apprehend it in his mind. This composition develops the subject with thorough insight. Its conclusion returns to making stillness primary, showing an especially sound understanding of the essentials of sagely learning. Selected for inclusion.
Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: Those writing on this topic generally elaborate upon yin and yang, movement and stillness, rambling without reaching any conclusion. You alone base your argument on the mind as the Supreme Ultimate, profoundly grasping the essential meaning.

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭甘批〔理□詞暢氣裕雄渾信士〕
考試官敎授王批〔議論從心得發出迥然自別〕
天下有至理惟天下至人能盡之何者理出於
天天全於聖人之一心其寂然而不動也是太
極之靜而陰也其感而遂通天下之故也是太
極之動而陽也以陰陽爲動靜而有所以主宰
之者是爲太極以寂感爲動靜而亦有所主
宰之者是爲能全體太極吁惟聖人能全體太
極此聖人所以爲太極之全體也然則聖人之
===
能從事於心極也其聖人所以能全體太極乎
嘗聞之易曰易有太極是太極也不離乎陰陽
而亦不雜乎陰陽以動靜爲體用而寔有根抵
乎動靜體用之間者是則化育流行之本體也
其在於天則然矣是何以屬之聖人而聖人亦
何以全體乎太極耶蓋太極雖原於天而其理
則具於人心是即所謂性也是即所謂心極也
天有元亨而吾人得之則爲仁爲中仁也中也
是太極之用之所以行也天有利貞而吾人得
punctuated:
考試官敎諭甘批〔理□詞暢，氣裕雄渾，信士。〕
考試官敎授王批〔議論從心得發出，迥然自別。〕
天下有至理，惟天下至人能盡之。何者？理出於天，天全於聖人之一心。其寂然而不動也，是太極之靜而陰也；其感而遂通天下之故也，是太極之動而陽也。以陰陽爲動靜，而有所以主宰之者，是爲太極；以寂感爲動靜，而亦有所主宰之者，是爲能全體太極。吁！惟聖人能全體太極，此聖人所以爲太極之全體也。然則聖人之能從事於心極也，其聖人所以能全體太極乎？
嘗聞之，《易》曰：「易有太極。」是太極也，不離乎陰陽，而亦不雜乎陰陽。以動靜爲體用，而寔有根抵乎動靜體用之間者，是則化育流行之本體也。其在於天則然矣，是何以屬之聖人，而聖人亦何以全體乎太極耶？蓋太極雖原於天，而其理則具於人心，是即所謂性也，是即所謂心極也。天有元亨，而吾人得之則爲仁爲中。仁也，中也，是太極之用之所以行也。天有利貞，而吾人得
translation_en:
Examiner Gan, Instructor, comments: 〔The principle is □ [?], the language fluent, and the vital force ample, powerful, and integrated—a trustworthy scholar [?].〕
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: 〔The argument arises from insights gained in his own mind and stands distinctly apart.〕
There is an ultimate principle in the world, and only the world's perfected person can fully realize it. Why? Principle issues from Heaven, and Heaven is fully embodied in the single mind of the sage. When that mind is still and unmoving, this is the stillness and yin of the Supreme Ultimate (taiji); when it responds to stimuli and thereby comprehends the affairs of the world, this is the movement and yang of the Supreme Ultimate. Taking yin and yang as movement and stillness, that which governs them is called the Supreme Ultimate. Taking quiescence and response as movement and stillness, likewise to have that which governs them is to embody the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety. Ah! Only the sage can embody the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety. This is why the sage constitutes the complete embodiment of the Supreme Ultimate. Is the sage's ability to devote himself to the ultimate within the mind, then, what enables him to embody the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety?
I have heard it said in the Book of Changes: “In the Changes there is the Supreme Ultimate.” This Supreme Ultimate is inseparable from yin and yang, yet is not mingled with them. Stillness and movement constitute its substance and function, yet something is truly rooted within this stillness and movement, substance and function: this is the fundamental substance of the flowing processes of transformation and nurture. Such is its existence in Heaven. Why, then, is it attributed to the sage, and how can the sage embody the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety? Although the Supreme Ultimate originates in Heaven, its principle is fully present in the human mind. This is precisely what is called human nature, and precisely what is called the ultimate within the mind. Heaven possesses origination and flourishing; when we humans receive these, they become benevolence and centrality. Benevolence and centrality are what allow the function of the Supreme Ultimate to operate. Heaven possesses benefit and constancy; when we humans receive…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
之則爲義爲正義也正也是太極之體之所以
立也體立用行則爲太極全體能體立而用行
則聖人能爲太極全體也夫太極天道之至極
也聖人即能從事於心極其又何以能全體乎
太極耶曰心者理之會而盡心則所以會理之
全也惟能會理之全斯可以言太極全體矣蓋
太極之全體無物不有而無有一理之不備無
時不流行而無有一息之或間者也衆人有之
而不知固不可以言體賢人踐之而未盡亦豈
===
所以言全體乎惟聖人能以一心而涵太極之
祕故能以一身而體太極之全時而動焉爲仁
爲中是太極之用也動亦一太極也時而靜焉
爲義爲正是太極之體也靜亦一太極也以是
仁義中正體備於聖人之一心而無有一之或
虧是以其渾全者而全此太極也以是仁義中
正流行於聖人之一心而無有一之或間是以
其流行者而全此太極也譬則人身焉非四肢
百骸畢具不可以言全體四肢百骸具矣然非
punctuated:
之，則爲義、爲正。義也，正也，是太極之體之所以立也。體立用行，則爲太極全體；能體立而用行，則聖人能爲太極全體也。夫太極，天道之至極也。聖人即能從事於心極，其又何以能全體乎太極耶？曰：心者，理之會，而盡心則所以會理之全也。惟能會理之全，斯可以言太極全體矣。

蓋太極之全體，無物不有，而無有一理之不備；無時不流行，而無有一息之或間者也。衆人有之而不知，固不可以言體；賢人踐之而未盡，亦豈所以言全體乎？惟聖人能以一心而涵太極之祕，故能以一身而體太極之全。時而動焉，爲仁、爲中，是太極之用也，動亦一太極也；時而靜焉，爲義、爲正，是太極之體也，靜亦一太極也。以是仁義中正，體備於聖人之一心，而無有一之或虧，是以其渾全者而全此太極也。以是仁義中正，流行於聖人之一心，而無有一之或間，是以其流行者而全此太極也。

譬則人身焉，非四肢百骸畢具，不可以言全體。四肢百骸具矣，然非
translation_en:
…it becomes righteousness and rectitude. Righteousness and rectitude are that through which the substance of the Supreme Ultimate (taiji) is established. When its substance is established and its functioning proceeds, this constitutes the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety. By being able to establish that substance and carry out that functioning, the sage can embody the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety. Now, the Supreme Ultimate is the utmost culmination of the Way of Heaven. Even if the sage can devote himself to the ultimate within the mind, how can he thereby embody the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety? The answer is: the mind is where principles converge, and fully realizing the mind is the means of bringing together principle in its entirety. Only when one can bring together principle in its entirety can one speak of embodying the Supreme Ultimate in full.

The Supreme Ultimate in its entirety is present in every thing, with not a single principle lacking; it flows and operates at every moment, without even a single breath’s interruption. Ordinary people possess it but do not know it, so they certainly cannot be said to embody it. Worthy people put it into practice but do not exhaust it: how, then, could they be said to embody it in its entirety? Only the sage can embrace the mystery of the Supreme Ultimate within his single mind, and therefore embody its entirety in his own person. When the time calls for activity, he is benevolent and centered: this is the functioning of the Supreme Ultimate, and his activity is itself a Supreme Ultimate. When the time calls for stillness, he is righteous and upright: this is the substance of the Supreme Ultimate, and his stillness is itself a Supreme Ultimate. Thus benevolence, righteousness, centeredness, and rectitude are fully present in substance within the sage’s single mind, with none in any way deficient. Through their integral completeness, he fully embodies this Supreme Ultimate. These same qualities flow and operate within the sage’s single mind, with none ever interrupted. Through their flowing operation, he fully embodies this Supreme Ultimate.

Take the human body as an analogy. Unless its four limbs and all its bones are present, it cannot be called a complete body. Yet even when its four limbs and all its bones are present, unless…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
有精神血脉以充溢貫注乎其間亦不可以言
全體也故以聖心而無一理之或虧也其猶四
肢百骸之無不具以其無一息之或間也其猶
精神血脉之無不充溢而貫注乎若聖人者眞
能全體乎太極其亦眞可謂太極之全體矣或
者以爲性體本全仁義中正蓋人人有之亦人
人能盡之者而何以獨歸之聖人不知性體雖
無不全而發見則有偏曲方其爲發見之一曲
也是猶一體也其致曲而有誠也是猶因一體
===
以求全體也若聖人則由稟受而全體無不兼
該由應感而全體無不呈露天之所動心與之
一焉心之所萌天亦與之一焉以全其天於一
心也萬物統體一太極也是太極之全體也以
達其天於萬感也物物各具一太極也是太極
之所以爲全體也故以是而立極於人也爲人
極以是而建極於天下也爲皇極夫極爲皇極
則不惟吾之所以錫極而保極者由於斯將舉
天下之所以會極而歸極者亦由於斯由是則
punctuated: 有精神血脉以充溢貫注乎其間，亦不可以言全體也。故以聖心而無一理之或虧也，其猶四肢百骸之無不具；以其無一息之或間也，其猶精神血脉之無不充溢而貫注乎。若聖人者，眞能全體乎太極，其亦眞可謂太極之全體矣。或者以爲性體本全，仁義中正蓋人人有之，亦人人能盡之者，而何以獨歸之聖人？不知性體雖無不全，而發見則有偏曲。方其爲發見之一曲也，是猶一體也；其致曲而有誠也，是猶因一體以求全體也。若聖人，則由稟受而全體無不兼該，由應感而全體無不呈露。天之所動，心與之一焉；心之所萌，天亦與之一焉。以全其天於一心也，萬物統體一太極也，是太極之全體也；以達其天於萬感也，物物各具一太極也，是太極之所以爲全體也。故以是而立極於人也，爲人極；以是而建極於天下也，爲皇極。夫極爲皇極，則不惟吾之所以錫極而保極者由於斯，將舉天下之所以會極而歸極者亦由於斯。由是則
translation_en:
…unless vital spirit and blood also fill and circulate throughout them, one cannot speak of a complete body. Thus, that the sage’s mind lacks no principle is like the body’s possessing all its limbs and bones; that it suffers no interruption for even a single breath is like vital spirit and blood filling and circulating throughout the body. Such a person as the sage can truly embody the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety and may indeed be called the complete embodiment of the Supreme Ultimate.

Some maintain that human nature is intrinsically complete: benevolence, righteousness, centrality, and correctness are qualities that everyone possesses and can fully realize. Why, then, attribute this exclusively to the sage? They do not understand that, although human nature is complete in everyone, its manifestations may be partial and distorted. When it manifests itself in just one particular aspect, this is like a single member of the body. To develop that particular aspect to the utmost and thereby attain sincerity is like proceeding from one member to seek the complete body. With the sage, however, the endowment received encompasses the whole without exception, and responses to external stimuli reveal the whole without exception. Whatever Heaven sets in motion, the mind is one with it; whatever arises in the mind, Heaven likewise is one with it.

By fully realizing what is Heaven-given within the single mind, the myriad things, taken together, constitute one Supreme Ultimate: this is the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety. By extending what is Heaven-given through the myriad responses, each thing possesses a Supreme Ultimate of its own: this is how the Supreme Ultimate constitutes a complete whole. Thus, when through this one establishes the ultimate standard among human beings, it is the Ultimate Standard for Humanity; when through this one establishes the ultimate standard throughout the realm, it is the August Ultimate. When this ultimate standard becomes the August Ultimate, not only does the means by which I confer and preserve that standard derive from this; the means by which all under Heaven assemble at and return to that standard also derive from this. From this, then…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
知天之由一中以分造化也此極也此全體也
人之由一心以全造化於天也此極也亦此全
體也然則太極一天而已矣聖人之能爲太極
全體也亦一天而已矣吁此天下之至理所以
惟天下至人能盡之而聖人之心極乃其所以
通於三極而與天爲一也歟雖然動靜之全固
人心之所兼體然所謂人生而靜者則又性眞
之本體也北辰在天以不動而名爲極則聖人
之全體乎太極也亦豈以動而得之乎周子所
===
謂定以中正仁義固其主靜以立極之大端而
所謂無欲故靜云者則尤所以主靜之要旨也
吁人能由無欲以求靜由靜以求立極則於全
體太極之義其庶幾矣
表
擬宋作敬天圖羣臣賀表乾道七年
陳經邦
同考試官敎諭朱 批 援引精詳詞語莊重形
容敬天意甚切
punctuated:
知天之由一中以分造化也，此極也，此全體也；人之由一心以全造化於天也，此極也，亦此全體也。然則太極，一天而已矣；聖人之能爲太極全體也，亦一天而已矣。吁！此天下之至理，所以惟天下至人能盡之，而聖人之心極，乃其所以通於三極而與天爲一也歟！雖然，動靜之全，固人心之所兼體；然所謂「人生而靜」者，則又性眞之本體也。北辰在天，以不動而名爲極，則聖人之全體乎太極也，亦豈以動而得之乎？周子所謂「定以中正仁義」，固其主靜以立極之大端；而所謂「無欲故靜」云者，則尤所以主靜之要旨也。吁！人能由無欲以求靜，由靜以求立極，則於全體太極之義，其庶幾矣！

表
擬宋作《敬天圖》，羣臣賀表。乾道七年。
陳經邦

同考試官敎諭朱批：援引精詳，詞語莊重，形容敬天意甚切。
translation_en:
…we understand that Heaven unfolds creation and transformation from a single center: this is the Ultimate, and this is its complete substance. When a person, through a single heart, brings Heaven’s creation and transformation to completeness, this is the Ultimate, and likewise its complete substance. Thus the Supreme Ultimate is simply the one Heaven; the sage’s capacity to embody the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety is likewise simply the one Heaven. Ah! This is the utmost principle of all under Heaven, which only the most perfected person under Heaven can fully realize. Is not the Ultimate in the sage’s heart therefore what enables him to communicate with the Three Ultimates—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—and become one with Heaven? Nevertheless, although the human heart embodies both activity and stillness in their entirety, what is meant by “human beings are still at birth” is the original substance of the nature in its genuineness. The Northern Pole in the heavens is called the Ultimate because it does not move. How, then, could the sage attain complete embodiment of the Supreme Ultimate through activity? What Master Zhou calls “establishing it through centrality, correctness, humaneness, and righteousness” is indeed the principal means by which he gives primacy to stillness and establishes the Ultimate. Yet the statement “without desire, therefore still” expresses still more particularly the essential meaning of giving primacy to stillness. Ah! If a person can seek stillness through freedom from desire, and seek to establish the Ultimate through stillness, he will come close to the meaning of embodying the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety.

Memorial
A model congratulatory memorial from the assembled officials on the Song emperor’s production of the Diagram of Reverence for Heaven. Seventh year of the Qiandao reign [1171].
By Chen Jingbang.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “The citations are precise and thorough, and the language dignified. It expresses the intention of revering Heaven with great aptness.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: The form is upright and dignified, and the exposition detailed and clear. This is the work of someone skilled in four-and-six parallel prose.
Comment by Examiner Miao, Instructor: Loyalty and devotion find expression within the parallel phrases. It properly accords with the form of a congratulatory memorial and merits inclusion.

On a certain day of a certain month in the seventh year of Qiandao, Your servants, so-and-so and others, offer congratulations upon the imperially composed Diagram of Reverence for Heaven.
We humbly submit: the stellar lodges Kui and Bi shine in their courses; from the embroidered throne are displayed the essentials of the sages’ classics. The charts and writings inaugurate an auspicious age; the jeweled imperial inscription reveals the grandeur of Heaven’s mandate. Looking upward, we perceive that Heaven’s descending scrutiny is not remote, and know that there is a way reverently to receive it. Duty demands strict care in preserving this mandate; our resolve is earnest, with the trembling caution of one treading upon ice. We, so-and-so and others, in fear and joy, bow our heads to the ground and kowtow.
We humbly reflect that the government of the Two Emperors and Three Kings was rooted in the Way, and their Way was rooted in the heart. The Way is rooted in the heart, and nothing is more essential to the heart than taking reverence as its master. The heart takes reverence as its master, and no expression of reverence is greater than serving Heaven. Through cultured thought and reverence, Yao could make his great virtue shine forth; through vigilance over the subtle beginnings of affairs, Shun’s renewed brilliance truly accorded with Yao’s.
