出入靡常而尚書天人之交幾微易忽乃
於
燕閒之適更爲逸豫之防顧其微言每棼棼
而散見至於開卷竟兀兀於旁搜遂編摩
以成圖使簡明而易覽厭伏生之口澤飮
彼精華發孔壁之珍藏愼其樞要格言滿
punctuated:
克艱，湯式九圍，益嚴顧諟；文昭事於上帝，武受戒於丹書。矧姬旦敎千萬世爲臣之忠，而成王培八百年興王之業，祗陳《無逸》，克相有周。自昔求治之皇皇，孰非小心之翼翼？淵源雖遠，幸七觀存心法之精；汗竹方殷，賴一脈衍人文之賁。
玆蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，穆淸毓粹，靜一含元，爲天立心，撫羣龍而宅吉；以敬作所，馭六馬而中興。辨原道，觀化理之原；論用人，察銓綜之敘。謂人君敬怠之念，出入靡常，而《尚書》天人之交，幾微易忽。乃於燕閒之適，更爲逸豫之防。顧其微言，每棼棼而散見；至於開卷，竟兀兀於旁搜。遂編摩以成圖，使簡明而易覽。厭伏生之口澤，飮彼精華；發孔壁之珍藏，愼其樞要。格言滿
translation_en:
…overcoming difficulties. Tang set an example for the nine regions, attending ever more reverently to the luminous mandate. King Wen served the Lord on High with manifest devotion; King Wu received admonitions from the Cinnabar Writing. Furthermore, Ji Dan taught countless generations the loyalty proper to a minister, while King Cheng laid the foundation for eight hundred years of royal rule. Reverently setting forth Against Ease, Ji Dan ably assisted the Zhou. Of all those who earnestly sought good government in antiquity, who did not exercise vigilant care? Though these sources lie far in the past, fortunately “seven observations preserve” [?] the essentials of the teaching of the mind. Written records have grown abundant, yet a single line of transmission sustains the splendor of human culture.
Now we have reverently encountered [four circle marks in the text] Your Majesty, who nurtures purity in august serenity and embraces the primal source in stillness and singleness of purpose. You establish the mind on Heaven’s behalf, preside over the assembled dragons, and dwell in auspiciousness; you make reverence your dwelling, drive the six horses, and restore flourishing rule. In distinguishing and tracing the Way, you discern the source of transformative governance; in discussing the employment of men, you examine the ordering of selection and assessment. You hold that a ruler’s thoughts of reverence and indolence come and go without constancy, and that the subtle workings of the intercourse between Heaven and humanity in the Book of Documents are easily overlooked. Thus, even amid the pleasures of leisure, you further guard against ease and indulgence. Yet its subtle sayings appear scattered and tangled, so that opening the book entails laborious searches far and wide. You therefore compiled and arranged them into diagrams, making them concise, clear, and easy to consult. You partake fully of the legacy of Fu Sheng’s oral teachings, drinking in their essence; you bring forth the treasures hidden in the wall of Confucius’s house, attending carefully to their cardinal principles. Its maxims fill…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
戶牖取之左右逢原望道在憂勤亦云夙
夜匪懈
雲章煥
紫極弘敷邃古之文
天藻麗丹鉛永肇肅雍之助昔
聖祖録遺編於崇政倣訓堂階曁
神廟頒全經於學宫掄才冰鑑
燕謀尚傳於
中祕
===
鴻圖有待於
表章奮淵默之雷聲不謂瞻河洛於東觀炳
明威之日鑒何須厪記誦於雒陽曰旦曰
明凜陟降於宥密善繼善述篤駿惠於乂
康悟斲輪以傳心識洞
九玄之上謝還珠於兼體道通三極之先彼觴
戒豆銘心直閑於一事而矇詩瞽史功猶
費於多聞詎若是圖之顯設寔爲
聖學之大成也臣等恭際
punctuated: 戶牖，取之左右逢原。望道在憂勤，亦云夙夜匪懈。雲章煥紫極，弘敷邃古之文；天藻麗丹鉛，永肇肅雍之助。昔聖祖録遺編於崇政，倣訓堂階；曁神廟頒全經於學宫，掄才冰鑑。燕謀尚傳於中祕，鴻圖有待於表章。奮淵默之雷聲，不謂瞻河洛於東觀；炳明威之日鑒，何須厪記誦於雒陽？曰旦曰明，凜陟降於宥密；善繼善述，篤駿惠於乂康。悟斲輪以傳心，識洞九玄之上；謝還珠於兼體，道通三極之先。彼觴戒豆銘，心直閑於一事；而矇詩瞽史，功猶費於多聞。詎若是圖之顯設，寔爲聖學之大成也！臣等恭際
translation_en:
…windows and doors; wherever one reaches, left or right, one finds the source. Aspiring to the Way lies in anxious diligence; it is also said, “Never slackening, morning or night.” Imperial calligraphy shines in the Purple Pole, broadly unfolding the writings of remote antiquity; celestial compositions lend splendor to the work of brush and pigment, establishing enduring assistance toward reverence and harmony. Formerly, the Sage Ancestor recorded surviving writings at Chongzheng, taking their teachings as a model in his hall and on its steps [?]; later, the emperor known by the temple designation Shen distributed the complete Classic to the schools, providing a clear mirror for selecting talent. Plans for the peace of posterity are still transmitted within the palace archives; the grand design awaits elucidation and acclaim.
Sounding forth like thunder from profound silence, it unexpectedly allows us to behold the revelations of the He and Luo rivers in the Eastern Library [?]. Shining with an awesome, sunlike discernment, what need has it to depend upon memorization and recitation at Luoyang? Daybreak after daybreak, with ever-renewed illumination, one reverently senses the ascent and descent of the divine presence in profound stillness. Skillfully continuing and carrying forward the work of predecessors, one earnestly follows their example toward good government and peace. Understanding the wheelwright’s lesson, one transmits the understanding of the heart, with insight penetrating beyond the nine heavens; declining the returned pearl through comprehensive embodiment [?], the Way reaches back before the three cosmic powers.
As for admonitions on drinking cups and inscriptions on ritual vessels, these guard the mind only in a single matter; and the poems of blind musicians and the histories recited by blind officers still demand the labor of extensive learning. How could they equal the lucid presentation of this chart, which truly brings sagely learning to its fullest accomplishment! We, your servants, respectfully find ourselves living in …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
昌時仰承
懿範覩八法未乾之
御墨莫罄揄揚喜
一德已契於
璇穹無裨翊贊伏願
政叅元化
學務緝熈
聖心允合
天心而益隆
===
天眷
君道克配
天道而永介
天庥
一人合上下以同流萬載統華夷而順治臣等
無任瞻
天仰
聖激切忻忭之至謹奉
表稱
punctuated: 昌時，仰承懿範。覩八法未乾之御墨，莫罄揄揚；喜一德已契於璇穹，無裨翊贊。伏願政叅元化，學務緝熈，聖心允合天心而益隆天眷，君道克配天道而永介天庥。一人合上下以同流，萬載統華夷而順治。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切忻忭之至，謹奉表稱
translation_en: …in this flourishing age, we reverently receive Your Majesty’s exemplary guidance. Beholding the imperial ink, displaying the eight methods of calligraphy and not yet dry, we cannot exhaust our praises; rejoicing that Your Majesty’s single-minded virtue already accords with the jeweled heavens, we can offer nothing further by way of assistance. We humbly wish that your governance may participate in the primal work of transformation, and that your learning may strive for ever-continuing illumination; that your sagely heart may truly accord with Heaven’s heart and receive ever greater heavenly favor; and that the Way of the ruler may match the Way of Heaven and forever receive Heaven’s protection. May the One Man unite those above and below in a common course, and for ten thousand years bring the Chinese and the outer peoples together under harmonious rule. We, your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your sagely Majesty with the utmost ardor and joy. We respectfully submit this memorial to express…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
賀以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
王大道
同考試官教諭徐批揄揚我
皇上昭事之誠
繼述之善既極詳悉而末復祝願懃懇其忠愛藹然可想見也宜錄以式
===
同考試官教諭陳批我
皇上殿門聿成之詔媲美典謨子獨能颺言之非涵濡之深者耶
考試官教諭甘批宏詞朗識蓋渥沐
聖世之化而善鳴其盛者
考試官教授王批考據詳明宜取以式多士
帝王之道莫大乎敬天然必奉順其申錫
之意而後時憲之義彰莫重乎法祖然必
駿惠其於昭之神而後繼序之心盡蓋天
之意在人祖之神在天本流通浹洽而無
punctuated:
賀以聞。

第叁場
策
第一問
王大道

同考試官教諭徐批：揄揚我皇上昭事之誠、繼述之善，既極詳悉，而末復祝願懃懇，其忠愛藹然可想見也。宜錄以式。

同考試官教諭陳批：我皇上殿門聿成之詔，媲美典謨。子獨能颺言之，非涵濡之深者耶？

考試官教諭甘批：宏詞朗識，蓋渥沐聖世之化而善鳴其盛者。

考試官教授王批：考據詳明，宜取以式多士。

帝王之道，莫大乎敬天，然必奉順其申錫之意，而後時憲之義彰；莫重乎法祖，然必駿惠其於昭之神，而後繼序之心盡。蓋天之意在人，祖之神在天，本流通浹洽而無
translation_en:
…to offer congratulations and submit them for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essay
First Question
Wang Dadao

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: His praise of our Emperor’s sincerity in reverently serving Heaven and his excellence in continuing and carrying forward his predecessors’ work is already exceedingly thorough and detailed. At the close, he again offers earnest good wishes. One can readily perceive his abundant loyalty and affection. This should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Our Emperor’s edict announcing the completion of the palace halls and gates rivals the Canons and Counsels of the Book of Documents in excellence. You alone have been able to proclaim this eloquently—is this not because you have been deeply steeped in their teachings?

Comment by Examiner Gan, Instructor: Grand diction and clear understanding: here is someone who has been richly imbued with the transforming influence of this sagely age and can eloquently celebrate its flourishing.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: The examination of textual evidence is detailed and clear. This should be selected as a model for the many scholars.

In the Way of emperors and kings, nothing is greater than revering Heaven. Yet only by respectfully complying with its intent in repeatedly bestowing blessings can the meaning of taking Heaven as one’s model be made manifest. Nothing is weightier than emulating one’s ancestors. Yet only by fully following their luminous spirits can the resolve to continue their succession be fulfilled. For Heaven’s intent resides in human beings, while the ancestors’ spirits reside in Heaven; these inherently circulate freely and permeate one another, without…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
間也不有以奉順之則無以隆昭事而承
其休不有以駿惠之則無以廣孝思而揚
其烈是故惟時惟幾所以敬天也而祖之
神益以安敬之至也而亦莫非孝也善繼
善述所以法祖也而天之意益以順孝之
達也而亦莫非敬也知乎此則我
皇上因時以盡制
敷極以錫民
成功巍然文章煥然足以克當
===
天心而增光
祖烈者可以仰窺其萬一矣請因明問而敬對
揚之自古帝王繼天立極莫不有道以相
授受堯之命舜也曰允執厥中舜之命禹
也亦曰惟精惟一允執厥中伊尹之稱湯
曰王懋昭大德建中于民是中者固帝王
心學之精也而皇極之說則未之前聞蓋
自洛書錫於神禹而九疇之數始章武王
訪於箕子而皇極之說始著考之洪範九
punctuated:
間也。不有以奉順之，則無以隆昭事而承其休；不有以駿惠之，則無以廣孝思而揚其烈。是故惟時惟幾，所以敬天也，而祖之神益以安，敬之至也，而亦莫非孝也；善繼善述，所以法祖也，而天之意益以順，孝之達也，而亦莫非敬也。知乎此，則我皇上因時以盡制，敷極以錫民，成功巍然，文章煥然，足以克當天心而增光祖烈者，可以仰窺其萬一矣。請因明問而敬對揚之。
自古帝王繼天立極，莫不有道以相授受。堯之命舜也，曰：「允執厥中。」舜之命禹也，亦曰：「惟精惟一，允執厥中。」伊尹之稱湯，曰：「王懋昭大德，建中于民。」是中者，固帝王心學之精也，而皇極之說則未之前聞。蓋自洛書錫於神禹，而九疇之數始章；武王訪於箕子，而皇極之說始著。考之《洪範》，九
translation_en:
…without interruption. Unless one reverently complies with it, there is no way to exalt the illustrious service rendered to Heaven and receive its blessings; unless one faithfully follows it, there is no way to extend filial devotion and proclaim the ancestors’ achievements. Thus, attending to the proper times and the incipient signs of change is the means of revering Heaven, and thereby the ancestral spirits become ever more at peace. This is reverence at its utmost, yet it is also entirely filial. Skillfully carrying on the ancestors’ purposes and completing their undertakings is the means of taking them as models, and thereby Heaven’s intent is ever more fully fulfilled. This is filial devotion fully realized, yet it is also entirely reverent. Understanding this, we may glimpse a tiny part of how Our Emperor adapts to the times to perfect his institutions and extends the supreme standard to bless the people: his achievements are towering, his civilized accomplishments radiant, fully answering Heaven’s heart and adding luster to the ancestors’ glorious deeds. Allow me, in response to your illuminating question, reverently to expound upon these matters.
Since antiquity, emperors and kings have succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard, invariably transmitting the Way from one to another. When Yao charged Shun, he said: “Sincerely hold fast to the mean.” When Shun charged Yu, he likewise said: “Be discerning, be single-minded, and sincerely hold fast to the mean.” Yi Yin, praising Tang, said: “The king diligently manifested his great virtue and established the mean among the people.” This mean is indeed the essence of the emperors’ and kings’ learning of the mind; yet an explanation of the August Standard had not previously been heard. Only when the Writing of the Luo River was bestowed upon divine Yu did the scheme of the Nine Categories first become manifest; only when King Wu consulted Jizi did the explanation of the August Standard become explicit. Examining the Great Plan, the nine…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
疇以皇極居五蓋疇數有九而五居其中
人君之象也初一爲五行次二爲五事三
爲八政四爲五紀皆皇極之所由立六爲
三德七爲稽疑八爲庶徵九爲福極皆皇
極之所以行此皇極所以必居於五而洪
範一書固人君治天下之大法也乃若以
大訓皇以中訓極則孔穎達牽合之辭而
以九疇配八卦作內篇以釋之者迺蔡沈
氏術數之說其曰惟大作中大則受之實
===
與本文之義有未融也故朱熹氏作皇極
辨以明之曰皇者君也極者標準之謂也
要之皇固有大之義不可外君而言大極
固有中之義不可外準而言中所謂皇建
有極者蓋言大君立此中以爲天下之準
而已自今觀之堯舜之執中執此極也湯
之建中建此極也三聖相承而守一道曰
中曰極其名雖殊其義一也自是而後此
義漸微漢則詩書不事何以窺乎洛範之
punctuated: 疇以皇極居五，蓋疇數有九，而五居其中，人君之象也。初一爲五行，次二爲五事，三爲八政，四爲五紀，皆皇極之所由立；六爲三德，七爲稽疑，八爲庶徵，九爲福極，皆皇極之所以行。此皇極所以必居於五，而洪範一書固人君治天下之大法也。乃若以大訓皇，以中訓極，則孔穎達牽合之辭；而以九疇配八卦，作內篇以釋之者，迺蔡沈氏術數之說。其曰「惟大作中，大則受之」，實與本文之義有未融也。故朱熹氏作《皇極辨》以明之，曰：「皇者，君也；極者，標準之謂也。」要之，皇固有大之義，不可外君而言大；極固有中之義，不可外準而言中。所謂「皇建有極」者，蓋言大君立此中以爲天下之準而已。自今觀之，堯舜之執中，執此極也；湯之建中，建此極也。三聖相承而守一道，曰中曰極，其名雖殊，其義一也。自是而後，此義漸微。漢則詩書不事，何以窺乎洛範之
translation_en:
…among the categories, the Sovereign Standard occupies the fifth position. There are nine categories, and five stands at their center: it represents the ruler. First are the Five Phases; second, the Five Personal Affairs; third, the Eight Affairs of Government; and fourth, the Five Arrangements of Time. These are all means by which the Sovereign Standard is established. Sixth are the Three Virtues; seventh, the Examination of Doubts; eighth, the Various Signs; and ninth, Blessings and Extremities. These are all means by which the Sovereign Standard is put into practice. This is why the Sovereign Standard must occupy the fifth position. The Great Plan is indeed the great method by which a ruler governs the world.

As for glossing huang as “great” and ji as “the mean,” these are forced interpretations by Kong Yingda. Matching the nine categories with the eight trigrams and composing the Inner Chapters to explain them, meanwhile, represents Cai Shen’s numerological teachings. His statement, “Only the great can establish the mean; being great, one receives it” [?], does not fully accord with the meaning of the original text. Thus Zhu Xi wrote his Disquisition on the Sovereign Standard to clarify it, saying: “Huang means the ruler; ji means a standard.” In essence, huang certainly carries the sense of greatness, but one cannot discuss that greatness apart from the ruler; ji certainly carries the sense of centrality, but one cannot discuss that centrality apart from a standard. The expression “The sovereign establishes the standard” simply means that the great ruler establishes this mean as the standard for all under Heaven.

Viewed from the present, when Yao and Shun held fast to the mean, they were holding fast to this standard; when Tang established the mean, he was establishing this standard. These three sages succeeded one another and upheld a single Way. Whether called “the mean” or “the standard,” the names differ, but the meaning is one. Thereafter, this meaning gradually faded. Under the Han, they did not attend to the Classic of Poetry and the Book of Documents; how, then, could they gain insight into what lay within the Luo Writing and the Great Plan…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
精唐則大綱未正何以敘乎彞倫之大至
宋五星雖聚人文未著又焉能識乎龜書
之祕治不古若無怪其然也於乎神龜負
文以開洪範聖人行其道而葆其真洪範
尊皇極以統八疇聖人詳其法而一其道
蓋天以神道設教而其精斯示聖人以至
德合天而其統斯傳爰稽道詮載徵記牒
膺
帝天眷命之隆契帝王心法之要千古而再見
===
者其我
聖祖暨我
皇上乎洪惟
太祖高皇帝應貞元之運當廓清之期汛掃胡
元肇造區宇本之心極以為莫匪爾極之
地者有典章焉炳如日星豈能盡述哉竊
窺其敬
天而隆昭事之忱者則
精誠有錄
punctuated:
精；唐則大綱未正，何以敘乎彞倫之大？至宋，五星雖聚，人文未著，又焉能識乎龜書之祕？治不古若，無怪其然也。於乎！神龜負文以開洪範，聖人行其道而葆其真；洪範尊皇極以統八疇，聖人詳其法而一其道。蓋天以神道設教，而其精斯示；聖人以至德合天，而其統斯傳。爰稽道詮，載徵記牒，膺帝天眷命之隆，契帝王心法之要，千古而再見者，其我聖祖暨我皇上乎！
洪惟太祖高皇帝，應貞元之運，當廓清之期，汛掃胡元，肇造區宇。本之心極，以為莫匪爾極之地者，有典章焉，炳如日星，豈能盡述哉！竊窺其敬天而隆昭事之忱者，則精誠有錄，
translation_en:
…its essence. Under the Tang, the fundamental framework had not been set right: how could the great principles of the constant human relationships be put in order? When it came to the Song, although the five planets gathered, cultural refinement had not yet become manifest: how, then, could they comprehend the secrets of the writing borne by the tortoise? That government fell short of antiquity is therefore no cause for wonder. Ah! The divine tortoise bore the markings that disclosed the Great Plan; the sage put its Way into practice and preserved its authenticity. The Great Plan exalted the August Ultimate to govern the other eight categories; the sage elaborated its methods and unified its Way. Heaven established its teaching through divine workings, and thereby revealed its essence; the sage accorded with Heaven through consummate virtue, and thereby transmitted its succession. Examining expositions of the Way and consulting written records, we find those who received the abundant favor and mandate of Heaven above and grasped the essentials of the sovereigns’ teaching of the mind. Those in whom this has appeared again after a thousand ages—are they not our sagely ancestor and our reigning emperor?
We reverently reflect upon Emperor Taizu Gao: he responded to the cycle of renewal and met the moment for sweeping away disorder. He swept away the non-Chinese Yuan and founded the realm anew. Rooting this in the ultimate standard within his mind, he made the realm a place where “all conform to your ultimate standard.” The statutes and institutions embodying this shine like the sun and stars: how could they all be recounted? Humbly considering his reverence for Heaven and the profound sincerity with which he illustriously served it, we find a record of his utmost sincerity…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
存心省躬有錄以至
大祀諸書無一而不純乎天也嘗召賛善劉三
吾曰朕觀洪範一篇帝王為治之要道也
命儒臣書之揭於
座右朝夕觀覽乃自為註何其深於皇極之
旨而闡千載未發之蘊乎此固
聖祖得天以懋開先之績所以啓佑乎
神孫者也
皇上稟神聖之資值亨嘉之會
纘大合華
執中布度本之心極以為敷錫民極之本者
有典章焉焯如雲漢豈能盡述哉竊窺其
法
祖而嚴時保之翼者則創
玄極殿崇
郊祀禮脩
明倫大典以至
欽天頌諸作無一而不合乎天也嘗
punctuated:
存心、省躬有錄，以至《大祀》諸書，無一而不純乎天也。嘗召賛善劉三吾曰：「朕觀《洪範》一篇，帝王為治之要道也。」命儒臣書之，揭於座右，朝夕觀覽，乃自為註。何其深於皇極之旨，而闡千載未發之蘊乎！此固聖祖得天以懋開先之績，所以啓佑乎神孫者也。
皇上稟神聖之資，值亨嘉之會，纘大合華，執中布度，本之心極，以為敷錫民極之本者，有典章焉，焯如雲漢，豈能盡述哉？竊窺其法祖而嚴時保之翼者，則創玄極殿，崇郊祀禮，脩《明倫大典》，以至《欽天頌》諸作，無一而不合乎天也。嘗
translation_en:
…there are records on preserving the mind and examining oneself, extending to such books as the Great Sacrifice: none fails to accord wholly with Heaven. He once summoned Liu Sanwu, the Admonisher, and said: “I find that the ‘Great Plan’ chapter contains the essential Way by which emperors and kings govern.” He ordered his Confucian ministers to write it out and display it beside his seat. He read it morning and evening, and then composed his own commentary. How profoundly he understood the meaning of the Sovereign Ultimate, bringing to light implications that had remained unexplored for a thousand years! This was indeed how the Sagely Ancestor gained Heaven’s favor and magnificently accomplished his founding work, thereby guiding and protecting his divine descendant.
His Majesty, endowed with divine sagacity and encountering an auspicious convergence of circumstances, continues the great inheritance and unites its splendor [?]. He holds to the Mean and promulgates standards, grounding them in the ultimate standard of his own mind as the basis for bestowing the ultimate standard upon the people. His institutions and regulations shine like the River of Heaven: how could they all be recounted? I humbly observe his emulation of his ancestor and his solemn vigilance in constantly preserving this inheritance. He founded the Hall of the Mysterious Ultimate (Xuanji dian), exalted the rites of the suburban sacrifices, and compiled the Great Compendium for Clarifying Human Relationships (Minglun dadian). These and other works, including the Hymn of Reverence for Heaven (Qintian song), all accord with Heaven. He once…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
製敬一箴并序有曰匪敬弗聚匪一弗純頒
布中外以開示心學何其深於皇極之旨
而契千載不傳之祕乎此固
皇上得天以大丕承之烈所以對揚乎
聖祖者也邇因
三殿及門鼎建告成
綸音渙發更名
正殿及門曰
皇極中曰
===
中極後曰
建極左右閣曰文昭武成左右門曰會極歸極
東西角門曰弘政宣治廼下
明詔曰帝王以至敬事
天必順承因革之
命以達孝尊
祖必善通繼述之權夫
璇題昭揭而
帝制尊崇肅乎體元居正之義
punctuated:
製《敬一箴》并序，有曰：「匪敬弗聚，匪一弗純。」頒布中外，以開示心學。何其深於皇極之旨，而契千載不傳之祕乎！此固皇上得天以大丕承之烈，所以對揚乎聖祖者也。
邇因三殿及門鼎建告成，綸音渙發，更名正殿及門曰皇極，中曰中極，後曰建極，左右閣曰文昭、武成，左右門曰會極、歸極，東西角門曰弘政、宣治。廼下明詔曰：「帝王以至敬事天，必順承因革之命；以達孝尊祖，必善通繼述之權。」夫璇題昭揭，而帝制尊崇，肅乎體元居正之義，
translation_en:
…composed the Admonition on Reverence and Unity (Jingyi zhen), together with a preface, which says: “Without reverence, there is no gathering together; without unity, there is no purity.” He promulgated it throughout the capital and the provinces to elucidate the learning of the mind. How profoundly he understands the meaning of the imperial ultimate, and accords with its secret, left untransmitted for a thousand years! This indeed shows how His Majesty, having gained Heaven’s favor, magnifies the achievement of his grand succession and thereby acknowledges and extols the Sagely Ancestor.
Recently, upon the completion of the rebuilding of the three halls and their gates, an imperial pronouncement was issued far and wide, renaming the principal hall and its gate Huangji (“Imperial Ultimate”), the middle hall Zhongji (“Central Ultimate”), and the rear hall Jianji (“Establishing the Ultimate”). The left and right pavilions were named Wenzhao (“Civil Brilliance”) and Wucheng (“Military Accomplishment”); the left and right gates, Huiji (“Converging upon the Ultimate”) and Guiji (“Returning to the Ultimate”); and the eastern and western corner gates, Hongzheng (“Expanding Governance”) and Xuanzhi (“Diffusing Good Government”). He then issued an illustrious edict: “When emperors and kings serve Heaven with the utmost reverence, they must obediently receive its mandate concerning preservation and change; when they honor their ancestors with consummate filial piety, they must skillfully exercise discretion in carrying forward their predecessors’ undertakings.” Thus, with the jeweled inscriptions prominently displayed and the imperial institutions exalted, solemn is the principle of embodying the primal origin and occupying the proper central position…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
宸翰渙頒而人心趨嚮翕然遵道遵路之規信
大聖人之所作為綦隆於唐虞三代而陋漢唐
宋於不足言也嘗觀古昔聖帝明王莫不
創制立法昭則崇軌以垂示天下黃帝有
合宮之制堯有總章之設舜有四門之闢
周有明堂之建要皆順時酌宜不相沿襲
天之未啓聖人所不先也天之既啓聖人
所不後也或萬世由之而不嫌於尚同或
與時宜之而不嫌於為異此我
===
皇上肇建
殿門爰立名義
徽詞奥旨發
神聖之祕藏
熙號洪猷聳臣民之瞻仰不緣已然之迹而
敬迓其
申錫之庥所以為善事
天也不襲既往之文而潛契其精神之注所以
為善法
punctuated:
宸翰渙頒，而人心趨嚮，翕然遵道遵路之規。信大聖人之所作為，綦隆於唐虞三代，而陋漢唐宋於不足言也。
嘗觀古昔聖帝明王，莫不創制立法，昭則崇軌，以垂示天下。黃帝有合宮之制，堯有總章之設，舜有四門之闢，周有明堂之建，要皆順時酌宜，不相沿襲。天之未啓，聖人所不先也；天之既啓，聖人所不後也。或萬世由之，而不嫌於尚同；或與時宜之，而不嫌於為異。此我皇上肇建殿門，爰立名義，徽詞奥旨，發神聖之祕藏；熙號洪猷，聳臣民之瞻仰。不緣已然之迹，而敬迓其申錫之庥，所以為善事天也；不襲既往之文，而潛契其精神之注，所以為善法
translation_en:
…The imperial calligraphy was widely promulgated, and the hearts of the people turned toward it, united in observing the rule of following the Way and its proper path. Truly, the achievements of the great sage surpass even those of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties in their grandeur, reducing the Han, Tang, and Song to insignificance.
Looking back upon the sage emperors and enlightened kings of antiquity, we find that all established institutions and laws, made their standards manifest, and exalted their guiding principles, handing them down for the instruction of all under Heaven. Huangdi instituted the Joined Palace (Hegong); Yao established the Hall of General Illumination (Zongzhang); Shun opened the four gates; and the Zhou built the Hall of Light (Mingtang). In essence, all followed the needs of their times and weighed what was fitting, rather than simply copying their predecessors. What Heaven has not yet disclosed, the sage does not anticipate; what Heaven has already disclosed, the sage does not lag behind. Sometimes a practice is followed for ten thousand generations, without objection that it prizes conformity; sometimes it is adapted to the needs of the age, without objection that it introduces difference.
Thus our Emperor, in establishing the halls and gates, has assigned them names with fitting meanings. Their splendid wording and profound import reveal the hidden depths of his divine sagacity; their glorious designations and grand purposes inspire the reverent admiration of officials and people. Rather than following the traces of what has already occurred, he reverently welcomes Heaven’s renewed bestowal of blessings: this is how he serves Heaven well. Rather than copying the outward forms of the past, he inwardly accords with the spirit informing them: this is how he excels in emulating…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
祖也蓋其
仁孝誠敬各協于極故
制度考文悉會其精眞所謂無一事而不當
天心無一念而不符
祖德者也
皇上爲億萬年
皇極之主而
三殿之成則
皇上之福爲益盛
===
中天而起運端拱於玄默之尊見悠久之遐軌
焉
明詔之頒天下臣民之福爲益錫率土而咸和
優游於仁壽之域見沕穆之淳風焉推其
原蓋皇極之理天所啟也自神禹敘之至
武王而後傳其學其萬世之聖典乎自
聖祖註之至
皇上而後彰其盛其萬世之大業乎然此猶以
皇極之理言也若夫皇極之數又有可述
punctuated:
祖也。蓋其仁孝誠敬，各協于極，故制度考文，悉會其精，眞所謂無一事而不當天心，無一念而不符祖德者也。皇上爲億萬年皇極之主，而三殿之成，則皇上之福爲益盛，中天而起運，端拱於玄默之尊，見悠久之遐軌焉。明詔之頒，天下臣民之福爲益錫，率土而咸和，優游於仁壽之域，見沕穆之淳風焉。

推其原，蓋皇極之理，天所啟也。自神禹敘之，至武王而後傳其學，其萬世之聖典乎！自聖祖註之，至皇上而後彰其盛，其萬世之大業乎！然此猶以皇極之理言也。若夫皇極之數，又有可述
translation_en:
…the ancestors. His benevolence, filial devotion, sincerity, and reverence each accord with the ultimate standard. Thus, in establishing institutions and examining written forms, he fully comprehends their essential meaning. Truly, it may be said that not one undertaking fails to accord with Heaven’s mind, and not one thought fails to conform to ancestral virtue. Your Majesty is the sovereign embodying the Imperial Ultimate for countless ages. With the completion of the Three Halls, Your Majesty’s blessings grow still more abundant. Rising at the center of Heaven to inaugurate a new cycle, you sit with hands folded in the exalted stillness of profound silence; therein is revealed the far-reaching course of enduring rule. With the promulgation of the illustrious edict, blessings are bestowed still more abundantly upon the officials and people throughout the realm. All within the land live in harmony, at ease in a realm of benevolence and longevity; therein is revealed a pure influence, profound and harmonious.

Tracing this to its source, the principle of the Imperial Ultimate was disclosed by Heaven. From its exposition by the divine Yu to the time of King Wu, when its teaching was transmitted, was this not a sacred canon for all ages? From its annotation by the Sagely Ancestor to the time of Your Majesty, when its splendor was made manifest, was this not a great undertaking for all ages? Yet this still speaks only of the principle of the Imperial Ultimate. As for the numbers of the Imperial Ultimate, there is more that may be related…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
者昔者孔子之贊易也曰太極生兩儀兩
儀生四象四象生八卦又生爲六十四卦
是皆以生數言也太極之生生非
皇極之生生乎厥後宋儒邵雍氏有經世之作
發明皇極二字不一而足凡天地之變化
聖賢之事業萬物之感應罔不盡在其中
焉邵雍氏所言之數非
皇極之全數乎
皇上
===
淵衷睿思無所不包者其理默通於千聖福
祿壽考靡不有備者其數相生於萬年
皇上一考文之間而天下古今之理皆在焉誠
不偶然者也何其盛哉雖然覩河洛者猶
知明德之遠聽漢詔者思見德化之成愚
也竊伏海濱涵濡
聖化久矣
聖謨洋溢昭垂耳目能無一言頌之乎蓋
皇上之建皇極即所以體太極也
punctuated: 者。昔者孔子之贊易也，曰：「太極生兩儀，兩儀生四象，四象生八卦。」又生爲六十四卦，是皆以生數言也。太極之生生，非皇極之生生乎？厥後宋儒邵雍氏有經世之作，發明皇極二字，不一而足。凡天地之變化、聖賢之事業、萬物之感應，罔不盡在其中焉。邵雍氏所言之數，非皇極之全數乎？皇上淵衷睿思，無所不包者，其理默通於千聖；福祿壽考，靡不有備者，其數相生於萬年。皇上一考文之間，而天下古今之理皆在焉，誠不偶然者也，何其盛哉！雖然，覩河洛者猶知明德之遠，聽漢詔者思見德化之成。愚也竊伏海濱，涵濡聖化久矣。聖謨洋溢，昭垂耳目，能無一言頌之乎？蓋皇上之建皇極，即所以體太極也。
translation_en:
…to be recounted. In his commentary on the Changes, Confucius said: “The Supreme Ultimate generates the Two Modes; the Two Modes generate the Four Images; the Four Images generate the Eight Trigrams.” These in turn generate the sixty-four hexagrams. All this speaks of numbers in their generative operation. Is not the ceaseless generation of the Supreme Ultimate also that of the August Ultimate? Later, the Song Confucian scholar Shao Yong composed his Ordering the World, elucidating the two characters “August Ultimate” in more ways than can be enumerated. The transformations of Heaven and Earth, the undertakings of sages and worthies, and the mutual influence and response of all things are wholly encompassed within it. Are not the numbers of which Shao Yong spoke the complete numerical order of the August Ultimate?

Your Majesty’s profound heart and sagacious thought encompass everything: their principles accord silently with those of a thousand sages. Blessings, emoluments, and longevity are all fully present: their numbers generate one another for ten thousand years. In Your Majesty’s single act of examining literary learning, all the principles of the world, past and present, are contained. This is truly no mere coincidence. How magnificent it is!

Yet those who behold the Yellow River and Luo River still recognize the far-reaching power of luminous virtue; those who hear the edicts of the Han long to witness the fulfillment of transformation through virtue. Foolish as I am, dwelling obscurely on the seacoast, I have long been steeped in Your Majesty’s sagely transforming influence. Your sagely counsels flow abundantly, set forth clearly for all to hear and see. Could I fail to offer a word in praise? For Your Majesty’s establishment of the August Ultimate is precisely the means of embodying the Supreme Ultimate.

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
皇上之敷皇極卽所以斂福極也太極體於一
身則與天竝運而恒久不已福極斂於天
下則凝命益固而
壽考無疆故天不愛道而四曜重輝雨暘時若
地不愛寶而四靈畢至海岳效祥百辟欽
承乎
聖敬懋有師師之風萬民優沃於
皇仁丕見熈熈之俗乾坤寧謐中夏乂安此福
極之徵隨昌運以日集
===
皇極之道同天載而難名也所可爲頌如此而
已若夫
皇上心極之蘊淵微至妙豈儒生所能賛一詞
哉謹對
第二問
李廷儀
同考試官教諭王 批 體認親切闡究詳明末段
咏歎朱子閩學得傳可以觀志殆閩士之選者
同考試官教諭唐 批 易與春秋聖人精蘊所
punctuated:
皇上之敷皇極，卽所以斂福極也。太極體於一身，則與天竝運而恒久不已；福極斂於天下，則凝命益固而壽考無疆。故天不愛道，而四曜重輝，雨暘時若；地不愛寶，而四靈畢至，海岳效祥。百辟欽承乎聖敬，懋有師師之風；萬民優沃於皇仁，丕見熈熈之俗。乾坤寧謐，中夏乂安。此福極之徵，隨昌運以日集；皇極之道，同天載而難名也。所可爲頌，如此而已。若夫皇上心極之蘊，淵微至妙，豈儒生所能賛一詞哉？謹對。

第二問
李廷儀

同考試官教諭王批：「體認親切，闡究詳明。末段咏歎朱子閩學得傳，可以觀志，殆閩士之選者。」

同考試官教諭唐批：「易與春秋，聖人精蘊所
translation_en:
His Majesty’s dissemination of the Supreme Standard is precisely how he gathers the utmost blessings. When the Supreme Ultimate is embodied in his own person, he moves in concert with Heaven, enduring without cease; when the utmost blessings are gathered throughout the realm, the Mandate is consolidated ever more firmly, and his longevity knows no bounds. Thus Heaven does not withhold its Way: the four luminaries shine with renewed brilliance, and rain and sunshine come in due season. Earth does not withhold its treasures: the four numinous creatures all arrive, and the seas and mountains manifest auspicious signs. The assembled lords reverently uphold his sagely reverence, diligently cultivating the practice of learning from one another. The myriad people are abundantly nourished by imperial benevolence, conspicuously displaying a joyous way of life. Heaven and Earth are tranquil, and the central realm is well governed and at peace. These signs of utmost blessings gather daily with the flourishing fortunes of the age; the Way of the Supreme Standard, like Heaven’s workings, is difficult to describe. This is all that can be offered in praise. As for the profound, subtle, and supremely wondrous significance of the ultimate standard within His Majesty’s heart, how could a Confucian scholar contribute even a word in its praise? Respectfully submitted in reply.

Second Question
Li Tingyi

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “His understanding is intimate and precise, and his exposition and inquiry are detailed and clear. The closing passage celebrates the transmission of Master Zhu’s Fujian learning, revealing the writer’s aspirations. He is surely among the finest scholars of Fujian.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: “The Book of Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals are where the sages’ most refined and profound insights…”

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
寓秦漢而下儒者惟朱子啓蒙綱目獨得其宗此作發揮
殆盡取之
考試官教諭冓批明贍得體錄之
考試官教授王批發明朱子得易春秋之
傳意詳盡
善學易者精於理而不偏於數善治春秋
者斷以義而不泥於文數者易之具也造
化之精蘊不與焉文者春秋之詞也王道
之大權不與焉學易而不能神會其理則
===
聖人心法之精滯而弗達學春秋而不能
深惟其義則聖人經世之典晦而弗宣惟
夫不偏於數而洞徹乎至理之原不泥於
文而獨觀夫取舍之極然後道法各當其
可經傳不失其則以之出入造化發揮陰
陽則可以遠紹乎四聖之緒以之進退古
今表裏人物則可以上翼乎一王之典而
易與春秋始大明於天下此朱熹啓蒙綱
目之作所以大有功於聖人也請因明問
punctuated:
寓。秦漢而下，儒者惟朱子《啓蒙》《綱目》獨得其宗，此作發揮殆盡，取之。

考試官教諭冓批：明贍得體，錄之。

考試官教授王批：發明朱子得《易》《春秋》之傳，意詳盡。

善學《易》者，精於理而不偏於數；善治《春秋》者，斷以義而不泥於文。數者，《易》之具也，造化之精蘊不與焉；文者，《春秋》之詞也，王道之大權不與焉。學《易》而不能神會其理，則聖人心法之精滯而弗達；學《春秋》而不能深惟其義，則聖人經世之典晦而弗宣。惟夫不偏於數而洞徹乎至理之原，不泥於文而獨觀夫取舍之極，然後道法各當其可，經傳不失其則。以之出入造化，發揮陰陽，則可以遠紹乎四聖之緒；以之進退古今，表裏人物，則可以上翼乎一王之典。而《易》與《春秋》始大明於天下，此朱熹《啓蒙》《綱目》之作所以大有功於聖人也。請因明問，
translation_en:
…are lodged. Among scholars from the Qin and Han onward, only Master Zhu, in his Introduction to the Study of the Changes and Outline and Details, grasped their essential purport. This essay expounds it almost exhaustively. Accept it.

Examiner Gou [?], Instructor, comments: Clear, ample, and appropriate in form. Include it.

Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: It elucidates how Master Zhu inherited the transmission of the Book of Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals; its treatment is detailed and exhaustive.

Those who study the Book of Changes well penetrate its principles without becoming unduly attached to numbers; those who study the Spring and Autumn Annals well judge by moral meaning without becoming constrained by wording. Numbers are the instruments of the Changes; the profound subtleties of creation and transformation are not contained in them. Wording constitutes the language of the Spring and Autumn Annals; the great discretionary authority of the kingly Way is not contained in it. If one studies the Changes but cannot intuitively apprehend its principles, the essence of the sages’ method of cultivating the mind remains obstructed and inaccessible. If one studies the Spring and Autumn Annals but cannot ponder its moral meaning deeply, the sages’ canon for ordering the world remains obscure and unexpounded. Only by avoiding undue attachment to numbers and thoroughly penetrating the source of ultimate principle, and by avoiding fixation on wording and discerning for oneself the ultimate grounds of acceptance and rejection, can the Way and its methods each find their proper application, and the classics and commentaries retain their standards. Through this, one may range through creation and transformation and elucidate yin and yang, thereby carrying forward the distant legacy of the four sages. Through this, one may weigh advancement and demotion in antiquity and the present, and examine people and affairs outwardly and inwardly, thereby lending support to the canon of the true king. Only then do the Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals become fully illuminated throughout the world. This is why Zhu Xi’s composition of the Introduction to the Study of the Changes and Outline and Details rendered such great service to the sages. title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
而敬陳之昔者孔子有感於易道之中興
也作十翼以承三聖之統陰陽消息之奧
辭占象變之微學之而韋編三絕數年而
始無太過甚矣易道之大也然其所以通
神明之德體天地之撰以發明千聖不傳
之祕者豈無所本哉蓋自龍馬負而河圖
出乾坤縱而六子橫先天之學所以爲萬
事萬物之本而後天特效法耳孔子之易
主於是耳則其自二而四自四而八自八
===
而十六自十六而三十二自三十二而六
十四者乃太極自然之妙用有莫知其所
以然者聖人何庸心也楊雄司馬光之流
不識聖人作易之意氣朔日星之說見於
子雲之太玄而方部州家有五無十何以
成變化而行鬼神一歲二首歸餘於養何
以定周天之度而當期之日此所謂以艱
深文淺近蘇洵詆之是已虛氣之說固潛
虛之主本若曰虛者物之府也氣者生之
punctuated: 而敬陳之。昔者孔子有感於易道之中興也，作十翼以承三聖之統。陰陽消息之奧，辭占象變之微，學之而韋編三絕，數年而始無太過，甚矣，易道之大也！然其所以通神明之德，體天地之撰，以發明千聖不傳之祕者，豈無所本哉？蓋自龍馬負而河圖出，乾坤縱而六子橫，先天之學所以爲萬事萬物之本，而後天特效法耳。孔子之易主於是耳。則其自二而四，自四而八，自八而十六，自十六而三十二，自三十二而六十四者，乃太極自然之妙用，有莫知其所以然者，聖人何庸心也？楊雄、司馬光之流，不識聖人作易之意。氣朔日星之說，見於子雲之《太玄》，而方部州家，有五無十，何以成變化而行鬼神？一歲二首，歸餘於養，何以定周天之度而當期之日？此所謂以艱深文淺近，蘇洵詆之是已。虛氣之說，固《潛虛》之主本。若曰：「虛者，物之府也；氣者，生之
translation_en:
…and respectfully set it forth. In former times, Confucius, moved by the revival of the Way of the Changes, composed the Ten Wings to carry on the tradition of the three sages. Such are the profundities of yin and yang waxing and waning, and the subtleties of the statements, divinations, images, and transformations, that in studying them he wore through the leather bindings three times; only after several years did he begin to avoid major errors. How vast indeed is the Way of the Changes! Yet could his means of comprehending the powers of spiritual beings, embodying the workings of Heaven and Earth, and elucidating secrets that a thousand sages had not transmitted have lacked a foundation? When the dragon-horse bore its markings and the River Chart appeared, Qian and Kun were arranged vertically and the six children horizontally. The learning of Prior Heaven thus provides the foundation of all affairs and all things; Later Heaven merely follows its pattern. This alone was the guiding principle of Confucius’s Changes. Its progression from two to four, four to eight, eight to sixteen, sixteen to thirty-two, and thirty-two to sixty-four is the wondrous, spontaneous operation of the Supreme Ultimate. There is something here whose reason for being cannot be known: what need had the sage to contrive it deliberately?

Men such as Yang Xiong and Sima Guang did not understand the sage’s intention in making the Changes. Explanations of seasonal qi, new moons, the sun, and the stars appear in Ziyun’s [Yang Xiong’s] Supreme Mystery, yet its divisions into directions, regions, provinces, and families have five but lack ten. How could these accomplish transformations and set ghosts and spirits in motion? With “two heads in one year” [?], and the remainder assigned to “Nurturing,” how could it establish the degrees of the celestial circuit and correspond to the days of a full year? This is what is meant by dressing up the shallow and commonplace in difficult and abstruse language. Su Xun was right to condemn it.

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
戶也體質性神名事行命皆起於此似有
得於五行生成之數而以行準卦變以解
命準彖象是亦王通之見也一代名儒如
君實且猶妄謬若此則休咎之徵子母之
言又何責於劉更生之陋也此非所謂偏
於數而不精乎理者耶朱熹憤末學支離
之病而作啓蒙自圖書卦畫以迄蓍策變
占凡四篇之中原始要終探玄索隱所以
爲開物成務之具者精矣自今觀之始之
===
以河圖見八卦之所由肇先天之經也繼
之以洛書見九疇之所由成先天之緯也
太極兩儀四象八卦從中而起先天之位
也分二掛一揲四歸奇由中而衍先天之
策也三同二異以明其對待之體圓星方
土以擬其生出之原無極之前陰含陽也
而自姤至坤者其機深有象之後陽分陰
也而自復至乾者其體隱乾坤立天地之
準坎離互陰陽之根造化之所闔闢日月
punctuated:
戶也。體、質、性、神、名、事、行、命，皆起於此。」似有得於五行生成之數，而以行準卦變，以解命準彖象，是亦王通之見也。一代名儒如君實，且猶妄謬若此，則休咎之徵、子母之言，又何責於劉更生之陋也？此非所謂偏於數而不精乎理者耶？朱熹憤末學支離之病而作《啓蒙》，自圖書卦畫以迄蓍策變占，凡四篇之中，原始要終，探玄索隱，所以爲開物成務之具者精矣。
自今觀之，始之以河圖，見八卦之所由肇，先天之經也；繼之以洛書，見九疇之所由成，先天之緯也。太極、兩儀、四象、八卦，從中而起，先天之位也；分二、掛一、揲四、歸奇，由中而衍，先天之策也。三同二異，以明其對待之體；圓星方土，以擬其生出之原。無極之前，陰含陽也，而自姤至坤者，其機深；有象之後，陽分陰也，而自復至乾者，其體隱。乾坤立天地之準，坎離互陰陽之根，造化之所闔闢，日月
translation_en:
…the gateway. Form, substance, nature, spirit, designation, affairs, conduct, and destiny all arise from this.” This seems to grasp something of the numbers through which the Five Phases generate and complete things. Yet taking “conduct” as corresponding to hexagram changes, and explanations of “destiny” as corresponding to the Judgments and Images, is also Wang Tong’s view. If even Junshi [Sima Guang], a renowned Confucian scholar of his age, could fall into such unfounded errors, why further reproach Liu Gengsheng for the inadequacy of his signs of good and ill fortune and his statements about mother and child? Is this not what is meant by being partial to numbers without a thorough understanding of principle? Indignant at the fragmented understanding afflicting latter-day scholars, Zhu Xi wrote the Introduction to the Study of the Changes (Qimeng). From the River Chart and Luo Writing and the drawing of hexagrams to milfoil stalks, changes, and divination, its four chapters trace beginnings and comprehend outcomes, probe mysteries and seek out what is hidden. It is an exquisite instrument for disclosing the nature of things and bringing undertakings to completion.
Viewed now, it begins with the River Chart, showing how the eight trigrams originated: this is the warp of the Prior Heaven arrangement. It proceeds with the Luo Writing, showing how the Nine Categories were formed: this is the weft of the Prior Heaven arrangement. The Supreme Ultimate, the Two Modes, the Four Images, and the eight trigrams arise from the center: these are the positions of Prior Heaven. Dividing the stalks into two, setting one aside, counting them in fours, and gathering the remainders unfold from the center: these are the milfoil operations of Prior Heaven. “Three alike and two different” elucidates its structure of paired opposites; “round stars and square earth” models the source of its generation [?]. Before the Non-Ultimate, yin contains yang, and the workings of the sequence from Gou to Kun are profound; after images exist, yang differentiates yin, and the underlying structure of the sequence from Fu to Qian is hidden. Qian and Kun establish the standard for Heaven and Earth; Kan and Li reciprocally embody the roots of yin and yang. That through which the creative transformations close and open, and the sun and moon…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
之所出入春夏秋冬晦朔弦望晝夜長短
行度盈縮何莫非先天之運也自此乾坤
交而為泰坎離交而為既濟固後天流行
之用要皆因先天已成之體而縱橫之耳
是故發易書之蘊者啟蒙也盡聖人之蘊
者先天也故曰先天圖心法也又曰圖雖
無文天地萬物之理盡在其中至此而天
地鬼神之奧不可以探其微哉昔者孔子
有感於大雅之不作也因魯史以寓一王
===
之法惇典庸禮之權命德討罪之義固有
晉楚不能同其史游夏不能贊其辭甚矣
春秋之難也然其所以拯頹綱以繼三五
鼓芳風而扇遊塵以正二百四十二年南
面之事者豈無其要哉蓋自周道衰而乾
綱墜禮樂壞而倫紀斁尊周之義汩沒於
亂臣賊子之害陵夷非一日矣夫子之作
春秋正為此耳則其治在諸侯治在五霸
治在大夫而有隱桓莊閔之春秋有僖文
punctuated:
之所出入，春夏秋冬，晦朔弦望，晝夜長短，行度盈縮，何莫非先天之運也？自此乾坤交而為泰，坎離交而為既濟，固後天流行之用，要皆因先天已成之體而縱橫之耳。是故發易書之蘊者，啟蒙也；盡聖人之蘊者，先天也。故曰：「先天圖，心法也。」又曰：「圖雖無文，天地萬物之理盡在其中。」至此而天地鬼神之奧，不可以探其微哉？
昔者孔子有感於大雅之不作也，因魯史以寓一王之法。惇典庸禮之權，命德討罪之義，固有晉楚不能同其史，游夏不能贊其辭。甚矣，春秋之難也！然其所以拯頹綱以繼三五，鼓芳風而扇遊塵，以正二百四十二年南面之事者，豈無其要哉？蓋自周道衰而乾綱墜，禮樂壞而倫紀斁，尊周之義汩沒於亂臣賊子之害，陵夷非一日矣。夫子之作春秋，正為此耳。則其治在諸侯，治在五霸，治在大夫，而有隱桓莊閔之春秋，有僖文
translation_en:
…through which they emerge and enter; spring, summer, autumn, and winter; the moon’s last day, new moon, quarters, and full moon; the varying lengths of day and night; and the advances and retardations of celestial motions—what among these is not the operation of the Prior Heaven? From this, Qian and Kun unite to form Tai, and Kan and Li unite to form Jiji. These are indeed the functions of the flowing activity of the Posterior Heaven, yet all simply draw upon the already established structure of the Prior Heaven and deploy it in every direction. Thus, what reveals the hidden meaning of the Book of Changes is the Introduction to the Study of the Changes (Yixue qimeng); what fully expresses the sages’ hidden meaning is the Prior Heaven. Hence it is said: “The Diagram of the Prior Heaven is the method of the mind.” It is also said: “Although the diagram has no words, the principles of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things are all contained within it.” Having reached this point, can one not probe the subtleties of the mysteries of Heaven, Earth, ghosts, and spirits?
Long ago, Confucius, moved by the disappearance of the great norms of cultivated order, drew upon the annals of Lu to embody the laws of a true king. In its authoritative judgments concerning the strengthening of established norms and the application of ritual, and its principles for rewarding virtue and punishing wrongdoing, neither the annals of Jin nor those of Chu could equal this history; neither Ziyou nor Zixia could add a word to its language. How difficult indeed is the Spring and Autumn Annals! Yet could there be no essential principle by which it rescued the collapsing order and carried forward the legacy of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, stirred a fragrant moral breeze and swept away drifting dust, and set right the affairs of rulers over two hundred and forty-two years? Since the Way of Zhou declined and Heaven’s governing order collapsed, rites and music had fallen into ruin, and human relationships and their ordering principles had decayed. The principle of honoring Zhou was submerged beneath the harm wrought by rebellious ministers and treacherous sons. This decline had continued for far longer than a single day. It was precisely for this reason that the Master composed the Spring and Autumn Annals. Thus, governing authority lay with the regional lords, with the Five Hegemons, and with the grandees; accordingly, there were the Spring and Autumn Annals of Dukes Yin, Huan, Zhuang, and Min, and those of Dukes Xi and Wen…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
宣成之春秋有昭襄定哀之春秋者固天
時人事之適然有不可得而隱諱者聖人
何庸心也左丘明穀梁赤公羊高之流不
識聖人春秋之義丘明受經於仲尼而好
惡之同者僅一二焉然或先經以始事而
夏正周正之辨不能闕其疑或後經以終
義而大夫告老之後不當書其卒此所謂
善於理而失之誣鄭玄評之是已赤高之
傳則又有下於是者觀其以衛輒為尊祖
===
是天性可得而戕也以祭仲為行權是神
器可得而窺也或以不納子糾為內惡或
以諸侯之溺愛為合正清而婉者不免失
之短辨而裁者不免失之俗范甯譏之是
已超出七氏如三傳且猶紕繆若是則災
異之傳子母之論又何取於劉子駿之通
也此非所謂泥於文而不斷以義者耶朱
熹慨舊史是非之亂而作綱目自威烈之
紀以迄五季之衰凡千三百餘年之間宏
punctuated:
宣成之春秋，有昭襄定哀之春秋者，固天時人事之適然，有不可得而隱諱者，聖人何庸心也？左丘明、穀梁赤、公羊高之流，不識聖人春秋之義。丘明受經於仲尼，而好惡之同者僅一二焉。然或先經以始事，而夏正周正之辨不能闕其疑；或後經以終義，而大夫告老之後不當書其卒。此所謂善於理而失之誣，鄭玄評之是已。赤、高之傳，則又有下於是者。觀其以衛輒為尊祖，是天性可得而戕也；以祭仲為行權，是神器可得而窺也。或以不納子糾為內惡，或以諸侯之溺愛為合正。清而婉者不免失之短，辨而裁者不免失之俗，范甯譏之是已。超出七氏如三傳，且猶紕繆若是，則災異之傳、子母之論，又何取於劉子駿之通也？此非所謂泥於文而不斷以義者耶？
朱熹慨舊史是非之亂而作綱目，自威烈之紀以迄五季之衰，凡千三百餘年之間，宏
translation_en:
…the Spring and Autumn Annals of Dukes Xuan and Cheng, and the Spring and Autumn Annals of Dukes Zhao, Xiang, Ding, and Ai: these divisions arose naturally from the circumstances of the times and human affairs, containing things that could not be concealed or glossed over. What need had the sage to impose his own intentions?
Men such as Zuo Qiuming, Guliang Chi, and Gongyang Gao did not understand the principles of the sage’s Spring and Autumn Annals. Qiuming received the classic from Zhongni [Confucius], yet his approvals and disapprovals agreed with the sage’s in only one or two instances. Sometimes he places his account before the corresponding entry in the classic to explain an event’s beginnings, yet fails to leave unresolved the uncertainties concerning the distinction between the Xia and Zhou calendars. Sometimes he places it after the entry to complete its meaning, yet records the deaths of grandees when these should not have been recorded after their retirement. This is what is meant by being adept at explaining principles but erring through misrepresentation. Zheng Xuan’s assessment was correct.
The commentaries of Chi and Gao contain things still worse. Consider their treatment of Zhe of Wei as honoring his grandfather: this would permit the destruction of natural familial affections. Their treatment of Ji Zhong as exercising discretion would permit coveting the sacred vessel of sovereign power. Sometimes they treat the failure to admit Zijiu as an evil committed within the state; sometimes they treat the feudal lords’ excessive affection as conforming to proper principles. The commentary that is clear and subtle cannot escape the fault of narrowness; the one that distinguishes and judges cannot escape the fault of vulgarity. Fan Ning’s criticism was correct. Even the Three Commentaries, which surpass the seven other schools, contain errors such as these. What, then, is there to commend in Liu Zijun’s comprehensive learning concerning the traditions of disasters and anomalies and the theories of mother and child [?]? Is this not what is meant by clinging to the wording without judging according to principle?
