title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
綱大曰隱義微文所以明屬辭比事之意
者悉矣自今觀之詳書甲子則歲周而天
道明春秋之繫王於天也特書正統則統
正而人道定春秋之大一統也有正例以
書沿革興廢之類有變例以書善惡勸戒
之宜一春秋之經也或追言其始而遂及
其終或詳陳其事而備載其言一春秋之
傳也秦楚韓魏之僭別猶夫吳越之誅宋
齊梁陳之分卑是即五覇之罪三國疑無
===
漢矣而昭烈之尊所以排陳壽之妄廬陵
疑無唐矣而中宗之帝所以斥周紀之訛
莽楊雄以發其美新之邪晉陶潛以彰其
恥宋之節他如湔托始之餘辜抑元經之
帝魏五胡雲擾深究其源南北分爭悉謹
其始何莫非春秋尊周之意也雖其出入
遷固而其類不一表裏范馬而其辭不同
要之諸史之所折衷率皆以春秋尊周之
意而裁成之耳是知得春秋之法者綱目
punctuated: 綱大曰，隱義微文，所以明屬辭比事之意者悉矣。自今觀之，詳書甲子，則歲周而天道明，春秋之繫王於天也；特書正統，則統正而人道定，春秋之大一統也。有正例以書沿革興廢之類，有變例以書善惡勸戒之宜，一春秋之經也；或追言其始而遂及其終，或詳陳其事而備載其言，一春秋之傳也。秦楚韓魏之僭別，猶夫吳越之誅；宋齊梁陳之分卑，是即五覇之罪。三國疑無漢矣，而昭烈之尊，所以排陳壽之妄；廬陵疑無唐矣，而中宗之帝，所以斥周紀之訛。莽楊雄，以發其美新之邪；晉陶潛，以彰其恥宋之節。他如湔托始之餘辜，抑《元經》之帝魏，五胡雲擾，深究其源，南北分爭，悉謹其始，何莫非春秋尊周之意也？雖其出入遷固，而其類不一；表裏范馬，而其辭不同。要之，諸史之所折衷，率皆以春秋尊周之意而裁成之耳。是知得春秋之法者，《綱目》
translation_en:
…its broad outlines and major entries [?], its concealed judgments and subtle wording—all fully elucidate the purpose of arranging statements and juxtaposing events. Viewed from the present, its detailed recording of the cyclical dates makes the cycle of years and the Way of Heaven clear: this follows the Spring and Autumn Annals in linking the king to Heaven. Its explicit designation of the legitimate succession rectifies that succession and establishes the human order: this follows the Annals in honoring unified rule. It has regular conventions for recording continuity and change, rise and fall, and exceptional conventions suited to recording good and evil, encouragement and admonition; in this it is wholly at one with the canonical text of the Annals. Sometimes it traces an affair back to its beginning and follows it through to its conclusion; sometimes it recounts events in detail and fully records the words spoken. In this it is wholly at one with the commentaries on the Annals.

Its distinction of Qin, Chu, Han, and Wei as usurping states resembles the condemnation of Wu and Yue; its demotion of Song, Qi, Liang, and Chen as divided regimes corresponds to the condemnation of the Five Hegemons. In the Three Kingdoms period, one might suppose that Han no longer existed; yet its honoring of Zhaolie refutes Chen Shou’s false account. With the Prince of Luling, one might suppose that Tang no longer existed; yet its recognition of Zhongzong as emperor rejects the error of the annals of Zhou. By assigning Yang Xiong to Wang Mang’s regime, it exposes the perversity of his Praise of the Xin; by assigning Tao Qian to Jin, it makes manifest his integrity in regarding service to Song as shameful. Other examples include clearing away the lingering faults of the choice of a narrative starting point [?] and rejecting the recognition of Wei’s rulers as emperors in the Fundamental Classic (Yuan jing). When the Five Hu peoples rose in tumult like gathering clouds, it investigated the origins deeply; when north and south divided and contended, it treated every beginning with care. How could any of this fail to embody the Annals’ intention of honoring Zhou?

Although it draws upon and departs from Sima Qian and Ban Gu, its categories are not identical to theirs; although it complements Fan Ye and Sima Guang, its wording differs. In essence, when weighing the various histories, it consistently shapes its judgments according to the Annals’ intention of honoring Zhou. Thus we know that the work which has grasped the method of the Spring and Autumn Annals is the Outline and Details (Gangmu)…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
也該聖人之法者尊周也故曰春秋二三
策萬古開羣蒙又曰定褒貶於往前示勸
懲於來世此綱目之所以繼獲麟而作也
至此而史外傳心之要典不可以究其旨
哉夫易心法之精也而啓蒙發其蘊春秋
經世之典也而綱目嗣其統是前乎千百
世之上而集羣聖之大成者孔子一人而
已後乎千百世之下而集諸儒之大成者
朱熹一人而已昔韓宣子適楚見易象與
===
魯春秋曰周禮盡在魯矣乃今知周公之
德與周之所以王朱熹閩人也其有功於
聖門彰彰如是百世之下當必有神會而
私淑之如宣子之所云者愚生何足以與
於此
第三問
周良賓
同考試官教諭陳批
楊搉古循吏為守令法程而揀任責成之議最為切當有用之學也
punctuated:
也。該聖人之法者，尊周也。故曰：「春秋二三策，萬古開羣蒙。」又曰：「定褒貶於往前，示勸懲於來世。」此綱目之所以繼獲麟而作也。至此而史外傳心之要典，不可以究其旨哉？夫易，心法之精也，而啓蒙發其蘊；春秋，經世之典也，而綱目嗣其統。是前乎千百世之上，而集羣聖之大成者，孔子一人而已；後乎千百世之下，而集諸儒之大成者，朱熹一人而已。昔韓宣子適楚，見易象與魯春秋，曰：「周禮盡在魯矣！乃今知周公之德與周之所以王。」朱熹，閩人也，其有功於聖門，彰彰如是。百世之下，當必有神會而私淑之，如宣子之所云者。愚生何足以與於此！

第三問
周良賓

同考試官教諭陳批：
楊搉古循吏，為守令法程，而揀任責成之議，最為切當，有用之學也。
translation_en:
…is so. What encompasses the sage’s method is honoring Zhou. Thus it is said: “The few bamboo slips of the Spring and Autumn Annals dispel the ignorance of multitudes for all ages.” It is also said: “Fix praise and blame upon the past; show encouragement and admonition to generations to come.” This is why the Outline and Details (Gangmu) was composed to continue the record after the capture of the qilin. At this point, can we not fathom the purport of this essential classic, which transmits the teaching of the mind beyond the recording of history? The Changes embodies the quintessence of the teaching of the mind, and the Introduction to the Study of the Changes (Qimeng) reveals its hidden meanings. The Spring and Autumn Annals is a classic for ordering the world, and the Outline and Details carries on its tradition. Thus, looking back through hundreds and thousands of generations, Confucius alone brought the achievements of all the sages to their culmination; hundreds and thousands of generations afterward, Zhu Xi alone brought the achievements of the Confucian scholars to their culmination. Formerly, Han Xuanzi traveled to Chu [?] and saw the Images of the Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals of Lu. He said: “The rites of Zhou are all preserved in Lu! Only now do I understand the virtue of the Duke of Zhou and how Zhou attained kingship.” Zhu Xi was a man of Min, and his contributions to the school of the sages are as manifest as this. A hundred generations hence, there will surely be those who comprehend him in spirit and take him as their teacher through his surviving teachings, much as Xuanzi’s words suggest. How could an ignorant student such as I be worthy to join their ranks!

Third Policy Question
Zhou Liangbin

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor:
He surveys [?] the exemplary administrators of antiquity as models for prefects and county magistrates. His discussion of selecting and appointing them and holding them accountable for results is especially pertinent and sound. This is learning of practical use.

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭朱批歷評守令之善而歸重
愛民詞意懇切是有先憂之志者
考試官教諭𠦬批深得置守令本意
考試官教授王批議論確當
君德莫大於格天求端於民者憲天之極
功也臣道莫大於尊君任勞於民者敬君
之急務也何則天人一理而民也者固天
心之所視以為依違也君臣一體而臣也
者固君身之所視以為勞逸也自夫一體
===
之義不明則為臣者惟知便己以自逸而
於代君綏民之意有所不切自夫一理之
義未孚則為君者雖欲體天以宣化而於
得人共治之願有所不達是故善言天者
不求之天而求之民民心悅而天意格矣
善事君者欲求諸民而先求諸心吾心盡
而君心逸矣君臣一心事使一道至德協
和於上下嘉氣徧蒸於海宇此固惇大成
裕之治而非藻飾於事功取必於智為者
punctuated:
同考試官教諭朱批：歷評守令之善，而歸重愛民，詞意懇切，是有先憂之志者。
同考試官教諭𠦬批：深得置守令本意。
考試官教授王批：議論確當。
君德莫大於格天，求端於民者，憲天之極功也。臣道莫大於尊君，任勞於民者，敬君之急務也。何則？天人一理，而民也者，固天心之所視以為依違也；君臣一體，而臣也者，固君身之所視以為勞逸也。自夫一體之義不明，則為臣者惟知便己以自逸，而於代君綏民之意有所不切；自夫一理之義未孚，則為君者雖欲體天以宣化，而於得人共治之願有所不達。是故善言天者，不求之天，而求之民，民心悅而天意格矣；善事君者，欲求諸民，而先求諸心，吾心盡而君心逸矣。君臣一心，事使一道，至德協和於上下，嘉氣徧蒸於海宇。此固惇大成裕之治，而非藻飾於事功、取必於智為者
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: He reviews in turn the merits of prefects and magistrates, placing greatest weight on loving the people. His language and meaning are earnest: here is someone resolved to be the first to take on worries.
Comment by Associate Examiner 𠦬 [?], Instructor: He has deeply grasped the original purpose of appointing prefects and magistrates.
Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: The argument is sound and appropriate.
No virtue of a ruler is greater than reaching Heaven; taking the people as one’s starting point is the highest achievement in following Heaven’s example. No duty of a minister is greater than honoring his ruler; undertaking toil for the people is the most urgent task in revering the ruler. Why is this? Heaven and humanity share one principle, and it is by looking to the people that Heaven determines whether to favor or withhold its favor. Ruler and ministers form one body, and it is upon his ministers that the ruler depends for his own toil or ease. When the meaning of forming one body is unclear, ministers know only how to suit their own convenience and secure their own ease, lacking earnest commitment to bringing peace to the people on the ruler’s behalf. When the meaning of sharing one principle has not won acceptance, the ruler, though wishing to embody Heaven and spread its transforming influence, cannot fully realize his desire to obtain worthy men with whom to govern.
Thus, those who speak well of Heaven seek understanding of it not in Heaven but among the people: when the people’s hearts are pleased, Heaven’s favor is attained. Those who serve their ruler well wish to seek the answer among the people, but first seek it within their own hearts: when I devote my heart fully, the ruler’s heart is at ease. Ruler and ministers share one heart; serving and directing follow one Way. Supreme virtue brings harmony between those above and below, and auspicious influences spread throughout the realm. This is indeed government in which generosity and breadth bring abundance, and cannot be compared with that of those who embellish their achievements and seek assured success through clever contrivance…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
之可同日語也知乎此則可對揚我
皇上用人安民之盛心而且可以尚論於邈古
之治矣執事發策至此乃復備及守令愚
生也晚且方蒲伏山谷誠無達於公府之
制而不足以辱教命之臨也然嘗遐覽載
籍窮探遠哲而有得於古之重守令者焉
請爲執事先詳往古而後及今之所當力
行者可乎唐虞以上九官十有二牧克宅
克俊其時朝無遺政野有餘麻穆穆雍雍
===
卓乎尚矣周室頒爵分土惟三公侯伯子
男各食采地官安於職民樂其業世祚綿
遠享八百有道之長非無自也自夫罷侯
置守而守之名立計戶爲令而令之制詳
則守令者固古之公侯伯子男之任也然
其馭貴也差以降其詔祿也差以薄而其
任民也則差以親矣夫其視民也親則凡
有志於建宣惠之績者易達而不壅其敘
位也廉則凡有志於覬高朗之澤者易堅
punctuated:
之可同日語也。知乎此，則可對揚我皇上用人安民之盛心，而且可以尚論於邈古之治矣。執事發策至此，乃復備及守令。愚生也晚，且方蒲伏山谷，誠無達於公府之制，而不足以辱教命之臨也。然嘗遐覽載籍，窮探遠哲，而有得於古之重守令者焉。請爲執事先詳往古，而後及今之所當力行者，可乎？
唐虞以上，九官十有二牧，克宅克俊，其時朝無遺政，野有餘麻，穆穆雍雍，卓乎尚矣。周室頒爵分土，惟三公侯伯子男，各食采地，官安於職，民樂其業，世祚綿遠，享八百有道之長，非無自也。自夫罷侯置守而守之名立，計戶爲令而令之制詳，則守令者固古之公侯伯子男之任也。然其馭貴也差以降，其詔祿也差以薄，而其任民也則差以親矣。夫其視民也親，則凡有志於建宣惠之績者易達而不壅；其敘位也廉，則凡有志於覬高朗之澤者易堅
translation_en:
…can be spoken of in the same breath. Understanding this, we can fittingly respond to and proclaim Our Emperor’s great resolve to employ worthy men and bring peace to the people, and can further discuss the government of distant antiquity. Your Honor’s policy question, having reached this point, also treats prefects and magistrates in detail. I, an unworthy student born late, am still crawling about among the mountains and valleys. I truly have no understanding of the institutions of public administration and am unworthy of the instruction you have graciously bestowed. Yet I have surveyed the written records of the distant past and thoroughly investigated the ancient sages, gaining some understanding of the importance the ancients attached to prefects and magistrates. May I first explain the past in detail for Your Honor, and then turn to what should now be vigorously put into practice?
In the age of Tang and Yu and earlier, the nine officials and twelve regional governors were able to occupy their posts and display their excellence. At that time, no affairs of government were neglected at court, and there was surplus hemp in the countryside [?]. Majestic and harmonious, that age was supremely exalted! The house of Zhou conferred ranks and apportioned territory: the three dukes [?], marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons each drew sustenance from their fiefs. Officials were secure in their posts, and the people took pleasure in their occupations. The dynasty’s allotted span extended far into the future, enjoying eight hundred years of government according to the Way; this was not without cause. Once the feudal lords were abolished and prefects appointed, the designation of prefect became established; once magistrates were appointed according to household numbers, the system of magistracies became fully defined. Thus prefects and magistrates indeed bore the responsibilities of the ancient dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons. Yet the noble standing accorded them was correspondingly lower, their allotted stipends correspondingly smaller, and their responsibility for the people correspondingly more immediate. Because they attended to the people closely, those intent on achieving results in extending benevolence could readily accomplish their aims without obstruction. Because their assigned rank was low, those intent on seeking the favor of the exalted ruler could readily remain steadfast…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
而不挫況乎天監在下視聽自民安民則
惠知人則哲聖帝明王率用此道固宜循
良之吏史不絕書而願治之君光昭簡冊
矣然三代而下求之漢唐僅有一二史稱
漢宣帝詔見刺史嘗曰庶民所以安其田
里政平訟理與我共此者其良二千石乎
推其意蓋謂太守吏民之本也是故有治
理稱效者或璽書褒美或增秩賜金一時
優異彰彰顯矣當其時郡邑大小感激思
===
奮各率乃職者無論百數而彊毅惠宣號
稱治最則趙廣漢韓延壽尹翁歸召信臣
朱邑魏相其人也蓋嘗析而辨之廣漢之
守京兆翁歸之治東海魏相之遷河南則
雅尚嚴督延壽之在潁川信臣之在南陽
朱邑之處渤海則務從寬大之數子者雖
其作用規模人人而殊然夷考其事如收
掾客之姦而竟致之法捕仲孫之猾而郡
莫敢犯收縛丞之詐而案治其罪茂陵遂
punctuated: 而不挫。況乎天監在下，視聽自民，安民則惠，知人則哲，聖帝明王率用此道。固宜循良之吏史不絕書，而願治之君光昭簡冊矣。然三代而下，求之漢唐，僅有一二。史稱漢宣帝詔見刺史，嘗曰：「庶民所以安其田里，政平訟理，與我共此者，其良二千石乎？」推其意，蓋謂太守吏民之本也。是故有治理稱效者，或璽書褒美，或增秩賜金，一時優異彰彰顯矣。當其時，郡邑大小感激思奮，各率乃職者，無論百數。而彊毅惠宣，號稱治最，則趙廣漢、韓延壽、尹翁歸、召信臣、朱邑、魏相其人也。蓋嘗析而辨之，廣漢之守京兆，翁歸之治東海，魏相之遷河南，則雅尚嚴督；延壽之在潁川，信臣之在南陽，朱邑之處渤海，則務從寬大。之數子者，雖其作用規模人人而殊，然夷考其事，如收掾客之姦而竟致之法，捕仲孫之猾而郡莫敢犯，收縛丞之詐而案治其罪，茂陵遂
translation_en:
…and not be thwarted. Moreover, Heaven watches over the world below, seeing and hearing through the people. To bring peace to the people is benevolence; to discern people’s character is wisdom. Sage emperors and enlightened kings have all followed this way. It is therefore fitting that histories should continually record upright and capable officials, and that rulers intent on good government should shine brightly in the historical annals. Yet after the Three Dynasties, even among the Han and Tang, only one or two such examples can be found.

History records that Emperor Xuan of Han summoned regional inspectors to audience and once said: “That the common people should live securely on their lands, that government should be equitable and lawsuits properly adjudicated—surely those who share this work with me are the worthy officials of two thousand bushels?” His meaning, when considered, was that commandery governors were the foundation upon which officials and people depended. Thus, those whose administration achieved commendable results were praised in letters bearing the imperial seal, or granted increases in rank and gifts of gold. The exceptional favor shown them was conspicuous in that age. At that time, officials of commanderies and counties, great and small, were moved to gratitude and eager effort; those who fulfilled their respective duties were beyond counting by the hundred. Among those renowned for firmness and resolve, for extending benevolent government, and for the finest administrative achievements were Zhao Guanghan, Han Yanshou, Yin Wenggui, Shao Xinchen, Zhu Yi, and Wei Xiang.

I have examined and distinguished their approaches. Guanghan, as governor of Jingzhao, Wenggui, in administering Donghai, and Wei Xiang, upon his transfer to Henan, consistently favored strict supervision. Yanshou in Yingchuan, Xinchen in Nanyang, and Zhu Yi in Bohai [?] devoted themselves to lenient and generous government. Although each of these men differed in his methods and administrative approach, an impartial examination of their deeds reveals such acts as arresting a corrupt clerk’s retainer [?] and ultimately bringing him to justice; apprehending the malefactor Zhongsun, so that no one in the commandery dared break the law; and arresting and binding a deceitful assistant magistrate, investigating his offenses, and punishing him. Maoling consequently…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
以大治此其迹雖不同而敢於任怨以貽
民心之安者同也至如歷召長老而教以
禮讓存問耆舊而身處儉約躬勸農桑爲
民均水而吏民稱爲召父玆其忘身之勞
先民之急有不可以循吏目之者哉此守
令之良吾有得於漢之可述者此也唐太
宗錄刺史於屏風亦嘗曰永惟治人之本
莫重刺史推其意蓋謂守令親民之官也
是故不歷刺史不得任侍郎不歷縣令不
===
得任臺郎給事一時鄭重炳炳著矣當其
時州師遠邇遘會興起者勞厥事者軫不
踵息而精明廉恕各擅所長則賈敦頤鄭
德本薛大鼎張允濟何易于其人也蓋嘗
就而論之敦頤之守冀州德本之守瀛州
大鼎之守滄州則惠澤旁流允濟之令武
陽易于之令昌邑則廉明並茂之數子者
雖其施爲次第人人而殊然夷考其事如
立堰庸水以興滹沱之利復渠廢塞以通
punctuated:
以大治。此其迹雖不同，而敢於任怨以貽民心之安者同也。至如歷召長老而教以禮讓，存問耆舊而身處儉約，躬勸農桑，爲民均水，而吏民稱爲召父，玆其忘身之勞、先民之急，有不可以循吏目之者哉？此守令之良，吾有得於漢之可述者，此也。
唐太宗錄刺史於屏風，亦嘗曰：「永惟治人之本，莫重刺史。」推其意，蓋謂守令親民之官也。是故不歷刺史，不得任侍郎；不歷縣令，不得任臺郎、給事。一時鄭重，炳炳著矣。當其時，州師遠邇遘會興起者，勞厥事者軫不踵息，而精明廉恕，各擅所長，則賈敦頤、鄭德本、薛大鼎、張允濟、何易于其人也。蓋嘗就而論之，敦頤之守冀州，德本之守瀛州，大鼎之守滄州，則惠澤旁流；允濟之令武陽，易于之令昌邑，則廉明並茂。之數子者，雖其施爲次第人人而殊，然夷考其事，如立堰庸水以興滹沱之利，復渠廢塞以通
translation_en:
…thereby bringing about excellent order. Although their deeds differed, they were alike in daring to incur resentment so as to bring peace to the people’s hearts. As for summoning elders in turn and instructing them in ritual propriety and deference, visiting and inquiring after the aged while personally living frugally, and personally encouraging farming and sericulture and distributing water equitably for the people, so that officials and commoners called their governor “Father Shao”—in forgetting their own toil and giving priority to the people’s urgent needs, could any of these men fail to qualify as exemplary officials? These are the excellent prefects and county magistrates of the Han whose deeds I have found worthy of recounting.
Emperor Taizong of the Tang recorded the names of regional inspectors on a screen. He also once said: “When I reflect continually on the foundations of governing the people, no officials are more important than regional inspectors.” His meaning, I take it, was that prefects and county magistrates were officials in close contact with the people. Thus, no one could become a vice minister without having served as a regional inspector, or become a ministry director or supervising secretary without having served as a county magistrate. The importance attached to these offices at the time was abundantly clear. In those days, prefectural officials near and far rose to meet the occasion; those who labored at their duties worked without respite [?]. In discernment, integrity, and forbearance, each excelled in his own way. Such men were Jia Dunyi, Zheng Deben, Xue Dading, Zhang Yunji, and He Yiyu. Let us consider them individually. When Dunyi governed Jizhou, Deben governed Yingzhou, and Dading governed Cangzhou, their beneficence spread far and wide. When Yunji served as magistrate of Wuyang and Yiyu as magistrate of Changyi, integrity and discernment flourished together. Although these men differed in the sequence of their administrative measures, an impartial examination of their deeds reveals such achievements as building weirs and putting water to use [?] to secure the benefits of the Hutuo River, and restoring disused and obstructed canals to open up…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
無棣之流而治名河北允稱鐺脚之譽此
其績雖各異而均於任勞以急國家之務
則一也至如政先愛利而徹蒙以發匿梲
之姦事務恤民而引舟以愧乘春之吏寬
茶榷而不征捐俸入以代輸玆其儉以持
身仁以惠下有不可以循吏名之者哉此
守令之賢吾有得於唐之可述者此也逮
至有宋率崇令典慶曆間銳意治安富弼
范仲淹皆嘗昌言守令之稱職務在監司
===
之得人其意以天下之廣郡邑之衆必欲
君人者斤斤而察之日亦不足矣故惟監
司督之刺史刺史督之縣令綱維相制纖
鉅畢舉則君不勞而萬事康民不勞而庶
禎出為而不有施而不著斯君道尊而臣
義立矣此有宋之世所以守令列至公卿
遂成忠厚之治而循良諸吏彬彬史策有
非愚生移晷所能立數也洪惟我
朝稽古建官守令之制悉倣疇昔
punctuated:
無棣之流，而治名河北，允稱鐺脚之譽。此其績雖各異，而均於任勞以急國家之務則一也。至如政先愛利，而徹蒙以發匿梲之姦；事務恤民，而引舟以愧乘春之吏；寬茶榷而不征，捐俸入以代輸。玆其儉以持身，仁以惠下，有不可以循吏名之者哉？此守令之賢，吾有得於唐之可述者，此也。
逮至有宋，率崇令典。慶曆間，銳意治安，富弼、范仲淹皆嘗昌言：守令之稱職，務在監司之得人。其意以天下之廣、郡邑之衆，必欲君人者斤斤而察之，日亦不足矣。故惟監司督之刺史，刺史督之縣令，綱維相制，纖鉅畢舉，則君不勞而萬事康，民不勞而庶禎出。為而不有，施而不著，斯君道尊而臣義立矣。此有宋之世所以守令列至公卿，遂成忠厚之治，而循良諸吏彬彬史策，有非愚生移晷所能立數也。
洪惟我朝稽古建官，守令之制悉倣疇昔。
translation_en:
…the waters of Wudi; their governance won renown in Hebei, fully meriting the praise that likened them to the three legs of a cauldron. Although their achievements differed, they were alike in accepting arduous responsibilities and attending urgently to the affairs of the state. Some made care for the people and their welfare the first concern of government, lifting concealment to expose the wrongdoing of those hiding a club [?]; others devoted their efforts to relieving the people and hauled a boat themselves to shame officials traveling in spring. They relaxed the tea monopoly and refrained from levying its charges, and contributed their salaries to pay what the people owed. Frugal in their own conduct and benevolent toward those below them, could any of these men fail to deserve the name of exemplary local official? These, then, are the worthy prefects and magistrates of the Tang whose deeds I have found deserving of recounting.
When the Song dynasty came, it generally upheld sound institutions. During the Qingli era, determined efforts were made to secure good government and peace. Fu Bi and Fan Zhongyan both openly declared that securing competent prefects and magistrates depended above all on choosing the right men as surveillance commissioners. Their reasoning was that, with so vast a realm and so many prefectures and counties, even the entire day would not suffice if the ruler insisted on scrutinizing every detail himself. Thus surveillance commissioners should oversee prefects, and prefects should oversee county magistrates. When the framework of authority provides mutual checks and matters great and small are all attended to, the ruler need not toil, yet all affairs prosper; the people need not toil, yet manifold blessings appear. Acting without claiming possession, bestowing benefits without displaying them: in this way the ruler’s Way is honored and the duties of ministers are established. This explains why, under the Song, prefects and magistrates rose to the ranks of dukes and high ministers, ultimately bringing about a government of loyalty and generosity. Its many exemplary officials adorn the historical records in such numbers that this humble student could not enumerate them on the spot in so brief a span.
Considering with reverence how our dynasty has consulted antiquity in establishing its offices, its system of prefects and magistrates follows in every respect the institutions of earlier times…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
神謨
聖訓布傳海宇洋洋可誦矣肆我
皇上夙夜敬事
上帝憲法
祖宗選任文武大吏之良而尤切切加意於守
令之職蓋體
上帝好生之心而欲以光久道化成之績也頃
年以來三載計吏三考黜陟亦旣聿用常
典矣至如納冢宰之議而奏罷貪肆因言
===
官之疏而不時考察其於緩急有賴之任
則又每每不拘常調而擢用雋名焉其加
惠黎元脩飭吏治之意可謂勤且至矣士
生其時苟有一命之寄一得之愚固宜祗
畏
天威覃心民事以慰我
皇上惓惓憲
天求治之心可也執事乃猶廑念於守令吏治
之問意者簠簋雖脩不廢庖錯雨暘雖應
punctuated: 神謨聖訓，布傳海宇，洋洋可誦矣。肆我皇上夙夜敬事上帝，憲法祖宗，選任文武大吏之良，而尤切切加意於守令之職，蓋體上帝好生之心，而欲以光久道化成之績也。頃年以來，三載計吏，三考黜陟，亦旣聿用常典矣。至如納冢宰之議而奏罷貪肆，因言官之疏而不時考察，其於緩急有賴之任，則又每每不拘常調而擢用雋名焉。其加惠黎元、脩飭吏治之意，可謂勤且至矣。士生其時，苟有一命之寄、一得之愚，固宜祗畏天威，覃心民事，以慰我皇上惓惓憲天求治之心可也。執事乃猶廑念於守令吏治之問，意者簠簋雖脩，不廢庖錯；雨暘雖應，
translation_en:
…The divine plans and sagely instructions have spread throughout the realm, abundant and worthy of recitation. Thus our Emperor reverently serves the Lord on High day and night, takes the imperial ancestors as his models, and selects worthy men for high civil and military office. He gives especially earnest attention to the duties of prefects and magistrates, embodying the Lord on High’s love of life and seeking to glorify the achievements of transformation through enduring adherence to the Way.

In recent years, officials have been assessed every three years and demoted or promoted after three assessments, duly following the established regulations. Furthermore, the Emperor has accepted the Minister of Personnel’s proposals and dismissed the corrupt and unrestrained, and has ordered special inspections in response to memorials from remonstrance officials. For posts upon which one must rely in ordinary times and emergencies alike, he has repeatedly promoted men of talent and reputation without adhering to the regular promotion schedule. His concern to benefit the common people and set official administration in order may indeed be called both diligent and thorough.

Scholars born in such a time, if entrusted with even the lowest official appointment or possessed of even one humble insight, should reverently stand in awe of imperial majesty and devote their minds to the people’s affairs. They may thereby answer our Emperor’s earnest desire to model himself on Heaven and seek good government. Yet you, honored examiners, still concern yourselves with this question about the administration of prefects and magistrates. Perhaps your meaning is that, although the ritual grain vessels are in order, the work of the kitchen must not be neglected [?]; although rain and sunshine arrive as they should…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
不忘桔槔之意乎抑或
主上體元之意雖切而有司之仰承
德意者有未至乎不然何
廟廊之上極稱至治而江海之遠猶有切問
也夫士之育於世也猶馬之育於閑也一
日一粟一日百里槽櫪之凡品也一食石
粟一日千里則驊騮騄駬非所論於驪黃
牝牡間矣故夫循行逐隊百里材也若乃
排難解紛志在不奪力行仁善期於不朽
===
===
則上襄矣執此而論人品犁然辨矣其孰
能遁之君之問治於臣也猶主之問耕於
僕也櫛沐菑畬胼胝畎澮此義僕也久而
任之豐其衣食假之心膂僕榮而主逸矣
否則日褫之可也故夫臣之克慎於官者
則久任之久任而有功則超遷之超遷不
效即三褫無枉也執此而論吏治翕然具
矣其孰能逃之今之議者曰官久則易怠
於宦成政久則易至於玩愒又曰按柱索
punctuated:
不忘桔槔之意乎？抑或主上體元之意雖切，而有司之仰承德意者有未至乎？不然，何廟廊之上極稱至治，而江海之遠猶有切問也？夫士之育於世也，猶馬之育於閑也。一日一粟，一日百里，槽櫪之凡品也；一食石粟，一日千里，則驊騮騄駬，非所論於驪黃牝牡間矣。故夫循行逐隊，百里材也；若乃排難解紛，志在不奪，力行仁善，期於不朽，則上襄矣。執此而論人品，犁然辨矣，其孰能遁之？

君之問治於臣也，猶主之問耕於僕也。櫛沐菑畬，胼胝畎澮，此義僕也。久而任之，豐其衣食，假之心膂，僕榮而主逸矣；否則日褫之可也。故夫臣之克慎於官者，則久任之；久任而有功，則超遷之；超遷不效，即三褫無枉也。執此而論吏治，翕然具矣，其孰能逃之？今之議者曰：「官久則易怠於宦成，政久則易至於玩愒。」又曰：「按柱索
translation_en:
…does not forget the well sweep? Or is it that, although His Majesty earnestly seeks to embody the primal virtue, the responsible officials have fallen short in reverently carrying out his benevolent intentions? Otherwise, why is consummate government praised so highly at court, while searching questions still arise in these distant regions by the rivers and sea? The nurturing of scholars in the world resembles the raising of horses in a stable. A horse that consumes one measure of grain a day [?] and travels a hundred li a day is an ordinary creature of the manger. One that consumes a shi of grain at a feeding and travels a thousand li a day is a Hualiu or Lü’er, a steed whose worth cannot be judged by whether it is black or yellow, mare or stallion. Thus, those who follow the regular course and keep with the herd possess merely the capacity to travel a hundred li. Those who resolve difficulties and disentangle disputes, whose determination cannot be shaken, who vigorously practice benevolence and goodness and aspire to an imperishable name, attain the highest excellence [?]. Judged by this standard, differences in human character become unmistakably clear. Who could evade such scrutiny?

A ruler’s questioning his ministers about government resembles a master’s questioning his servants about farming. Weather-beaten in newly reclaimed and cultivated fields, their hands and feet callused from labor among the furrows and irrigation channels—these are faithful servants. Employ them for a long time, provide them generously with clothing and food, and trust them as your own heart and limbs: the servants will be honored and the master at ease. Otherwise, they may be stripped of their positions any day. Thus, ministers who conscientiously attend to their offices should be retained for long terms; those who achieve results during long service should receive exceptional promotion. If they fail to perform after exceptional promotion, even stripping them of office three times would do them no injustice. Judged by this standard, the principles of managing officials are fully comprehended. Who could escape their application? Those who discuss the matter today say: “Officials who remain long in office readily grow indolent once their careers are established; those who administer affairs for a long time readily fall into negligence and procrastination.” They also say: “Pressing upon the bridge of a stringed instrument to seek…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
調則希音不能以自陳此謂久任之法不
足以示勸而適足以滯材者言也而不知
久任之中未嘗不可以行超遷之法今之
議者曰吏數易則下不安又曰官知其不
久則怠忽易生吏知其不久則覬覦競作
此謂超遷之法不足以表異而返足以病
治者言也而不知超遷之材未始不得之
於久任之後愚嘗謂世有治人政無定法
假令郡得一人焉邑得一人焉職務日舉
===
民心相安則久任之始宰公浪誕著賢聲
歷守應天益彰政譽如顧佐之齊名孝肅
可也先在鎮江綽有偉績比改蘇郡尤愜
輿情如林鶚之獨持大體可也如其不然
則汎駕之駑惰耕之僕去之惟恐其不速
耳烏用久任爲哉假令任已久矣而志不
移功已著矣而才益茂則超擢之積米賑
農活者無算任久遷秩留者萬衆如況鍾
之在姑蘇可也風裁震肅保障彌隆擒黠
punctuated: 調，則希音不能以自陳。此謂久任之法不足以示勸，而適足以滯材者言也，而不知久任之中未嘗不可以行超遷之法。今之議者曰：「吏數易，則下不安。」又曰：「官知其不久，則怠忽易生；吏知其不久，則覬覦競作。」此謂超遷之法不足以表異，而返足以病治者言也，而不知超遷之材未始不得之於久任之後。愚嘗謂，世有治人，政無定法。假令郡得一人焉，邑得一人焉，職務日舉，民心相安，則久任之。始宰公浪誕著賢聲，歷守應天，益彰政譽，如顧佐之齊名孝肅可也；先在鎮江，綽有偉績，比改蘇郡，尤愜輿情，如林鶚之獨持大體可也。如其不然，則汎駕之駑、惰耕之僕，去之惟恐其不速耳，烏用久任爲哉！假令任已久矣，而志不移；功已著矣，而才益茂，則超擢之。積米賑農，活者無算；任久遷秩，留者萬衆，如況鍾之在姑蘇可也；風裁震肅，保障彌隆，擒黠
translation_en: …a tune, then rare music cannot find expression. Such is the argument of those who claim that prolonged tenure cannot encourage officials but merely holds back talent. They fail to understand that exceptional promotion can still be practiced during a prolonged tenure. Those who discuss the matter today say: “If officials are changed frequently, those below them cannot feel secure.” They also say: “When an official knows his tenure will be short, negligence readily arises; when clerks know his tenure will be short, they compete in pursuing their own advantage.” Such is the argument of those who claim that exceptional promotion cannot distinguish outstanding service but instead impairs government. They fail to understand that men suited for exceptional promotion may well be discovered only after prolonged tenure. I have always maintained that the world has men capable of governing, but government has no fixed methods. Suppose a prefecture or county obtains such a man: if he attends to his duties daily and the people are content, retain him in office. Gu Zuo, for example, first won a reputation for worth as a county magistrate [the wording here is garbled: 公浪誕, ?]; subsequently, as prefect of Yingtian, his reputation for good government grew still greater, and he ranked alongside Xiaosu in renown. Or consider Lin E, who achieved conspicuous results while serving in Zhenjiang and, after his transfer to Suzhou Prefecture, satisfied popular expectations still more fully, showing an exceptional grasp of the larger concerns of government. If an official is otherwise, however, he is like an inferior horse that breaks free of its harness or a servant who shirks his plowing: one fears only that he cannot be removed quickly enough. What use is prolonged tenure then? Suppose a man has served long yet remains steadfast in purpose, and his achievements are already manifest yet his abilities continue to flourish: promote him exceptionally. Kuang Zhong in Gusu, for example, accumulated rice to relieve farmers, saving countless lives; after long service he was advanced in rank, while multitudes sought to retain him. Or take one whose stern bearing inspires awe and discipline, whose protection of the people grows ever stronger, and who captures crafty…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
寇於崇朝陟秉憲於江藩如許逵之治樂
陵可也不然則驟進之流希寵之輩抑之
惟恐其不力耳烏用超遷為哉隨時劑量
不執其方臨局制用不先其策則河南潁
川渤海南陽之治不患其不優於漢滄州
瀛州武陽昌邑之政不患不優於唐而我
皇上敬天勤民遠邁唐虞之功可永保於無疆
矣惟執事進而教之毋但曰書生之談焉
可也
===
第四問
周仕堦
同考試官教諭張 批 論學論政博而有條此必
知尚友先賢者宜錄
同考試官教諭宋 批 品藻先哲而能取法乎上
可以觀志矣
考試官教諭尹 批 稽古頗詳持議亦正
考試官教授王 批 評往哲如鑑佳士也
嘗聞弘經濟之猷崇建立之節者聲實表
punctuated:
寇於崇朝，陟秉憲於江藩，如許逵之治樂陵可也。不然，則驟進之流、希寵之輩，抑之惟恐其不力耳，烏用超遷為哉？隨時劑量，不執其方；臨局制用，不先其策。則河南、潁川、渤海、南陽之治，不患其不優於漢；滄州、瀛州、武陽、昌邑之政，不患不優於唐。而我皇上敬天勤民、遠邁唐虞之功，可永保於無疆矣。惟執事進而教之，毋但曰書生之談焉可也。

第四問
周仕堦

同考試官教諭張批：「論學論政，博而有條，此必知尚友先賢者，宜錄。」
同考試官教諭宋批：「品藻先哲，而能取法乎上，可以觀志矣。」
考試官教諭尹批：「稽古頗詳，持議亦正。」
考試官教授王批：「評往哲如鑑，佳士也。」

嘗聞弘經濟之猷、崇建立之節者，聲實表
translation_en:
…bandits within a single morning, and being promoted to exercise judicial supervision in the Jiangxi provincial administration—as in Xu Kui’s governance of Leling—would be appropriate. Otherwise, those who advance precipitously and seek favor must be restrained, the only concern being that the restraint might not be forceful enough. What use would exceptional promotion serve? Weigh circumstances as they arise, without clinging to a fixed method; devise measures for the situation at hand, without deciding on a strategy beforehand. Then there need be no fear that the administration of Henan, Yingchuan, Bohai, and Nanyang will fail to surpass that of the Han, or that the governance of Cangzhou, Yingzhou, Wuyang, and Changyi will fail to surpass that of the Tang. Thus the achievements of our Emperor, who reveres Heaven and diligently cares for the people, far surpassing those of Yao and Shun, may be preserved forever without limit. I ask only that you, sir, offer further instruction, rather than dismiss this merely as a scholar’s talk.

Fourth Policy Question
Zhou Shijie 周仕堦

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “His discussion of learning and government is broad yet orderly. He surely knows how to take the worthies of antiquity as his friends. He merits selection.”

Associate Examiner Song, Instructor, comments: “In appraising earlier sages, he takes the highest standards as his models. This reveals his aspirations.”

Examiner Yin, Instructor, comments: “His examination of antiquity is quite detailed, and his arguments are also sound.”

Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: “His assessments of past sages are like a mirror. He is an excellent scholar.”

I have heard that those who advance plans for ordering the realm and benefiting its people, and uphold the integrity required for lasting accomplishments, have their reputation and actual achievements manifested…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
於官箴風教垂之鄉誼乃士人之遐軌所
尚友而私淑者也豈以適然之遇沾沾自
效者名哉夫爲國爲民以宣其力是謂弘
經濟之猷立德立言以善其身是謂崇建
立之節此在我者歷百年而不泯也崇卑
異分顯晦異時遇之在外者非所以圖不
泯也能辨於此而惟其不泯者圖之則曠
然相感於形神意氣之外可以論學可以
論政矣是故貴弗崇也賤弗卑也出弗顯
===
也處弗晦也愚執此以覽觀往昔進退名
流自元愷以降上下數千餘載治化熙洽
豪傑之士往往鍾光岳之氣抱卓犖之才
崛起其間愚更僕未易數也姑就執事今
日所問者言之閩之名宦漢以前無聞也
自唐迄宋中朝之仕籍相通而往哲之勳
名漸著彬彬海隅代不乏人矣自今觀之
建學講道肇海濱鄒魯之風常衮之開府
也覲典申明沮藩鎮驕橫之氣柳冕之陳
punctuated:
於官箴，風教垂之鄉誼，乃士人之遐軌，所尚友而私淑者也。豈以適然之遇，沾沾自效者名哉？夫爲國爲民以宣其力，是謂弘經濟之猷；立德立言以善其身，是謂崇建立之節。此在我者，歷百年而不泯也。崇卑異分，顯晦異時，遇之在外者，非所以圖不泯也。能辨於此，而惟其不泯者圖之，則曠然相感於形神意氣之外，可以論學，可以論政矣。是故貴弗崇也，賤弗卑也，出弗顯也，處弗晦也。
愚執此以覽觀往昔進退名流，自元愷以降，上下數千餘載，治化熙洽，豪傑之士往往鍾光岳之氣，抱卓犖之才，崛起其間，愚更僕未易數也。姑就執事今日所問者言之：閩之名宦，漢以前無聞也。自唐迄宋，中朝之仕籍相通，而往哲之勳名漸著，彬彬海隅，代不乏人矣。自今觀之，建學講道，肇海濱鄒魯之風，常衮之開府也；覲典申明，沮藩鎮驕橫之氣，柳冕之陳
translation_en:
…in admonitions for officials, while their moral influence is handed down through the bonds of local community. They are enduring exemplars for scholars, who befriend them across the ages and privately learn from their example. Could their fame rest merely on a chance opportunity to serve, in which they complacently displayed their abilities? To exert one’s strength for the state and the people is what is meant by enlarging the designs of statecraft; to establish virtue and enduring teachings, thereby perfecting oneself, is what is meant by upholding the integrity required for lasting accomplishment. These things lie within oneself and remain undiminished after a hundred years. High and low rank differ in station; prominence and obscurity come at different times. Such opportunities depend on external circumstances and are not the means by which one seeks an enduring legacy. If one can distinguish these things and pursue only what will endure, one can enter freely into communion with the ancients beyond bodily form, spirit, intention, and vital force, and thus discuss learning and government. Hence noble rank does not exalt one, humble rank does not abase one, entering office does not make one illustrious, and remaining in retirement does not obscure one.
I humbly use this principle to survey the renowned men of the past, whether they entered service or withdrew. From the Eight Yuan and Eight Kai onward, across several thousand years, government and moral transformation flourished harmoniously. Heroic men, concentrating within themselves the vital essence of the heavens and mountains and possessing outstanding talents, repeatedly arose among them. Even with attendants taking turns, I could not readily finish enumerating them. Let me speak, then, only of those about whom you have asked today. Of Fujian’s renowned officials before the Han, nothing is known. From the Tang through the Song, as its official appointments became connected with those of the central court, the achievements and reputations of earlier worthies gradually became manifest. In this cultured corner beside the sea, no generation lacked such men. Viewed from the present, establishing schools and expounding the Way, thus initiating the tradition of a coastal Zou and Lu—the homeland of Confucian learning—was the work of Chang Gun when he opened his administrative headquarters. Clarifying the rules for court audiences and checking the arrogance and overbearing conduct of the regional military governors was the purpose of Liu Mian’s submission…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
情也敷文命而肅王章君子謂其得先務
之急强悍格心不遐遺於秀士張浚之拊
循也禁兵就鎭卽蕩滌乎妖氛葉夢得之
討賊也同民心而禦外患君子謂其得治
劇之宜辛次膺以雅淨撫全閩而案牘之
清時人稱其不擾陳俊卿以節省紓民瘼
而碑文之碎當世美其撝謙是鸞鳳之翔
不爲鷹鸇之志也辛棄疾以積鏹嚴武備
而海境賴以無虞趙必愿以節制整海防
===
而疆場爲之不聳是梓人之智而非杞人
之憂也令行禁止非曾鞏之守福州乎至
誠感人非王十朋之守泉州乎一則文章
經世號令等神君之稱一則不愧科名條
教藹陽春之澤可謂行顧言矣若夫日月
爭光者遍清漳之惠政木蘭遺愛者奏興
化之膚功觀其寇賊掃除而庶民安於田
野河潤百里而三農世蒙其恩胡銓潘畤
豈徒矯矯於行己之直者耶築海爲湖非
punctuated: 情也。敷文命而肅王章，君子謂其得先務之急。强悍格心，不遐遺於秀士，張浚之拊循也；禁兵就鎭，卽蕩滌乎妖氛，葉夢得之討賊也。同民心而禦外患，君子謂其得治劇之宜。辛次膺以雅淨撫全閩，而案牘之清，時人稱其不擾；陳俊卿以節省紓民瘼，而碑文之碎，當世美其撝謙。是鸞鳳之翔，不爲鷹鸇之志也。辛棄疾以積鏹嚴武備，而海境賴以無虞；趙必愿以節制整海防，而疆場爲之不聳。是梓人之智，而非杞人之憂也。令行禁止，非曾鞏之守福州乎？至誠感人，非王十朋之守泉州乎？一則文章經世，號令等神君之稱；一則不愧科名，條教藹陽春之澤。可謂行顧言矣。若夫日月爭光者，遍清漳之惠政；木蘭遺愛者，奏興化之膚功。觀其寇賊掃除，而庶民安於田野；河潤百里，而三農世蒙其恩。胡銓、潘畤，豈徒矯矯於行己之直者耶？築海爲湖，非
translation_en:
…his statement of the circumstances. By spreading civil instruction and upholding the royal laws, they earned the judgment of exemplary men that they understood which tasks demanded priority. Bringing the hearts of the fierce and unruly into submission, while neglecting none of the outstanding scholars: such was Zhang Jun’s work of conciliation. Stationing imperial troops in garrisons and promptly sweeping away the baleful atmosphere of rebellion: such was Ye Mengde’s suppression of bandits. By uniting the people’s hearts and warding off external threats, they earned the judgment of exemplary men that they understood how to govern in difficult circumstances.

Xin Ciying governed all Fujian with cultivated simplicity and purity; his administration was free of vexatious paperwork, and contemporaries praised him for not troubling the people. Chen Junqing relieved the people’s suffering through economy; when he had the commemorative inscription broken up, his contemporaries admired his modesty. This was the soaring of auspicious luan birds and phoenixes, without the predatory ambitions of hawks and falcons. Xin Qiji accumulated funds to strengthen military preparedness, and the coastal territory consequently enjoyed security. Zhao Biyuan brought order to coastal defenses through disciplined command, and the frontier consequently remained free from alarm. This was the master carpenter’s wisdom, rather than the groundless anxiety of the man of Qi.

Was it not Zeng Gong, as prefect of Fuzhou, whose commands were obeyed and whose prohibitions were observed? Was it not Wang Shipeng, as prefect of Quanzhou, who moved people through utter sincerity? The one applied literary learning to governing the world, and his commands earned him praise comparable to that of the ‘Divine Lord’; the other lived up to his examination distinction, and his administrative instructions abounded in the beneficence of spring sunshine. Their conduct may indeed be said to have accorded with their words.

As for achievements rivaling the sun and moon in brilliance, beneficent government extended throughout Qingzhang; as for an enduring legacy of kindness at Mulan, great merit was achieved in Xinghua. Consider how bandits were swept away and the common people lived securely in the countryside; how the river watered a hundred li and farming communities enjoyed its benefits for generations. Were Hu Quan and Pan Zhi merely men distinguished by upright personal conduct? As for embanking the sea to make a lake, was it not…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
郎簡之令福清乎捫鐘驗盜非陳襄之攝
浦城乎一則屹然海上之長城而萬世攸
賴一則翕然建中之召父而闔邑舉安均
之仁且智矣若夫庭無留訟者登魏公之
薦剡力制豪併者揚莆人之口碑觀其嚴
行鄉約而民不忍欺沉毀淫祠而俗隨丕
變趙公峴廖德明豈煦煦於姑息之仁者
耶之數君者或奏績於唐或擅名於宋其
時不同也或爲觀察安撫使或爲郡守縣
===
令其分不同也要之流愛敷仁以一身周
萬民之慮訏謨定議以一時豫萬載之猷
皆集事而不施其勞成功而不矜其智者
也至今爼豆之際有餘思焉豈能置優劣
於其間哉閩之鄉賢漢以前無聞也自唐
迄宋聲敎之漸磨日篤而豪俊之挺生日
蕃濟濟多士代不乏人矣自今觀之富貴
浮雲不草德妃之稱翰林之楊億也扶溝
召學毅然鼓篋而從程門之游酢也秉筆
punctuated:
郎簡之令福清乎？捫鐘驗盜，非陳襄之攝浦城乎？一則屹然海上之長城，而萬世攸賴；一則翕然建中之召父，而闔邑舉安。均之仁且智矣。若夫庭無留訟者，登魏公之薦剡；力制豪併者，揚莆人之口碑。觀其嚴行鄉約，而民不忍欺；沉毀淫祠，而俗隨丕變。趙公峴、廖德明，豈煦煦於姑息之仁者耶？之數君者，或奏績於唐，或擅名於宋，其時不同也；或爲觀察安撫使，或爲郡守縣令，其分不同也。要之，流愛敷仁，以一身周萬民之慮；訏謨定議，以一時豫萬載之猷。皆集事而不施其勞，成功而不矜其智者也。至今爼豆之際，有餘思焉，豈能置優劣於其間哉？

閩之鄉賢，漢以前無聞也。自唐迄宋，聲敎之漸磨日篤，而豪俊之挺生日蕃，濟濟多士，代不乏人矣。自今觀之，富貴浮雲，不草德妃之稱，翰林之楊億也；扶溝召學，毅然鼓篋而從，程門之游酢也。秉筆
translation_en:
…was it not Lang Jian when he served as Magistrate of Fuqing? As for identifying a thief by having suspects touch a bell, was this not Chen Xiang when he served as acting Magistrate of Pucheng? The one stood like a great wall upon the sea, upon which countless generations would depend; the other was acclaimed throughout Jian as another Father Shao, bringing peace to the entire county. Both were benevolent and wise. As for the man whose court had no unresolved lawsuits, his name appeared in the Duke of Wei’s written recommendation; the man who firmly restrained powerful engrossers of property won the enduring praise of the people of Pu. Consider how they rigorously enforced community compacts, so that the people could not bear to deceive them, and submerged and destroyed shrines to illicit cults, so that local customs underwent a great transformation. Were Zhao Gongxian [?] and Liao Deming merely men whose benevolence consisted in indulgent kindness? These several gentlemen achieved distinction either under the Tang or under the Song: their times differed. Some served as Surveillance Commissioners or Pacification Commissioners, others as prefects or county magistrates: their responsibilities differed. Yet all spread loving care and benevolence, each attending in his own person to the concerns of the whole populace; through grand plans and settled deliberations, they prepared in their own time policies for ten thousand years to come. All accomplished their duties without making a show of their exertions, and achieved success without boasting of their wisdom. Even today, when sacrificial vessels are set out in their honor, fond remembrance lingers. How could one rank them as superior or inferior?

Of Fujian’s local worthies, none are recorded before the Han. From the Tang through the Song, the gradual influence of moral instruction grew ever deeper, while outstanding men arose in ever greater numbers. Distinguished scholars abounded; no generation lacked them. Looking back from the present, there was Yang Yi of the Hanlin Academy, who regarded wealth and rank as floating clouds and refused to draft the designation of Virtuous Consort. There was You Zuo of Cheng’s school, who, summoned to study at Fugou [?], resolutely took up his book satchel and followed him. Wielding the brush…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
於朝廷之上倡道於伊洛之濱君子以爲
正松栢獨秀開燕翼之心傳胡安國之春
秋也刺史潭州宣大學之誠意眞德秀之
衍義也明道於父子之間殫智於君民之
際君子以爲忠劉彝爲安定高徒而都水
著績於治事也有明徵林希逸作三子口
義而清白騰芳於服官也無餘愧擬諸分
陰之惜同一砥柱中流也鄭俠上流民圖
而以唐之賢佞兩臣分軸進悟陳剛中以
===
諫去國而與子韶之第一人物竝驅爭先
揆諸延年之疏同一夷齊之後也德望老
成非曾公亮之出入三朝乎始終一節非
蘇頌之佐理五朝乎一則折遼夏之傲一
則鄙惠卿之徼可謂太平賢相矣而徹樂
辭花致金人之愧服抗言日錄斥安石之
偏邪是有得於華夷之辨而君命不辱深
識乎否泰之機而善類保全顏師魯陳瓘
豈非剛毅不回者耶楊先生安在非楊時
punctuated: 於朝廷之上，倡道於伊洛之濱，君子以爲正。松栢獨秀，開燕翼之心傳，胡安國之春秋也；刺史潭州，宣大學之誠意，眞德秀之衍義也。明道於父子之間，殫智於君民之際，君子以爲忠。劉彝爲安定高徒，而都水著績於治事也，有明徵；林希逸作三子口義，而清白騰芳於服官也，無餘愧。擬諸分陰之惜，同一砥柱中流也。鄭俠上流民圖，而以唐之賢佞兩臣分軸進悟；陳剛中以諫去國，而與子韶之第一人物竝驅爭先。揆諸延年之疏，同一夷齊之後也。德望老成，非曾公亮之出入三朝乎？始終一節，非蘇頌之佐理五朝乎？一則折遼夏之傲，一則鄙惠卿之徼，可謂太平賢相矣。而徹樂辭花，致金人之愧服；抗言日錄，斥安石之偏邪。是有得於華夷之辨，而君命不辱；深識乎否泰之機，而善類保全。顏師魯、陳瓘，豈非剛毅不回者耶？楊先生安在？非楊時
translation_en:
…at the imperial court, and championing the Way on the banks of the Yi and Luo rivers: gentlemen deemed this upright conduct. Standing alone in excellence like pine and cypress, and initiating a transmission of the teachings of the mind for the benefit of later generations—such was Hu Anguo’s Spring and Autumn Annals commentary. Serving as prefect of Tanzhou and expounding the sincerity of intention taught in the Great Learning—such was Zhen Dexiu’s Extended Meaning of the Great Learning. Making the Way clear between father and son, and exhausting their wisdom in the service of ruler and people: gentlemen deemed this loyal devotion.

Liu Yi was an outstanding pupil of Anding; his achievements in water administration furnished clear evidence of his ability in practical affairs. Lin Xiyi wrote the Oral Explanations of the Three Masters, and his reputation for integrity in office left him nothing to be ashamed of. Compared with the man who cherished every fraction of an hour, they likewise stood as a pillar of rock amid the current. Zheng Xia submitted his Picture of Displaced People and presented separate scrolls depicting a worthy minister and a sycophantic minister of the Tang, seeking to awaken the ruler’s understanding. Chen Gangzhong left the capital because of his remonstrance, keeping pace and vying for precedence with Zishao, acclaimed as the foremost man of his time. Measured against Yannian’s memorial [?], they were alike successors to Boyi and Shuqi.

For mature virtue and standing, was there not Zeng Gongliang, who served at court and away from it through three reigns? For unwavering integrity from beginning to end, was there not Su Song, who assisted in governing through five reigns? One checked the arrogance of Liao and Xia; the other scorned Huiqing’s pursuit of advantage [?]. They may be called worthy chief councillors of an age of peace. Then there were those who had the music stopped and declined ceremonial flowers, bringing the people of Jin to shame and admiration; and who spoke out against the Daily Record, denouncing Anshi’s partiality and perversity. The former grasped the distinction between Chinese and outsiders and did not disgrace his ruler’s commission; the latter deeply understood the turning points between adversity and prosperity and preserved worthy men from harm. Were Yan Shilu and Chen Guan not firm and resolute, never swerving?

“Where is Master Yang?” Was it not Yang Shi …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
之震遠夷乎周易在洛陽非羅從彥之學
伊川乎一則見排於童貫一則吏隱於博
羅可謂守道君子矣而四諫馳聲尚致位
於殿學兩河經理竟見摧於汪黃是危言
於正人登用之時而勁氣彌顯危行於忌
功主和之日而正氣愈堅蔡襄李綱豈非
忠義不撓者耶之數子者或際全盛而得
行其志或遭多難而披瀝其忠其顯晦不
同也或居鼎鼐之任或司諫諍之職其崇
===
===
卑不同也要之立綱陳紀亹亹於維世之
功秉義樹勳惓惓於經邦之略皆天下爲
度而不狃於身謀大節是全而不搖於浮
議者也至今桑梓之末有餘感焉豈能置
升降於其間哉雖然惟聖人能立於無過
之地自賢人而下者未必無白璧之瑕也
寧學聖人而未至以一善而成名者未可
爲鸜鵒之中也數君子之賢尚矣就其中
而論之得無可擇而取之者乎蓋常袞之
punctuated:
之震遠夷乎？「周易在洛陽」，非羅從彥之學伊川乎？一則見排於童貫，一則吏隱於博羅，可謂守道君子矣。而四諫馳聲，尚致位於殿學；兩河經理，竟見摧於汪黃。是危言於正人登用之時，而勁氣彌顯；危行於忌功主和之日，而正氣愈堅。蔡襄、李綱豈非忠義不撓者耶？之數子者，或際全盛而得行其志，或遭多難而披瀝其忠，其顯晦不同也；或居鼎鼐之任，或司諫諍之職，其崇卑不同也。要之，立綱陳紀，亹亹於維世之功；秉義樹勳，惓惓於經邦之略。皆天下爲度而不狃於身謀，大節是全而不搖於浮議者也。至今桑梓之末有餘感焉，豈能置升降於其間哉？

雖然，惟聖人能立於無過之地，自賢人而下者，未必無白璧之瑕也。寧學聖人而未至，以一善而成名者，未可爲鸜鵒之中也。數君子之賢尚矣，就其中而論之，得無可擇而取之者乎？蓋常袞之
translation_en:
…whose influence awed the distant foreign peoples? As for the saying, “The Changes of Zhou is in Luoyang,” does this not refer to Luo Congyan’s studying under Yichuan? One was excluded through Tong Guan’s opposition; the other lived in seclusion while holding office in Boluo. They may indeed be called gentlemen who upheld the Way. Then there was the man whose fame spread through the four remonstrators and who eventually attained the rank of Hall Academician; and the man whose administration of the Two He regions ultimately met with defeat at the hands of Wang and Huang. The former spoke uprightly when upright men were being advanced to office, and his unyielding spirit became all the more manifest; the latter acted uprightly in days when merit provoked jealousy and peace was advocated, and his moral resolve grew still firmer. Were Cai Xiang and Li Gang not men unwavering in loyalty and righteousness?

Of these men, some encountered an age of full prosperity and could put their aspirations into practice; others met with many troubles and laid bare their loyalty. They differed in their prominence or obscurity. Some held the responsibilities of chief councillors; others occupied remonstrance offices. They differed in the elevation or modesty of their positions. In essence, they established guiding principles and set forth rules, laboring tirelessly to sustain the world; they upheld righteousness and achieved distinction, devoted wholeheartedly to plans for governing the realm. All took the whole realm as their measure rather than becoming engrossed in schemes for personal advantage. They preserved their integrity in great matters and were not swayed by shallow criticism. Even today, we later-born people of their native region still feel their enduring influence. How could we rank them above or below one another?

Nevertheless, only sages can stand free of error. Worthy men and those below them may still have flaws in their white jade. Better to study the sages, even without attaining their stature; those who win fame through a single good quality cannot be placed “among the mynah birds” [?]. The worthiness of these gentlemen is indeed exalted. Yet, examining them individually, are there not qualities we can select and adopt? For Chang Gun’s …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
開郡八閩之宗也吾不敢議也游酢之講
學儒者之純也吾無間然也外此則張浚
之精忠不能不賴子以成其美剛中之正
直不能不須友以成其忠曾子固之文章
王龜齡之奏疏胡澹庵之諫書眞西山之
學政雖凜凜於當時而楊億靈州之議希
逸老莊之傳康侯汲引於秦檜之門中立
推轂於蔡京之手千載而下好事者不免
有遺喙焉春秋責備賢者能無集長之論
===
乎要之士君子立身穹壤之間古人與稽
者尚友之志也能自得師者用中之準也
昔孟子嘗以伯夷柳下惠爲聖人矣而乃
所願則孔子之外弗學焉周茂叔敎人志
伊尹學顏淵而充以過則聖期之甚矣趨
嚮之不可不崇也數君子名賢碩彦海宇
流光理學淵源致治龜鑑謂之非百世之
師不可然而志學之所趨以孔子爲標的
者則又安敢畫於是哉愚生妄謬之思如
punctuated:
開郡，八閩之宗也，吾不敢議也。游酢之講學，儒者之純也，吾無間然也。外此，則張浚之精忠，不能不賴子以成其美；剛中之正直，不能不須友以成其忠。曾子固之文章，王龜齡之奏疏，胡澹庵之諫書，眞西山之學政，雖凜凜於當時，而楊億靈州之議，希逸老莊之傳，康侯汲引於秦檜之門，中立推轂於蔡京之手，千載而下，好事者不免有遺喙焉。《春秋》責備賢者，能無集長之論乎？
要之，士君子立身穹壤之間，古人與稽者，尚友之志也；能自得師者，用中之準也。昔孟子嘗以伯夷、柳下惠爲聖人矣，而乃所願，則孔子之外弗學焉。周茂叔敎人志伊尹、學顏淵，而充以過則聖，期之甚矣！趨嚮之不可不崇也。數君子名賢碩彦，海宇流光，理學淵源，致治龜鑑，謂之非百世之師不可。然而志學之所趨，以孔子爲標的者，則又安敢畫於是哉？愚生妄謬之思如
translation_en:
…in opening up the prefecture, he became the revered exemplar of the Eight Min regions; I dare not criticize him. You Zuo’s teaching exemplified the purity of a Confucian scholar; I find no fault in it. Beyond these, however, Zhang Jun’s wholehearted loyalty depended upon his son to bring its excellence to completion, while Gangzhong’s uprightness required a friend to perfect his loyalty. The literary writings of Zeng Zigu, the memorials of Wang Guiling, the remonstrance of Hu Dan’an, and the scholarship and governance of Zhen Xishan commanded awe in their day. Yet Yang Yi’s proposal concerning Lingzhou, Xiyi’s transmission of the teachings of Laozi and Zhuangzi, Kanghou’s advancement through Qin Hui’s patronage, and Zhongli’s promotion at Cai Jing’s hands inevitably leave grounds for criticism among those who delight in such matters, even a thousand years later. The Spring and Autumn Annals demands perfection of the worthy: can we dispense with considering how to bring together their respective strengths?
In essence, for a gentleman establishing himself between Heaven and Earth, measuring himself against the ancients expresses his aspiration to befriend the worthy of antiquity; being able to find his own teachers provides a standard for putting the Mean into practice. Mencius once called Bo Yi and Liu Xiahui sages, yet his own aspiration was to learn from none other than Confucius. Zhou Maoshu taught people to aspire to Yi Yin and learn from Yan Yuan, and, by developing themselves further and surpassing them, to become sages [?]. How lofty were his expectations! One’s aspirations must indeed be elevated. These gentlemen were renowned worthies and eminent talents whose brilliance spread throughout the realm, fountainheads of the Learning of Principle and models for achieving good government. We cannot deny that they are teachers for a hundred generations. Yet when one’s aspiration in learning takes Confucius as its target, how could one dare stop at their level? This foolish student’s rash and mistaken thoughts are as…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
此惟執事恕其狂而教之幸甚
第五問
李廷春
同考試官教諭唐批閱此時務策純粹之資經
濟之才閎遠該博之學具見矣其頊頊董賈者歟
同考試官教諭王批兵食一策多浮冗可厭此
作思深計遠言切慮詳殆悉心當世之務者
考試官教諭尹批區畫周詳鑿鑿可行
考試官教授王批行文議事迥出衆作
===
何以足兵曰求之賦而已遇變而通之以
權者善制兵者也何以足食曰因其利而
已時絀而不失其道者善制食者也蓋因
地取材而軌物備焉兵不外賦而足也而
强敵之來叵測民心之渙難收若不審主
客之勢而通之以損益之權則泥常以倖
功未有能濟者矣因天分地而財用出焉
食不加稅而足也而師旅之需無窮公私
之困已極若不執仁義之樞而要之於公
punctuated:
此，惟執事恕其狂而教之，幸甚。

第五問
李廷春

同考試官教諭唐批：閱此時務策，純粹之資、經濟之才、閎遠該博之學具見矣。其頊頊董賈者歟？
同考試官教諭王批：兵食一策，多浮冗可厭。此作思深計遠，言切慮詳，殆悉心當世之務者。
考試官教諭尹批：區畫周詳，鑿鑿可行。
考試官教授王批：行文議事，迥出衆作。

何以足兵？曰：求之賦而已。遇變而通之以權者，善制兵者也。何以足食？曰：因其利而已。時絀而不失其道者，善制食者也。蓋因地取材而軌物備焉，兵不外賦而足也。而强敵之來叵測，民心之渙難收，若不審主客之勢而通之以損益之權，則泥常以倖功，未有能濟者矣。因天分地而財用出焉，食不加稅而足也。而師旅之需無窮，公私之困已極，若不執仁義之樞而要之於公
translation_en:
…such are my thoughts. I would be most fortunate if you would pardon my presumption and instruct me.

Fifth Question
Li Tingchun

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, County School Instructor: Reading this policy essay on current affairs, one sees fully revealed the writer’s pure natural endowments, talent for statecraft, and far-reaching, comprehensive learning. Might he rival Dong and Jia [?]?

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, County School Instructor: Essays on this policy question concerning troops and provisions are often tiresomely superficial and verbose. This composition shows profound thought and far-reaching planning; its words are pertinent and its deliberations detailed. Its author surely devotes his whole mind to the affairs of the present age.

Comment by Examiner Yin, County School Instructor: The arrangements proposed are comprehensive and meticulous, and demonstrably practicable.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Prefectural School Instructor: In composition and discussion of affairs, this stands far above the other essays.

How can troops be made sufficient? I say: seek them through the levies, and nothing more. One who responds to changing circumstances with judicious adaptation is skilled at organizing military forces. How can provisions be made sufficient? I say: make use of the available advantages, and nothing more. One who does not depart from the proper Way even in straitened times is skilled at managing provisions. By drawing resources from the land according to its character, the prescribed requirements are fully supplied; troops can thus be made sufficient without going beyond the levies. Yet the arrival of a powerful enemy is unpredictable, and once the people’s allegiance has scattered, it is difficult to recover. Unless one examines the relative circumstances of defender and invader and adjusts arrangements through judicious reductions and additions, one merely clings to routine and hopes for success by chance. No one has ever succeeded in this way. By following Heaven’s seasons and allocating the land, financial resources become available; provisions can thus be made sufficient without increasing taxes. Yet the demands of armies are inexhaustible, and public and private resources alike are already strained to the utmost. Unless one holds fast to benevolence and righteousness as the pivot and brings matters into accord with impartial…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
平之道則任法以取盈日見其敝也已故
權者所以濟兵制之所不及而道又所以
善取民之制於不窮者也知乎此可與計
兵食矣請因明問而籌之昔者孔子論政
而繫之以足食足兵民信之三言至於必
不得已則寧去兵去食不肯須臾去信焉
蓋足食足兵而民信者道之常也去兵去
食而不失信者權不離道也此計兵食之
準也夫閩枕山襟海魚鹽稼穡之區而風
===
物之會也制兵則水陸營寨星列於腹邊
制食則錢穀屯鹽羅致於郡邑此其為備
素預宜夫威德之施不可勝用也夫何忠
良之吏罕繼文武之政日頹峒丁島酋竝
起肆毒遂至驅不教之民以示之餌出有
數之粟以委之壑而兵食交困幾不可為
矣仰仗我
皇上軫念邊氓
嘉納臺議
punctuated:
平之道，則任法以取盈，日見其敝也已。故權者，所以濟兵制之所不及；而道又所以善取民之制於不窮者也。知乎此，可與計兵食矣。請因明問而籌之。昔者孔子論政，而繫之以足食、足兵、民信之三言，至於必不得已，則寧去兵、去食，不肯須臾去信焉。蓋足食、足兵而民信者，道之常也；去兵、去食而不失信者，權不離道也。此計兵食之準也。
夫閩枕山襟海，魚鹽稼穡之區，而風物之會也。制兵則水陸營寨星列於腹邊，制食則錢穀屯鹽羅致於郡邑。此其為備素預，宜夫威德之施不可勝用也。夫何忠良之吏罕繼，文武之政日頹，峒丁島酋竝起肆毒，遂至驅不教之民以示之餌，出有數之粟以委之壑，而兵食交困，幾不可為矣。仰仗我皇上軫念邊氓，嘉納臺議，
translation_en:
…the way of fairness, then reliance on regulations to exact the full amount will only reveal their harmful effects day by day. Thus discretionary judgment remedies what military institutions fail to provide, while the Way ensures that the system of taking resources from the people operates properly without exhausting them. One who understands this may be consulted on planning military forces and provisions. Allow me to consider these matters in response to your discerning question. Formerly, when Confucius discussed government, he linked it to three requirements: sufficient food, sufficient military forces, and the people's trust. If compelled by unavoidable necessity, he would rather dispense with military forces and food than abandon trust even for a moment. Having sufficient food and military forces together with the people's trust is the constant principle of the Way; dispensing with military forces and food without losing trust is discretionary judgment that does not depart from the Way. This is the standard for planning military forces and provisions.
Min rests against the mountains and is girdled by the sea. It is a region of fish, salt, and farming, where local products and customs converge. In its military arrangements, camps and fortified posts for land and naval forces are scattered like stars throughout the interior and frontier. In its provisioning arrangements, money and grain, military agricultural colonies, and salt revenues are marshaled throughout the prefectures and counties. With such preparations long established, one would expect the exercise of might and beneficence to have inexhaustible resources at its disposal. Why, then, have loyal and worthy officials so rarely had worthy successors, while civil and military administration has deteriorated daily? Men of the mountain settlements and island chieftains rose together to wreak havoc. It came to the point that untrained people were driven forth as bait for them, and limited stocks of grain were poured into a ravine. Military forces and provisions alike were brought into desperate straits, almost beyond remedy. We have relied upon our Emperor, who has taken the frontier people to heart and graciously accepted the Censorate's proposals…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
善任將帥
簡用督臣食足於
內帑之頒而
神謨用廣兵强於東淅之調而
聖武丕昭山魈以次撲滅海氛日就蕩平八郡
蒸黎孰不欣覩太平之象而仰荷
天恩於無極也今執事以桑土之防衣袽之戒
而惓惓焉兵食之爲計豈不以峒丁之起
伏不常島夷之去來靡定客兵之調不可
===
爲常而
內帑之頒尤非可繼乎是故計兵者稽夫乘
之數則曰民壯不可不練也明守望之規
則曰保甲不可不嚴也欲復營伍之制則
曰衞士之坐食不可不簡也將峻華夷之
防則曰海艦戰陣之法不可不操而習也
凡計出此者孰非土著之議乎然而訓習
雖勤卒未必習服也水陸之兵雖足未必
其遇敵而不畏也欲專倚以備緩急難矣
punctuated:
善任將帥，簡用督臣，食足於內帑之頒，而神謨用廣；兵强於東淅之調，而聖武丕昭。山魈以次撲滅，海氛日就蕩平。八郡蒸黎，孰不欣覩太平之象，而仰荷天恩於無極也？今執事以桑土之防、衣袽之戒，而惓惓焉兵食之爲計，豈不以峒丁之起伏不常，島夷之去來靡定，客兵之調不可爲常，而內帑之頒尤非可繼乎？
是故計兵者，稽夫乘之數，則曰民壯不可不練也；明守望之規，則曰保甲不可不嚴也；欲復營伍之制，則曰衞士之坐食不可不簡也；將峻華夷之防，則曰海艦戰陣之法不可不操而習也。凡計出此者，孰非土著之議乎？然而訓習雖勤，卒未必習服也；水陸之兵雖足，未必其遇敵而不畏也。欲專倚以備緩急，難矣。
translation_en:
…He has employed commanders well and selected supervising ministers for service. Provisions have been made sufficient through grants from the imperial treasury, extending the reach of his divine plans; military strength has been increased through troops transferred from eastern Zhejiang [?], brilliantly manifesting his sagely martial power. The mountain demons have been destroyed in succession, and the baleful atmosphere at sea is daily being cleared away. Among the common people of the eight prefectures, who does not rejoice to behold the signs of peace and look up in boundless gratitude for imperial grace? Now you, sir, mindful of securing the nest with mulberry roots and keeping cloth ready to caulk a leaking boat, devote earnest attention to planning for troops and provisions. Is this not because the tribesmen of the mountain settlements rise and subside unpredictably, the island barbarians come and go without certainty, troops from elsewhere cannot be summoned as a regular expedient, and grants from the imperial treasury are even less sustainable?
Thus, those planning military affairs examine the numbers of military levies and say that the local militia must be trained. They clarify the rules for watch and ward and say that the mutual-responsibility system of household organization must be rigorously enforced. Wishing to restore the organization of military units, they say that guard soldiers who draw rations while remaining idle must be inspected and screened. Intending to strengthen the defenses separating Chinese from barbarians, they say that naval warfare and battle formations must be drilled and practiced. Of all proposals along these lines, which does not advocate reliance on locally raised troops? Yet, however diligent the training, the soldiers may not become proficient and obedient; however adequate the numbers of troops on land and water, they may not prove fearless when encountering the enemy. To rely exclusively on them to meet emergencies would be difficult indeed.

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
必也通之以權乎自今言之分任副將以
嚴簡閱之規專任閫臣以總行陣之紀所
以計練主兵者已有成式矣而初練之卒
有勇知方之未能其可遽以輕試乎留班
者汰弱存強而寓節縮之法上班者正籍
明禁而杜冒濫之門所以計去客兵者亦
有微意矣而有制之兵臨敵應機之有賴
其能遽委而去乎是練主兵所以培其本
也存客兵所以治其標也本之所培者日
===
以益標之所治者漸以損去留無與於巳
損益惟其所宜此權之不可以巳也說者
比於渴之掘井而飲病其備之不豫誠是
也井既泥而渴方甚乃不一掘以濟其急
焉惡在其為制兵之權耶計食者慨屯政
之廢則曰屯田之弊當清也憤寺租之侵
沒於豪右則曰鬻田之議當遵也病商人
中納之不廣則曰私鹽之禁不可不嚴也
考九府圜法之制則曰錢法亦可通行也
punctuated:
必也通之以權乎？自今言之，分任副將以嚴簡閱之規，專任閫臣以總行陣之紀，所以計練主兵者已有成式矣。而初練之卒，有勇知方之未能，其可遽以輕試乎？留班者汰弱存強，而寓節縮之法；上班者正籍明禁，而杜冒濫之門。所以計去客兵者亦有微意矣。而有制之兵，臨敵應機之有賴，其能遽委而去乎？是練主兵所以培其本也，存客兵所以治其標也。本之所培者日以益，標之所治者漸以損。去留無與於巳，損益惟其所宜，此權之不可以巳也。說者比於渴之掘井而飲，病其備之不豫，誠是也。井既泥而渴方甚，乃不一掘以濟其急焉，惡在其為制兵之權耶？

計食者慨屯政之廢，則曰：「屯田之弊當清也。」憤寺租之侵沒於豪右，則曰：「鬻田之議當遵也。」病商人中納之不廣，則曰：「私鹽之禁不可不嚴也。」考九府圜法之制，則曰：「錢法亦可通行也。」
translation_en:
…Must we not, then, make the arrangements workable through expedient judgment? As matters now stand, responsibilities are divided among the vice regional commanders to enforce strict rules for selection and inspection, while overall responsibility is entrusted to the regional commander to maintain discipline in the ranks and formations. Thus, established procedures already exist for training locally based troops. Yet newly trained soldiers are not yet capable of possessing both courage and a sense of proper conduct. Can they hastily be put to the test without due care? Among troops retained on duty, the weak are weeded out and the strong kept, thereby incorporating measures for economy and reduction; among those coming on duty, registers are corrected and prohibitions made clear, closing off opportunities for fraudulent claims and excessive enrollment. Thus, plans to dispense with troops brought in from elsewhere also embody a considered intention. Yet disciplined troops are what we rely upon to face the enemy and respond to changing circumstances. Can we abruptly cast them aside and send them away? Training local troops strengthens the root; retaining outside troops addresses the branches. What strengthens the root should increase daily, while what addresses the branches should gradually diminish. Whether troops are dismissed or retained should have nothing to do with oneself; reductions and increases should depend solely on what is appropriate. Such expedient judgment cannot be abandoned.

Some commentators compare this to digging a well for water only when thirsty, criticizing the failure to prepare in advance. They are certainly right. But when the well is already silted up and thirst is acute, if one will not even dig to meet the emergency, wherein lies the expedient judgment needed to manage troops?

Those planning provisions deplore the collapse of military agricultural administration and say: “Abuses in the military agricultural colonies must be cleared away.” Indignant that rents from monastery lands are appropriated and embezzled by powerful local families, they say: “The proposal to sell the lands should be followed.” Troubled that too few merchants deliver provisions under the salt-certificate system, they say: “The prohibition of illicit salt must be strictly enforced.” Examining the monetary institutions of the Nine Treasuries, they say: “The coinage system, too, can be put into general operation.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
凡計出此者孰非軍餉之資乎然而屯鹽
錢粟之利其入也有限師徒供億之煩其
出也無窮欲其免於告匱亦難矣必也反
之於道乎自今言之郡縣之積逋動以數
萬計稽籍而追之誠足以濟一時之用矣
要之法可加於富人其在窮民則曷勝其
求也有司催科之政其能任法而直行乎
水陸之餽餉月計三萬餘量入而出之誠
不免有匱乏之憂矣要之養兵所以衛民
===
不食於民將安用夫兵也浙中稅畝之規
其可泥常而不講乎故用賢養民所以開
食之源也因時立法所以導食之流也流
之所導者日以充源之所開者日以裕心
政善運而有常仁義並行而不悖此道之
所以無敝也說者比於罟之竭澤而漁病
其政之太苛誠是也罟非數而魚滿尺乃
不一取以資其用焉惡在其為制食之道
耶夫用權以制兵固以濟變也而主客相
punctuated: 凡計出此者，孰非軍餉之資乎？然而屯鹽錢粟之利，其入也有限；師徒供億之煩，其出也無窮。欲其免於告匱，亦難矣。必也反之於道乎！自今言之，郡縣之積逋，動以數萬計，稽籍而追之，誠足以濟一時之用矣。要之，法可加於富人，其在窮民，則曷勝其求也？有司催科之政，其能任法而直行乎？水陸之餽餉，月計三萬餘，量入而出之，誠不免有匱乏之憂矣。要之，養兵所以衛民，不食於民，將安用夫兵也？浙中稅畝之規，其可泥常而不講乎？故用賢養民，所以開食之源也；因時立法，所以導食之流也。流之所導者日以充，源之所開者日以裕。心政善運而有常，仁義並行而不悖，此道之所以無敝也。說者比於罟之竭澤而漁，病其政之太苛，誠是也。罟非數而魚滿尺，乃不一取以資其用焉，惡在其為制食之道耶？夫用權以制兵，固以濟變也，而主客相
translation_en:
Of all the plans arising from these proposals, which would not provide resources for military supplies? Yet the revenues from military agricultural colonies, salt, coinage, and grain are limited, while the burdensome expenditure of supplying the troops is boundless. It would be difficult to avoid shortages. Surely we must return to the proper Way!

As matters now stand, accumulated tax arrears in prefectures and counties commonly amount to tens of thousands. Checking the registers and recovering these arrears would certainly suffice to meet immediate needs. Ultimately, however, the law can be applied to the rich, but how could the poor bear such demands? In pressing for tax payments, can the responsible officials simply enforce the law without qualification? Supplies for the land and naval forces amount to more than thirty thousand each month. Even if expenditure is measured against revenue, there will certainly still be cause to fear shortages. Ultimately, troops are maintained to protect the people. If they are not to be fed at the people's expense, how are those troops to be employed? As for Zhejiang's regulations for taxing land by the mu, can we cling to established practice and refuse to consider them?

Thus, employing worthy men and nurturing the people opens the source of provisions; establishing laws suited to the times channels their flow. What is channeled grows more abundant each day, and the source that is opened grows daily more ample. When the mind and governance function well and with constancy [?], and benevolence and righteousness proceed together without conflict, this Way remains free of harmful consequences.

Those who compare this to draining a marsh to catch fish with nets, criticizing the excessive harshness of such government, are certainly right. But if the nets are not fine-meshed and the fish are a full foot long, yet one still refuses to make even a single catch to meet one's needs, wherein lies the proper way of managing provisions?

Now, using discretionary measures to manage troops is indeed intended to meet changing circumstances; yet the local and visiting troops mutually …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
觀振作之機寓焉由是以鼓敵愾之氣以
興親長之義以齊步伐之法以明進止之
機比及三年而閩兵皆浙兵矣又何山海
强敵之足患哉得道以制食固以正經也
而官民一體足國之道存焉由是以敷愛
養之實以制樽節之宜以勤先勞之政以
謹出納之司比及三年而有財斯有用矣
又何筦庫告絀之爲慮哉況乎兵食相須
非二策也閩食之不足以客兵耗之耳果
===
使主兵之練有成則養兵之費有數食不
求足而自足矣此萬世之利而濟時之遠
策也抑愚又有說焉島夷之入寇也月港
海滄之民嘯聚而附焉而諸峒不逞之徒
又角起而爲之翼是與閩爲敵者半閩人
也如之何閩兵之不弱以靡也頃者臺臣
有城邑建官之議不惟剪賊之羽翼而且
厚吾之藩籬是誠制治保邦之要也由是
以通沿海魚鹽之利以通諸番貿易之利
punctuated:
觀，振作之機寓焉。由是以鼓敵愾之氣，以興親長之義，以齊步伐之法，以明進止之機，比及三年，而閩兵皆浙兵矣。又何山海强敵之足患哉？得道以制食，固以正經也，而官民一體，足國之道存焉。由是以敷愛養之實，以制樽節之宜，以勤先勞之政，以謹出納之司，比及三年，而有財斯有用矣。又何筦庫告絀之爲慮哉？況乎兵食相須，非二策也。閩食之不足，以客兵耗之耳。果使主兵之練有成，則養兵之費有數，食不求足而自足矣。此萬世之利，而濟時之遠策也。
抑愚又有說焉。島夷之入寇也，月港、海滄之民嘯聚而附焉，而諸峒不逞之徒又角起而爲之翼，是與閩爲敵者半閩人也。如之何閩兵之不弱以靡也？頃者臺臣有城邑建官之議，不惟剪賊之羽翼，而且厚吾之藩籬，是誠制治保邦之要也。由是以通沿海魚鹽之利，以通諸番貿易之利
translation_en:
…observe one another, and therein lies an opportunity to invigorate them. Through this, stir their spirit of enmity toward the foe, foster their sense of duty to love their kin and respect their elders, establish uniform rules for marching, and make clear when to advance and halt. Within three years, the troops of Fujian would all be like the troops of Zhejiang. What formidable enemies in the mountains or at sea would then be cause for concern? To manage provisions in accordance with the Way is indeed to put regular principles into proper order; when officials and people form one body, the means of enriching the state are present. Through this, give practical effect to loving care for the people, establish appropriate measures of economy, diligently pursue governance that leads the people and labors for them, and exercise care over the offices responsible for receipts and disbursements. Within three years, resources would be available to meet expenditure. Why then worry that the treasuries and storehouses might report shortages? Moreover, troops and provisions depend on one another: these are not two separate policies. Fujian’s provisions are insufficient only because troops brought in from elsewhere consume them. If the training of local troops truly succeeds, the expense of maintaining them will have definite limits, and provisions will become sufficient without any deliberate effort to make them so. This would bring benefits for all ages and constitute a far-reaching policy for meeting the needs of the present.
Yet I, in my humble judgment, have something further to say. When the island barbarians invade, people from Yuegang and Haicang gather in bands and join them, while lawless men from the various mountain settlements also rise in rivalry to serve as their wings. Thus, half of those who make themselves Fujian’s enemies are themselves people of Fujian. How could Fujian’s troops fail to be weakened and worn down? Recently, a censor proposed walling towns and establishing officials there. This would not only clip the bandits’ wings but also strengthen our defenses. It is indeed essential to establishing order and safeguarding the realm. Through this, open up the profits from coastal fishing and salt, and open up the profits from trade with foreign peoples…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
逐末少者譏而不征逐末多者征而有數
則不惟島嶼之患可息而且軍需之利日
興是又裕民足國之機也要之亦達乎權
而不離乎道焉耳此外則衛霍桑孔之爲
而孔子之所棄也愚生惡敢以欺執事
punctuated: 逐末少者，譏而不征；逐末多者，征而有數。則不惟島嶼之患可息，而且軍需之利日興，是又裕民足國之機也。要之，亦達乎權而不離乎道焉耳。此外，則衛霍桑孔之爲，而孔子之所棄也。愚生惡敢以欺執事？
translation_en: …Those pursuing commerce on a small scale should be inspected but not taxed; those pursuing it on a large scale should be taxed at prescribed rates. Then not only could the troubles arising from the islands be quelled, but revenues for military supplies would increase daily. This, too, is an opportunity to enrich the people and provide sufficiently for the state. In essence, this is simply to understand expedient measures without departing from the Way. Beyond this lie the practices of Wei and Huo, Sang and Kong—practices that Confucius rejected. How would I, an ignorant student, dare deceive you, honored examiners?

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄後序
嘉靖甲子秋八月癸酉福建
鄉試錄成宮以職事當序諸
末簡宮惟
國家取士以文乃古言揚之制
他日出而仕也亦即以言敷
奏於上蓋唐虞成周皆用之
===
則上所取與士所待取非言
莫以也蓋亦自唐虞成周皆
然矣今年春禮部列議
上請檄所司取士文必純正簡實
有益於世用乃入彀今所奉
行秩如也此非慮士爲文不
及言揚敷奏之盛而思以挽
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄後序

嘉靖甲子秋八月癸酉，福建鄉試錄成，宮以職事當序諸末簡。宮惟國家取士以文，乃古言揚之制。他日出而仕也，亦即以言敷奏於上，蓋唐虞成周皆用之。則上所取與士所待取，非言莫以也，蓋亦自唐虞成周皆然矣。

今年春，禮部列議上請，檄所司，取士文必純正簡實，有益於世用，乃入彀。今所奉行，秩如也。此非慮士爲文不及言揚敷奏之盛，而思以挽
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

On the guiyou day of the eighth month, in autumn of the jiazi year of Jiajing [1564], the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination was completed. By virtue of my official duties, I, Gong, am responsible for writing a postface on its concluding leaves. I consider that the state’s selection of men through literary composition follows the ancient institution of advancing men on the basis of their words. Later, when they enter official service, it is likewise through words that they present their reports to the sovereign. This practice was employed under the rulers of Tang and Yu and during the flourishing Zhou. Thus, words are indispensable both to the sovereign’s selection of men and to the scholars who await selection. This has indeed been so ever since Tang, Yu, and the flourishing Zhou.

In the spring of this year, the Ministry of Rites set forth its deliberations and petitioned the throne to issue instructions to the responsible authorities: compositions used in selecting men must be pure and correct, concise and substantial, and useful in practical affairs before their authors may qualify for selection. These instructions have now been implemented in an orderly manner. Is this not out of concern that scholars’ compositions fall short of the excellence once achieved in advancement through words and in reports to the throne, and from a desire to lead them back …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
之於古也歟御史陳萬言奉
上德意惟虔惟慎飭戒簾内外百
執事各奉
上德意亦惟虔惟慎今觀所取文
果純正而簡實無鉤棘侈靡
諸浮薄不經狀發策設論果
人人可需經濟實用矣又豈
===
非諸士乘遘時會各吐所自
得思以無負於唐虞成周千
古一盛時也歟雖然士有所
言有所以言一時感奮信難
欲愈久愈感奮尤難古昔明
良相遇言可底績矣則猶慮
有靜言庸違者以厠乎其間
punctuated:
之於古也歟？御史陳萬言奉上德意，惟虔惟慎，飭戒簾内外百執事，各奉上德意，亦惟虔惟慎。今觀所取文，果純正而簡實，無鉤棘侈靡諸浮薄不經狀；發策設論，果人人可需經濟實用矣。又豈非諸士乘遘時會，各吐所自得，思以無負於唐虞成周千古一盛時也歟？
雖然，士有所言，有所以言。一時感奮信難，欲愈久愈感奮尤難。古昔明良相遇，言可底績矣，則猶慮有靜言庸違者以厠乎其間。
translation_en:
…to restore it to the ways of antiquity? Censor Chen Wanyan reverently and cautiously carried out the emperor’s benevolent intentions, admonishing all officials serving inside and outside the examination curtain. Each likewise carried out the emperor’s intentions with reverence and caution. Looking now at the selected compositions, we find them indeed sound and correct, concise and substantial, free of convoluted obscurity, extravagant ornament, and all the manifestations of frivolity and departure from the classics. In their responses to policy questions and assigned discourses, every candidate has indeed shown himself someone upon whom one may draw for practical service in governing the realm. Is this not also because these scholars, encountering this timely opportunity, have each expressed what they themselves have grasped, hoping not to fall short of an age of flourishing such as comes but once in a thousand years, comparable to the ages of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the perfected Zhou?
Even so, scholars have both what they say and that which underlies their saying it. To be stirred to exertion for a time is certainly difficult; to grow ever more inspired and diligent as time passes is harder still. In antiquity, when enlightened rulers and worthy ministers met, their words could yield accomplishments; yet there remained concern that among them might mingle those whose words in repose were fine, but whose conduct ran contrary to them.

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
周制鄉三物之敎以六藝與
德行竝乃學非言僞之辨其
致戒每惓惓焉然則士固以
言見取又不徒取其能言而
已也洪惟我
皇上應堯舜之運以明揚天下士
凡十有五舉於玆道久之化
===
棫樸濟濟又寔爲
壽考作人之徵我大小士蓋人得
黎獻
帝臣之願海隅出日亦罔不丕冒
久矣矧八閩方多事時蒙
上注意出多士父兄子弟於水火
海甸旣清
punctuated: 周制鄉三物之敎，以六藝與德行竝，乃學非言僞之辨，其致戒每惓惓焉。然則士固以言見取，又不徒取其能言而已也。洪惟我皇上應堯舜之運，以明揚天下士，凡十有五舉於玆。道久之化，棫樸濟濟，又寔爲壽考作人之徵。我大小士，蓋人得黎獻帝臣之願，海隅出日，亦罔不丕冒久矣。矧八閩方多事時，蒙上注意，出多士父兄子弟於水火。海甸旣清，
translation_en:
Under the Zhou institutions, local instruction comprised three categories, placing the Six Arts alongside virtue and conduct. Against misguided learning and specious argument [?], warnings were repeatedly and earnestly issued. Thus, although scholars are indeed selected on the basis of their words, they are not selected merely for their ability to speak.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor, answering to the destiny of Yao and Shun, has sought out and raised to prominence scholars throughout the realm; there have now been fifteen such selections. The transforming influence of his enduring Way, bringing forth a multitude of worthies as celebrated in “The Oaks” (Yupu), is indeed further evidence of his “nurturing men through a long life.” Among our scholars, greater and lesser alike, each has thus attained the wish to join the multitude of worthies serving as the Emperor’s ministers. Even the coastal reaches where the sun rises have long been abundantly covered by his beneficence. Moreover, when the Eight Min—the regions of Fujian—were beset by troubles, His Majesty bestowed his attention upon them, rescuing the fathers, elder brothers, sons, and younger brothers of our many scholars from fire and flood. Now that the coastal region has been pacified, …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
皇風宣鬯玆又寵借爾以風雲之
奇遇諸士蒙
上之賜可不謂至沃乎夫士以韋
布之賤遭逢
聖明蒙
上沃賜誠所謂千古一時不可不
思所以圖報而朱熹氏諸大
===
儒皆閩產皆能羽翼六經發
揮孔孟精蘊所謂聖門之言
言之至者也爾多士能由諸
大儒之傳推本鄒魯務正學
以言今出而言揚敷奏於時
務正言以圖報稱不惟不文
是憂惟徒文是懼言與行務
punctuated: 皇風宣鬯，玆又寵借爾以風雲之奇遇。諸士蒙上之賜，可不謂至沃乎？夫士以韋布之賤，遭逢聖明，蒙上沃賜，誠所謂千古一時，不可不思所以圖報。而朱熹氏諸大儒，皆閩產，皆能羽翼六經，發揮孔孟精蘊，所謂聖門之言，言之至者也。爾多士能由諸大儒之傳，推本鄒魯，務正學以言。今出而言揚，敷奏於時，務正言以圖報稱。不惟不文是憂，惟徒文是懼。言與行務
translation_en:
…the imperial influence spreads freely. Now you are further favored with an extraordinary opportunity, like the auspicious meeting of wind and cloud. Can the bounty that you scholars receive from His Majesty be called anything but supremely abundant? For scholars of humble station, clad in plain cloth, to encounter a sagely and enlightened ruler and receive His Majesty’s generous gifts is truly what is called an opportunity that comes but once in a thousand ages. You must consider how to repay it.

Zhu Xi and the other great Confucian scholars were all natives of Fujian. All were able to uphold and elucidate the Six Classics and unfold the profound teachings of Confucius and Mencius. These are what we call the words of the sages’ school—the highest attainment of expression. You scholars can follow the transmission of these great Confucians back to its source in Zou and Lu, the homes of Mencius and Confucius, and devote yourselves to orthodox learning as the foundation of your words. Now, as you come forward and gain advancement through your words, presenting your views to the age, strive for correct speech so that you may offer a fitting repayment. Your concern should not merely be a lack of literary accomplishment; what you should fear is merely literary accomplishment. Your words and deeds must …

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
期相副罔或有欺乃終始務
期言行相副亦罔或有惰居
則學孔孟爲儒因言以明道
術出則期與皐夔畢召爲儔
匹因言以立事功則庶幾爾
多士上不負
聖天子下亦不負我所司我所司
===
亦因爾多士以報
聖天子萬分之一否則昰爲庸違
之言而已爾昰爲學非言僞
之辯博而已爾不惟爾多士
將以徒文進不終齒錄於
聖世我所司以進徒文士不能稱
上意旨當亦與有責焉宫爲此懼
punctuated: 期相副，罔或有欺，乃終始務期言行相副，亦罔或有惰。居則學孔孟爲儒，因言以明道術；出則期與皐夔畢召爲儔匹，因言以立事功。則庶幾爾多士上不負聖天子，下亦不負我所司。我所司亦因爾多士以報聖天子萬分之一。否則昰爲庸違之言而已爾，昰爲學非言僞之辯博而已爾。不惟爾多士將以徒文進，不終齒錄於聖世，我所司以進徒文士，不能稱上意旨，當亦與有責焉。宫爲此懼，
translation_en:
…strive to make them accord, without any deception; from beginning to end, strive to make words and conduct correspond, without any indolence. When living in retirement, study Confucius and Mencius and become Confucian scholars, using words to elucidate the Way and its teachings. When entering office, aspire to stand alongside Gao Yao, Kui, the Duke of Bi, and the Duke of Shao, using words to accomplish deeds of merit. Then perhaps you assembled scholars will neither disappoint the sage Son of Heaven above nor fail us, the officials responsible for you, below. Through you, we too may repay one ten-thousandth of our debt to the sage Son of Heaven.
Otherwise, these will merely be words of outward assent concealing disobedience, merely eloquence and broad learning devoted to erroneous doctrines and false statements. Not only will you scholars advance through mere literary accomplishment and fail to retain your standing among those recognized in this sagely age; we officials, by advancing men of mere literary accomplishment and failing to fulfill His Majesty’s intentions, will also share the blame. I, Gong, am apprehensive on this account…

title: 嘉靖四十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
敢以告爾多士爾多士其勉
之於乎其尚相與勉之
山東東昌府高唐州恩縣儒
學教諭甘宮謹序
punctuated:
敢以告爾多士，爾多士其勉之！於乎，其尚相與勉之！
山東東昌府高唐州恩縣儒學教諭甘宮謹序。
translation_en:
…I venture to convey this to you, assembled scholars. Apply yourselves diligently! Ah, may you encourage one another in this endeavor!
Preface respectfully composed by Gan Gong, Instructor of the Confucian School of En County, Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong.
